The feedback is generally asked for by the manager to whom the employee reports into. Colleagues who participate in the 36 0 usually include the persons line manager, several peers,
reporting staff, and functional managers with whom the employee works regularly with.
The goal of the feedback is to provide a balanced view to an employee of how others view his or
her contributi on and performance in areas such as leadership, teamwork, interpersonal,
communication, management, contribution, work habits, interpersonal interaction, accountability,
vision and more, depending on the employee's job.
Key characteristics of the 360 review include:
• Availability to assign and request feedback for a specific period.
• Visibility of feedback can be set for HR, the manager and the employee ; therefore
controlling who has access to review submitted feedback.
• The anonymity of feedback can be set for HR, the manager and the employee hiding the
name of the employee who provides feedback.
• Review questionnaires can be created unique to each review, with the facility to define a
number of mandatory or optional questions using multiple choice & free text style
answers.

1.3. What are Peer Reviews
The Peer Review functionality allows a manager to send a review questionnaire to other employees
in the organisation and to request feedback from their team members . Talent management
administrators can create peer review questionnaires and assign these either to all man agers
across the entire organisation or to managers that belong to a specific organisational group , e.g.
all managers in Division A.
Key characteristics of the peer review include:
• The availability to assign and request feedback for a specific period.
• The visibility of feedback can be restricted for either HR, the manager or both.
• The anonymity of feedback provided can be set to hide the name of the employee who

3. Shift Swap
3.1. Overview
It is possible for employees to submit a request to swap a shift with another team member. Employees
can also accept or reject a request for a Shift Swap with another employee. In order for the Shift Swap
to be successful, managers must first ap prove a request for a Shift Swap. The Shift Swap approval
workflow is as follows:
1. Employee 1 submits a Shift Swap with employee 2.
2. Employee 2 is notified of the swap, and then accepts or reject the Shift Swap.
3. If employee 2 accepts the Shift Swap, then the swap notifies the manager of employee 2.
4. If the manager approves the Shift Swap, the Roster is then update for employee 1 and employee
2, to reflect the Shift Swap.
5. When the status of the swap changes to approved or rejected, both employees are updated of
the approval/rejection.

1. Overview 1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This guide aims to explain the Pay Code screens which have been converted from Back Office to
Portal.
It covers the following:
• The Pay Code Screen
• Pay Code Screen Configuration
• Configuring Pay Codes
• Pay Code Groups
• Data Migration
1.2. What is the Pay Code Screen?
The Pay Codes Screen maintains codes, which are automatically generated by the system and
maintained on an ad-hoc basis by authorized personnel. Portal supports an unlimited amount of
Pay Codes, such as Basic, Overtime or Lates. Pay Codes required for Time & Attendance purposes
are determined by operational policies. If you are linked to the Pay system, the code and
descriptions will already have been set up.

The Pay Code Screen can be accessed by the following steps:
1. Quick jump to the WFM Admin Dashboard.
2. Select WFM Configuration.

What is Roster?
The Workforce Management Roster function ensures your organisation has employees rostered to their
shifts in the correct place, at the correct time. This enables your organisation to successfully meet your
business needs, therefore, matching business demand with resource supply. Features within the Roster
function include:
• AutoRostering
• Roster creation and publishing
• Alerts for under/over staffing, budget variations, breaches of WTD
• Rostered versus contracted hours tracking
• Configurable validation rules
• Absence entitlement tracking and validation

Standard Calculation
Overview
The Standard Calculation is used when there is a Work Pattern matching every combination of times
that employees can work and have the associated calculation rules specified at the Work Pattern level.
With this calculation type, employees can clock in or have their default hours generated.
For example, this calculation type can be used for when employees work on cycle shifts within a
manufacturing organisation. Employees can clock in for their shifts and the o vernight calculation runs
to calculate against their Work Pattern.
Note: It is advised to discuss your existing Time and Attendance solution configuration and your
organisational requirements, with your CoreHR project team, to ensure the Roster solution
configured is optimised to the highest potential of meeting your organisational requirements.
Note: The Split Rule cannot be used in conjunction with the Standard Calculation. The Standard
Calculation ensures a one to one mapping with the Roster Rules and the employee shift.

The Standard Calculation – Multi Pattern calculation option is only available where employees are not
clocking for their shifts . This calculation type ensures that the Primary Pattern and Additional Pattern
default hours are summed together and are the generated against the Primary Pattern Pay Code.
• Rostered hours are calculated for multi -patterns by summing the default hours specified on
each Primary and Additional Work Pattern. Additional non-contract days are not calculated.
• Premium hours calculated, are taken from the Primary Pattern regardless of what is specified
on the Additional Work Pattern.
The l inking of Team Areas with Cost Centres with the Multi Pattern calculation is based on each
employee being assigned one Team Area per day. If an employee is rostered to work across multiple
Team Areas, on the same day , the system calculates all hours against the Cost Centre/Team Area
associated with the Primary Pattern for that day.

paid a higher rate for overtime, as the Time Exceptions (late) are not offset against overtime

7. AutoRoster AutoRoster Overview
AutoRoster is a process that can be run to automatically generate a Team Area’s Roster. The
AutoRoster process considers a set of rules, dictating the logic that gets applied, for filling the staffing
requirements of a Team Area. This means that the AutoRoster process looks at the business logic and
organisational rules you require the system to apply , when choosing the most appropriate employee s
to fill each Roster gap.
The AutoRoster process looks at the Validation Rules, that have been assigned to the Team Area, and
the employee Roster Contract Details , that have been configured within the system. Based on these
criteria, the process then rosters employees accordingly subject to their availability and suitability.
It is possible for the AutoRostering process to be configured so that certain days are priority . For
example, busier days such as Saturdays or Sundays can be rostered to fill staffing requirements first.
There are multiple ways to configure AutoRoster, subject to your organisational requirements. For
further information on the AutoRoster configuration options, view the General Roster Configuration
training material on CoreHR University.

1.3. What is the Parallel Mode?
Generate Timesheets in Parallel Mode. As mentioned in the previous section, Generate Timesheets has been moved from the back office
to Portal. In order to support the transition, the portal version of Generate Timesheets runs a
parallel mode to support the re-generation of a previously transferred period that was completed
via the back office.
The features within the Parallel Mode are the following:
• WFM company: Parallel Mode can be enabled per WFM company. If a client has more
than one company using Portal, the parallel mode can be run separately for each.
• Validation: Parallel mod e is run to validate those calendars or periods which have
previously been migrated to show that there are no discrepancies found.
• Leavers: Parallel Transfers do not impact the live mode. Employees are not marked as
leavers.
• Analysis and Review: Parallel Run details are stored into backup tables for analysis and
review. For further information see Tables for Parallel Run.

WFM V28: Generate Timesheets - User Guide
1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide.
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to generate timesheets. This functionality
for generating timesheets was previously completed through the Back Office and is now available on
CorePortal. This is a brand new CoreHR feature for V28. There are no changes to the existing Payroll
Rules and how they are configured.
This guide will instruct you how to how to:
• Retrieve Hours for Payroll.
• View Generated Payroll Hours detail.
• Transfer hours to Payroll.
1.2. General Overview.
The Generate Ti mesheets is now available in Portal – from either the Workforce Management
Dashboard or the Admin Dashboard. This allows more streamlined payroll integration. This gives you:
• Improved functionality access alongside Payportal.
• View details of converted hours before transferring them to Payroll.
• The possibility of continuing tasks while the applications run in the background.

ew details of converted hours before transferring them to Payroll.
• The possibility of continuing tasks while the applications run in the background. • An estimation given of the length of the process.
• Notifications given on completion of the processes.

2. Functionality Overview
2.1. Process
The Generate Timesheets process takes place in two steps:
• Ready to Retrieve: Step 1: This converts T&A timesheets into Payroll Hours based on payroll
rules configured in WFM.
• Ready to Transfer : Step 2 : This transfers Payroll Hours to CoreHR Payroll or c reates a n
interface file where applicable.

By using the Retrieve Hours function you are converting timesheets in to Payroll hours. This allows you
to select specific calendars within a company and send them to Payroll.

1.2.4. Leave Requests versus Absences
The following points should be taken into consideration regarding Leave Requests and Absences:
• A Leave Request is submitted by an employee, for manager approval. Before it may proceed
as an official absence, a Leave Request must be actioned by a manager, to either approve or
reject the request.
• An Absence can be directly entered on an employee record, by a manager.
When a Leave Request date has passed, it is seen as an historical timesheet within the system. This
Leave Request then shows as an Absence.

1.1. Purpose of Document
The purpose of this guide is to provide an overview of user guidance and the configuration associated

1.2. Overview of Feature
Overlapping Warnings display during the actioning of employee Leave Requests, alerting the approver
at the approval/rejection stage. This feature alerts approvers if a Leave Request overlaps with:
• An absence or approved Leave Request for another employee in the approver’s remit.
• An un-actioned request for another employee in the approver’s remit.
• A previously rejected request for the same employee.
For further information on general Leave Requests , view Leave Requests & Absence user guide on
CoreHR University.
Note:
• This feature provides a warning to the approver only , to be taken into consideration.
However, does not prevent the approver from approving/rejecting the Leave Request.
• Warnings for ‘Sick’ absence are only displayed when it is submitted for manager approval,
not when it is directly entered on the employee record. This means that the warnings are
only triggered if the absence request goes through an approval process. Therefore,
warnings are not triggered if absence is directly entered for the employee without approvals.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Pay Code Access Groups
functionality.
It is intended for use by HR Administrators that manage the listings of Pay codes available to
managers and employees when entering leave requests, absences and timesheets.
This guide includes:
• Pay Code Access Groups explained.
• How to access and create Pay Code Groups.
• How to assign Pay Codes Groups to Managers and Employees.
• How to configure Managers and Employees to have access to the correct codes.
1.2. What’s new for version 28!
• In portal, Managers absence and timesheet entries can be linked to pay code groups
assigned at employee level. The Manager input is reflective of pay code groups assigned
to the employee and/or the employee appointment combination.
• Managers can be granted access to additional pay codes within the group that are
marked as manager only.

The Pro Rata Length of Service Increments functionality makes it possible to pro rata anniversary-based
length of service increments. The service increment calculation, to determine the number of additional days awarded, can be based
on:
• Dates (days)
• Weeks
• Months
Therefore, the increment calculation takes the date s, weeks, or months , between the employee’ s
anniversary date and the end of the annual leave year into consideration.
For example, where the increment calculation is configured as ‘days’ based, this instructs the system to
calculate the service increment from the start of the year , to the date im mediately before the service
date. To do this, the system:
• Adds the full -service increment entitlement, then deducts the part of the year (days) to be
excluded from the additional days awarded.
• Applies the employee’s FTE to the remainder.
• Adds to the employee’s opening entitlement.
• Rounds the result, based on the Rounding Rule specified at the balance level.

If an employee is leaving an organisation, this also impacts their service increment.

2.1.13. TUPE date – Length of Service and Continuance Dates
Changes have been made to Balance and Occupational Entitlements to introduce TUPE dates. This
takes in to account an employee’s length of service when the existing company is part of an
acquisition and the employee is given a new start date.
What has changed?
• The system now has the option to factor in TUPE dates for service calculations when
determining entitlements to Occupational and Leave Balances, so the employee’s full
service is included.
• There are new drop-down values to the existing options on forms.
o For balance entitlements, see Balance Parameters/Employee Start Date now has a
Continuance/Tupe Date option.
o For Occupational Absence, see Absence Pay Parameters/ Length of Service Basis now
has Continuance/Tupe Date
Example:
An employee joined Company A on 01-Jan-1999
Their Occupational Sick Entitlement is 20 days. After 10 years’ service, the employee gets an
extra 5 days sick leave
Company A is acquired by Company B on 01-Jan-2020
The employee is given a start date with Company B of 01 -Jan-2020 & TUPE Date = 01 -Jan-1999

4.3. HESA Mapping Engine and HESA Tracker Log
When the HESA records are being generated, the HESA Mapping engine is responsible for mapping
the PeopleXD employee and contract data, to the corresponding CoreHESA person and contract
records. For each record, each field is processed in the mapping engine in the following order:
1. Is the employee exempt?
2. Is there a default value set?
3. Apply SQL Mapping Rules
4. Apply CoreHR Mapping References
5. Business rule validation engine (optional)
The HESA tracker log is a record of CoreHESA records that have been created or updated. Once the
initial data set (Full Generation) has been created for the current reporting year, any changes to
employee / contract records in PeopleXD will be processed by the HESA tracker log and mapping
engine. This will apply any rules, mappings and default values as appropriate. This information is
passed to the tracker log by a scheduled job that runs every 10 minutes. This includes:
• Any new employees created on PeopleXD.

1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the candidate anonymisation and CV
parsing functionality in PeopleXD Recruitment. This includes:

1.2. What is Candidate Anonymisation?
Candidate anonymisation allows you to hide personal information about a candidate for specific
stages of the recruitment process. For example, the candidate’s name, address information, and
contact details can be hidden.
1.3. What is CV Parsing?
When enabled, CVs are parsed when they are submitted by a candidate, or when a user manually
adds a CV to an existing candidate record.
The following information is then available in PeopleXD:

2. Configuration
2.1. Configuring Candidate Anonymisation
Candidate anonymisation can be enabled for a specific applicant status. To configure this, follow
the below steps:
1. Navigate to the Recruitment Dashboard.
2. Click the Toolbox tab.
3. From the My Recruit Toolbox widget, click Open on Applicant Status.
4. Click the three dot menu on the relevant status, then click Status Details.
5. Enable or disable the Anonymise Candidate Data toggle as required.
6. Click OK.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Data Migration Update Facility
widget. This includes:
• An overview of the Data Migration Update Facility widget.
• What records can be updated using the Data Migration Update Facility widget.
• How to update data using the Data Migration Update Facility widget.
• The dependency on Insight reports for employee and contract updates.
• Cancelling an update that is in progress.
• Fixing errors identified during the update.
• An appendix with detailed guidance for each of the 26 update options.

g an update that is in progress.
• Fixing errors identified during the update.
• An appendix with detailed guidance for each of the 26 update options. 1.2. What is the Data Migration Update Facility?
The Data Migration Update Facility can be used to make bulk updates to:
• 10 specific personal details on employee records (full list here in 1.3 Employee Updates).
• 12 specific contract elements (full list here in 1.4 Contract Updates)
• 4 reference data items (full list here in 1.5 Reference Data Updates)
Note:
This document does not cover the Data Migration Templates and Data Migration Options widgets,
as these are not part of the process for completing bulk updates. Refer to the Data Migration Tool
user guide for further guidance.

Description option.
This can be an efficient way to update records in bulk on CoreHR, rather than updating each individual

2. How to Complete an Update
2.1. Updating Person / Contract Records
To update existing employee / contract records, the system needs to know w hat records are to be
updated. This is facilitated using an Insight report. The report runs within the update facility and return
the required employee / contract records on screen.

This is facilitated using an Insight report. The report runs within the update facility and return
the required employee / contract records on screen. Follow the steps below to retrieve a list of employees / contracts in the update facility:
1. Create a report in Insight that identifies the set of records to be updated.
a. Reports must include the employee number.
b. Contract ID is not required for the contract updates (but is useful to add to ensure the
correct set of data is retrieved in Insight).
c. All other columns included in the report do not display in the update facility but are
useful to add to the report to ensure the correct set of data is being retrieved, e.g. name,
department etc.
Note:
It is only possible to update records that you currently have access to on the system. When the
Insight report is generated, records appear based on your ‘System Users’ access e.g. if you don’t
have access to the employee / contract in People Management / Payroll etc, you won’t have access
to it here.
Note:
If the report should only display specific employee or contract records, then any filters required
should be applied in Insight when creating the report either by:
• Adding filters to pre-filter the report, before it is run in the data migration tool.
• Adding prompts to the report to be filter when it is run in the data migration tool.

4.5. Report Timeout
CoreHR automatically kills off CoreInsight reports that run longer than one hour. The user that runs the
report will receive an email that their report has been stopped as it has exceeded the maximum duration.
In most cases, we have found that these poor-performing reports are joining to multiple areas and views
(scanning volumes of data) where there is no need and can be adjusted to return the same results much
faster. If you experience this report time out for a report that you have created, we recommended that
you review the report structure and contact CoreHR for further guidance if needed to make this run more
efficiently.

The GDPR Request Centre can be made available to users to complete the following employee requests:
Subject Access Requests – Any employee has the right to request a copy of the personal data the organisation has stored about them in a “structured commonly used and machine-readable format”. The GDPR Request Centre provides this data in both a CSV file and a machine-readable JSON file.

structured commonly used and machine-readable format”. The GDPR Request Centre provides this data in both a CSV file and a machine-readable JSON file. JSON – JavaScript Object Notation is an open-standard file format that uses human-readable text to transmit data objects consisting of attribute-value pairs and array data types. JSON is a language-independent data format.
Right to be Forgotten Requests – Any employee has the right to be forgotten as per GDPR guidelines. It is the responsibility of the organisation to carry out any due diligence and internal processes in relation to this request.

Organisational Role
A user needs to be assigned an Organisational Role in order to be able to see employee records on the GDPR Request Centre and within the Insight Reports.
There is a standard Org Role provided by The Access Group ‘GDPR Organisational Role’ and this needs to be assigned at Company access level.
Firstly, the Org Role needs to be activated. Navigate via People Management > Data Centre > References Data > Open> Organisational Role Types> filter by the GDPR role type and enable the active indicator.
You then need to define the org group that access is aligned to. This will either be at Company or Department level. It is only possible to define one level in PeopleXD by which employees will be grouped e.g. If set to Department, each department needs to be assigned to a user to ensure that all employees can be managed in the GDPR Request Centre. GDPR Control Parameters
GDPR Statutory Years for Deletion
When a deletion request is being processed, there is validation to prevent this occurring if the employee’s leave date is less than a specified number of years. This is defaulted to 7 years; however, this is configurable.
To manage the setting navigate via
Administrator Dashboard > Admin > Admin Settings > search for parameter gdpr_statutory_years.
Click on the Edit button and enter the required number of years. Click Save.

Cleardown Days for GDPR Requests GDPR request history for ‘query’ requests is automatically cleared down on the GDPR Request Centre after a specified number of days. This is defaulted to 30 days; however, this is configurable.
To manage the setting navigate via
Administrator Dashboard > Admin > Admin Settings > search for parameter gdpr_cleardown_days.
Click on the edit button and enter the required number of days. Click Save.

Request Success
The time taken for the request to be processed depends on the range and volume of data recorded for that employee. When the processing begins, the status updated to “PROCESSING!. Once the delete request finishes processing the request is immediately deleted from the GDPR Requests screen.
All traces of the deletion request are removed from PeopleXD and are not retrievable visa the GDPR request Centre. This is completed in accordance with the GDPR regulations. The request may be reported on via Insight, with the employee details redacted.
Deleting GDPR Requests
Subject Access Requests and failed Deletion requests will remain on the GDPR Requests screen for reference, until cleared down manually or automatically. Automatic clear down is carried out after 30 days, but this is configurable.
Successful deletion requests are immediately deleted from the GDPR Requests screen.
To manually delete a request click on the ellipses button and select Delete.

The ‘Core GDPR business area is available in Insight to facilitate reporting on GDPR activities. This is intended for use by those users responsible for managing GDPR within the organisation.
This allows reporting on the Activity View, which provides details of the requests submitted through the GDPR Requests Centre. Completed Data Deletion requests are reportable but with the employee reference removed.

username

Ask fields
The Ask field code prompts you to enter information and assigns your response to a bookmark. For the information to appear in the document, you must insert a Ref field that refers to the bookmark. Word prompts you for a response each time you update the Ask field, such as when you press F9 or step through the records in a mail merge.
You can use the Ask field in a document or as part of a mail merge.
To display the response in the content of the document, you must insert a Ref field after the Ask field.

Adding an ASK field On the Insert tab, in the Text group, click Quick Parts, and then click Field.
In the Field names list, select Ask.
In the Prompt box, type the question that you want answered.
In the Bookmark name box, type a name for the bookmark that will store the response to the prompt.
If you want a predefined response, select the Default response to prompt check box, and type the text.
If you want the same response to apply to all the records in a mail merge, select the Prompt before merging bookmark text check box. Otherwise, Word will prompt you for a response with each record.
Click OK
Example
To use the Ask field as part of a mail merge, do the following while you are setting up the mail merge:
On the Mailings tab, in the Write & Insert Fields group, click Rules, and then click Ask.
In the Bookmark box, type a name for the bookmark that will store the response to the prompt.
In the Prompt box, type the question you want answered.
If you want a predefined response, type the response in the Default bookmark text box.
If you want the same response to apply to all the records in the merge, select the Ask once check box. Otherwise, Word will prompt you for a response with each record.

Syntax When you view the Ask field code in your document, the syntax looks like this:
{ ASK Bookmark"Prompt" [Optional switches ] }
Note:  A field code tells the field what to show. Field results are what is shown in the document after having evaluated the field code. To toggle between viewing the field code and the field code results, press Alt+F9.
Instructions
Bookmark
The bookmark name assigned to the response to the prompt, for example, ClientName.
"Prompt"
Prompt text, which is displayed in a dialog box — for example, "Enter the client's name."
Optional switches
\d "Default "
Specifies a default response if you don't type a response in the prompt dialog box. For example, the field
{ ASK Typist "Enter typist's initials:" \d "tds" } assigns "tds" to the bookmark Typist if you don't enter a response.
If you don't specify a default response, Word uses the last response that was entered. To specify a blank entry as the default, type empty quotation marks after the switch. For example, type \d "" .
\o
When used in a mail merge main document, displays the prompt one time instead of each time you merge a new data record. The same response is inserted in each resulting merged document.

The Fill-In field prompts you to enter text. Your response is printed in place of the field.

When you create a new document that is based on a template (a .dotm or .dotx file) and that contains Fill-In fields, Word prompts you for a response at each Fill-In field.

IF field The If field compares two values and then inserts the text appropriate to the result of the comparison. When used in a mail merge main document, the If field can examine information in the merged data records, such as postal codes or account numbers. For example, you can send letters to only those clients located in a particular city.
You can use the If field in a document, or you can use the If field as part of an If-Then-Else rule in a mail merge.
To use the If field in a document, do the following:
On the Insert tab, in the Text group, click Quick Parts, and then click Field.
In the Field names list, select If.
In the Field codes box, type the expressions, operator, true text, and false text, following the syntax shown above.
Click OK.
To use the If field as part of a mail merge, do the following while you are setting up the mail merge:
1.On the Mailings tab, in the Write & Insert Fields group, click Rules, and then click If...Then...Else.
2.In the Field name list, select the name of a merge field, such as City.
3.In the Comparison list, select the operator that you want. For example, to single out recipients in a particular city, select Equal to.

uch as City.
3.In the Comparison list, select the operator that you want. For example, to single out recipients in a particular city, select Equal to. 4.In the Compare to box, type the value that you want to use. For example, to single out recipients in Tokyo, type Tokyo.
Note: If you selected is blank or is not blank in the Comparison list, leave the Compare to box empty.
5.In the Insert this text box, type the text that you want to appear in the document when the condition that you specified is true. For example, to customize the text for recipients in Tokyo, you can type especially for your Tokyo neighborhood.
6.In the Otherwise insert this text box, type the text that you want to appear in the document when the condition that you specified is not true. For example, to provide generic text for recipients who are not in Tokyo, you can type especially for your surrounding neighborhood.
Syntax
When you view the If field code in your document, the syntax looks like this:
{ IF Expression1OperatorExpression2TrueTextFalseText}
Note: A field code tells the field what to show. Field results are what is shown in the document after having evaluated the field code. To toggle between viewing the field code and the field code results, press Alt+F9.
Instructions
Expression1, Expression2

ing evaluated the field code. To toggle between viewing the field code and the field code results, press Alt+F9.
Instructions
Expression1, Expression2 Values that you want to compare. These expressions can be merge field data, bookmark names, strings of characters, numbers, nested fields that return a value, or mathematical formulas. If an expression contains spaces, enclose the expression in quotation marks.
Notes:
Expression2 must be enclosed in quotation marks so that it is compared as a character string.
If the operator is = or <>, Expression2 can contain a question mark (?) to represent any single character or an asterisk (*) to represent any string of characters.
If you use an asterisk in Expression2, the portion of Expression1 that corresponds to the asterisk and any remaining characters in Expression2 cannot exceed 128 characters.
Operator
Comparison operator. Insert a space before and after the operator.

TrueText, FalseText
Text that results when the comparison is true (TrueText) or false (FalseText). If FalseText isn't specified and the comparison is false, the IF field has no result. Each string containing multiple words must be enclosed in quotation marks.

How to make the answer to a FILLIN prompt repeat elsewhere in the document, without needing to repeat the FILLIN prompt itself.
The FILLIN prompt needs to be wrapped in another set of brackets with the words ‘SET’ and the reference of your choice given after for the prompt/answer, e.g.
{ SET TheName { FILLIN “Please write your name” } }
In order for the answer to then appear in the text, simply insert { TheName } wherever you wish the answer to this prompt to appear.

Expense Codes Background
Expense Codes are used to summarise transactions into groups of expenses/costs and liabilities, so they can be posted GL in the form of Debits and Credits. The following points should be taken into consideration regarding Expense Codes:
An Expense Code is not associated with an employee. Its possible to have a different expense Code for every element of pay an employee receives.
Expense Codes are used in conjunction with the Cost Centres, i.e. one Expense Code may be used in many different Cost Centres.
The Expense Code is normally derived based on the type of employee and the type of pat that the employee receives.
An Expense Code is an 8-digit number field. Data mapping can be used to ensure the Expense Code output by PeopleXD matches the Expense Code in the Financial Management System (FMS).

Approved process for raising
Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
The Reward Team and HR Analytics Team are responsible for producing and confirming the rates for existing grades. Requests for the creation of any new grades should be raised through these teams, or via the HRSEG on which these teams are represented.
To set up a new grade, the following items must be confirmed by the Reward and HR Analytics Teams:
Grade Code (e.g. 02S)
Grade Description (e.g. STANDARD GRADE 2)
The number of Scale Points on the grade (e.g. 9)
The full Scale Narrative of each point on the scale (e.g. POINT 1 NSP6)

ption (e.g. STANDARD GRADE 2)

The full Scale Narrative of each point on the scale (e.g. POINT 1 NSP6) Any Bar Points on the scale (e.g. points 7-9 are discretionary points)
The Yearly Full Time Rates (e.g. Point 1 - £15,765.00)
The Full Time Hours for the grade (e.g. 36.5)
Whether the grade should be available to select on new Staff Requests
Whether the grade will be subject to Cost of Living awards
The Effective Date of the new grade (likely to be the normal pay uplift date for the grade – e.g. 01-Aug-2021)
Consultation & Approval
Who is the owner of this information? Who needs to be consulted about this change before you begin work on it? Does anyone need to approve this change before it is implemented?
Requests for new grades and changes to existing grades should come from and be discussed with the Reward, HR Analytics, and Payroll teams. Grade-related requests will usually be discussed and agreed at HRSEG (Human Resources Systems Evaluation Group). However, if the changes requested must be implemented urgently, they may be agreed by another means e.g. email.
New Grades
Pensions should be consulted, as they will need to confirm which Pension Scheme should be assigned to the new grade.
Payroll should be consulted, as they will need to if they want to publish the grade to the web (see the Affected Reports section below).

The X5 team will need to be informed of the new grade as soon as possible, so that they can check whether any staff who will be on the grade are likely to be involved in research – if so, the new grade will need to be set up in X5 by their system support team. (X5 provides administrators and principal investigators (PIs) with a tool for costing research grant applications.)
Changes to existing grades or rates
Changes to existing grades or rates may result in employee records being updated, e.g. where a scale point is being removed. The HR Analytics team should therefore be consulted as the changes to employee records may need to be undertaken by the Data Service Team. The X5 team have asked for as much notice as possible in terms of rate changes. Ideally when these are being tested in the non-prod environment but certainly ahead of the update into production.

The change process applicable at the time of the change should be followed. The current process is to create a change request in OSM which is approved by the relevant approver. Ideally, the change should be approved prior to being put into QA testing.
The HRIS Functional Analysis Team are responsible for setting up new grades & points and amending existing grades & points.
If a new grade is being created and the Full Time Hours value for the grade is not present in the list of ‘FTE Hours’ in the database, a new value will need to be created. This can either be done via a separate change or added as a separate element to the current change. For information on how to add a new FTE Hours value, refer to the document How To – View and Maintain Reference Data.

Background
New functionality providing the ability to delete an employee’s appointment when processed in error either by way of replacing contract (transfer) or as a new additional contract. In addition, the ability to delete the latest appointment sequence if processed in error.
The delete contract functionality can be used for the following process scenarios:
Replacement Contract has been processed – Delete replacement and reinstate previous post
To be eligible for deletion a new replacement contract/appointment can either be appointed or commenced, but only where the new post has not been paid. Where a post has already been paid, a message is displayed stating that contract can’t be deleted.

ced, but only where the new post has not been paid. Where a post has already been paid, a message is displayed stating that contract can’t be deleted. Where the new replacement contract/appointment has already been ended, it can’t be deleted.
For replacement contracts, all previous post data will be reactivated. Appointment status is reversed and salary and cost allocation set as active.
The new replacement contract will be deleted, including salary, allowances, pensions, UDF’s.
Alternative Outcome
If the contract is the employee’s first and only substantive appointment the button to delete the contract will instead go through the screens for switching the appointment for a different one. This process allows the employee to keep their current appointment ID however, the post number and post sequence changes to the post that have been switched to. The posts available for selection need to be authorised in advance of selection.
Additional Contract has been processed – Delete additional contract
To be elegible for deletion the new additional contract can be either appointed or commenced, but only where the new post has not been paid. If the additional post has been paid, a message is displayed stating that contract can’t be deleted.
If the new additional contract/appointment has already been ended, it can’t be deleted.

a message is displayed stating that contract can’t be deleted.
If the new additional contract/appointment has already been ended, it can’t be deleted. For additional contracts, when the delete contract function is triggered the contract will be deleted, including salary, allowances, pensions, UDF’s.
Contract Amendment has been processed – Delete latest appointment sequence
The latest appointment sequence is deleted and previous sequence reactivated. No impact on salary etc.

Background
The Access Group has released new functionality providing the ability to delete an employee/person record, which can be used where the employee record was added in error.
There are limitations, which prevent a person record from being deleted, these are:
An employee record cannot be deleted if their salary has been paid. In this instance, an error will be displayed stating, “This person record cannot be deleted as they have already been processed by payroll.
An employee record cannot be deleted if WFM transactions exist on their record, such as Timesheet hours. In this instance, an error will be displayed stating, “This person record cannot be deleted as WFM Transactions have already been entered against it”.
Where the employee has hours recorded against a Timesheet, which has not been paid, these can be removed. Please see further guidance under section How to Remove WFM Timesheet Transactions Preventing Person Deletion.

How to Delete a Person
System process steps for deleting a person record.

Once returned back to the employee record the person status has updated from Active to Deleting. The person is not deleted immediately, a status of ‘Deleting’ will display and an overnight job will then delete the employee. There will still be an option to select Undo Delete under the Actions menu should you need to reverse these step, see next section for details.
Once the overnight job has completed to delete the person record the post record is still available, however the post appointment will have been deleted as part of this process. If creating a new post appointment, the same sequence number will be allocated.
The same employee number will not be re issued when setting up a new employee.
How to Undo Scheduled Delete Person
If the system delete has not yet happened, the user will be able to undo the pending delete. System process steps to undo a scheduled person delete.
Go to the Command Centre tab on the People Management dashboard.
Click the View button on the Employee section.
Search for the employee in question that is due to be deleted.
Click on the ACTIONS button, which is located in the top right hand corner of the screen.

After clicking on Yes to proceed with the Undo Delete Person the following confirmation action message is displayed:
Once returned back to the employee record the person status has updated from Deleting to Active once again. The scheduled overnight deletion job has been cancelled.
Reporting Against Scheduled Delete Person
It is still possible to report against the person scheduled to be deleted whilst they have the ‘Deleting’ person status and before the overnight process to delete the person record completes.
Whilst the employee has the ‘deleting’ person status the PERSUP17 HR Audit report will detail the pending delete action from the HR_PERSON table with the field name DELETE_IND.
After the overnight job has run and the person has been fully deleted it is no longer possible to report against their person record using the PERSUP17 HR Audit report.
This will have no impact on payroll reporting as any employee already paid cannot be deleted by this process, as noted in the background section of this document.

purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Employee Onboarding functionality
in People Management and how this is used. This includes: • What is Employee Onboarding and when it used by employees?
• The difference between ‘new starter onboarding’ and ‘existing employee cross-boarding’.
• An overview of the Social Hub dashboard.
• Detailed guidance on the main elements of the Social Hub dashboard and how they may
be used.
• Tracking employee onboarding progress as a manager or hr administrator.
Employee Onboarding is highly configurable to ensure that every organisation can manage the
onboarding and cross-boarding experience based on their own requirements. This document does
not cover configuration guidance. For full training on how to set up and configure each element of
Employee Onboarding, see the Employee Onboarding v28: How to Configure - User Guide.
1.2. What is Employee Onboarding?
Employee Onboarding is a platform that supports onboarding guidance for new joiners and re-
joiners, while also supporting continuous onboarding guidance for existing employees. For
example:
• New starter onboarding for employees joining or re-joining the organisation.
• Cross-boarding for existing employees who move to new contracts, appointments, and/or
teams.
• The requirement to release new Checklist Items to existing employees.

for existing employees who move to new contracts, appointments, and/or
teams.
• The requirement to release new Checklist Items to existing employees. • A platform encouraging existing employees to engage with their wider team.
Employees can commence onboarding before the join the organisation i.e. before their start date
or rehire date. If this is the case, the employee will need a CorePortal account (to be created in the
same way as you generally issue CorePortal accounts). However, they will only have access to the
Social Hub until their start date has elapsed. They will not be able to access any other part of the
CorePortal e.g. Employee Dashboard won’t be available to them until they have started.:

1.2. What are User Defined Fields?
1.2.1. UDFs Explained User Defined Fields (UDFs) are used to hold data where the system doesn’t provide this as
standard. These would typically be items that are specific to an individual organisation and will
differ from company to company.
For example, a company may wish to store a record of standard company equipment that has
been given to an employee. This can be cap tured in a UDF that is configured to display the exact
equipment list specific to that company.
UDFs can be created against:
• An employee
• A post
• A contract

UDFs may be configured using the following elements:
• Up to 12 standard fields:
o Text
o Number
o List
o Date
o Text Area
• Start Date & End Date
There is no limit to the amount of UDFs that can be configured.
1.2.2. Access to UDFs
UDFs are configured via the People Management dashboard. UDFs are available as standard to all
HR administrators via People Management. However, for each UDF created, it is possible to define
if managers and employees should also see it.

Introduction
CoreHR have a piece of functionality called the Job Seekers Register (“JSR”), which can be used to identify employees whose contracts are ending and who should be considered for redeployment within their companies.
The JSR is, in essence, just a register – adding an employee’s contract to it does not automate any kind of employment processes. However, the existence of a central register of “job seekers” may support the Senior Appointments team’s with the Priority Candidate Support Scheme (“PCSS”).
There are two ways to use the JSR:
Automatically – system rules can be configured to automatically identify employee contracts which are due to end and add them to the JSR.**
Manually – a flag called “JSR Override” can be used to manually add an employee’s contracts to and remove them from the JSR.

nd add them to the JSR.**
Manually – a flag called “JSR Override” can be used to manually add an employee’s contracts to and remove them from the JSR. **The automatic process requires a lot of careful thought about what types of contracts should be considered “eligible” for addition to the JSR. Rules can be configured based on organisational hierarchy and appointment details – e.g. all fixed-term contracts at Standard Grade 7 within a given department, or all contracts of any kind on the Marie Curie Student pay grade. These rules must be configured and thoroughly tested to ensure that they are working as desired. In the interests of speed, the Senior Appointments Team have opted not to adopt the automatic JSR process at this time.
The manual process for using the JSR is outlined below.
Adding an employee’s contract to the JSR
NB: The JSR functionality exists within CoreHR’s back-office. To access it, you must launch the back-office from CorePortal.
Navigate to: CorePersonnel > Employee Search > Person Profile
On the Employee Search screen, enter the name or personnel number of the employee you wish to add to the JSR. Double-click their record to enter the Person Profile screen.
In the upper right corner of the screen, go to the Select Detail menu and choose the option “Job Seekers”:
You will be taken to the Job Seekers Register screen.

er right corner of the screen, go to the Select Detail menu and choose the option “Job Seekers”:
You will be taken to the Job Seekers Register screen. NB: This is not the JSR itself, it’s just the area where you can add/remove a single employee.
In the lower half of the screen, you will see a list of the employee’s current appointments. Two fields are of interest here (circled in red):
JSR – this flag indicates whether the contract is already on the Job Seekers Register. It will be ticked once the record has been added by the overnight database job. This flag cannot be updated by users; it is a system-only flag.
JSR Override – This field determines whether the automatic or manual process will be used to add a contract to the JSR.
JSR Override has three options:
Calculate – use the eligibility rules configured in the system to determine whether the contract in question is eligible to be added to the JSR.
Yes – add the contract to the JSR manually, ignoring any eligibility criteria which may exist in the system.
No – never add the contract to the JSR, regardless of whether it meets any eligibility criteria.
To add a contract to the JSR, change the JSR Override field to “Yes”.
A warning message will appear. Click “Yes” to dismiss it:
Save your changes.

ia.
To add a contract to the JSR, change the JSR Override field to “Yes”.
A warning message will appear. Click “Yes” to dismiss it:
Save your changes. An overnight process (PERS_JOB_SEEKERS_REGISTER_PROC.PROCESS_J) will run in CoreHR, which will pick up the record you have amended and added it to the JSR.
The following day, if you return to the employee record, you will see the JSR flag is now ticked:
Removing an employee’s contract
If, for whatever reason, an employee no longer needs to be on the Job Seekers Register, it’s simple to remove them.
Navigate to: CorePersonnel > Employee Search > Person Profile
Go back to the employee record and choose “Job Seekers” from the Select Detail menu. On the Job Seekers Register screen, change the JSR Override field from “Yes” to “Calculate”:
The warning message will appear asking you to confirm you wish to make this change. Click “Yes” and save your changes. The overnight database job will run again and remove the employee contract from the JSR.
The following day, if you return to the employee record, you will see the JSR flag is no longer ticked.

Introduction
There is a piece of functionality within PeopleXD called the Job Seekers Register (“JSR”), which can be used to identify employees whose contracts are ending and who should be considered for redeployment within their companies.
The JSR is, in essence, just a register – adding an employee’s contract to it does not automate any kind of employment processes. However, the existence of a central register of “job seekers” may support the Senior Appointments team’s with the Priority Candidate Support Scheme (“PCSS”).
There are two ways to use the JSR:
Automatically – system rules can be configured to automatically identify employee contracts which are due to end and add them to the JSR.**
Manually – a flag called “JSR Override” can be used to manually add an employee’s contracts to and remove them from the JSR.

Manually – a flag called “JSR Override” can be used to manually add an employee’s contracts to and remove them from the JSR. **The automatic process requires a lot of careful thought about what types of contracts should be considered “eligible” for addition to the JSR. Rules can be configured based on organisational hierarchy and appointment details – e.g. all fixed-term contracts at Standard Grade 7 within a given department, or all contracts of any kind on the Marie Curie Student pay grade. These rules must be configured and thoroughly tested to ensure that they are working as desired. In the interests of speed, the Senior Appointments Team have opted not to adopt the automatic JSR process at this time.
The manual process for using the JSR is outlined below.
Adding an employee’s contract to the JSR
Navigate to: People Management > Employees > View > Key Information > Job Seekers Register
On the Employee Search screen, enter the name or personnel number of the employee you wish to add to the JSR. Click “View” to open the record:
On the Key Information tab, click the button for “Job Seekers Register” at the bottom of the screen:
You will be taken to the Job Seekers Register screen.
NB: This is not the JSR itself, it’s just the area where you can add/remove a single employee.

You will be taken to the Job Seekers Register screen.
NB: This is not the JSR itself, it’s just the area where you can add/remove a single employee. In the lower half of the screen, you will see a list of the employee’s current appointments. Two fields are of interest here (circled in red):
JSR – this flag indicates whether the contract is already on the Job Seekers Register. It will be ticked once the record has been added by the overnight database job. This flag cannot be updated by users; it is a system-only flag.
JSR Override – This field determines whether the automatic or manual process will be used to add a contract to the JSR.
JSR Override has three options:
Calculate – use the eligibility rules configured in the system to determine whether the contract in question is eligible to be added to the JSR.
Yes – add the contract to the JSR manually, ignoring any eligibility criteria which may exist in the system.
No – never add the contract to the JSR, regardless of whether it meets any eligibility criteria.
To add a contract to the JSR, change the JSR Override field to “Yes”.
A warning message will appear. Click “Yes” to dismiss it:
Your changes will be saved automatically.

Visual Studio Basics
This section provides some background information that you will need when working in Visual Studio.
Commonly-used terms
There are a number of commonly-used terms that appear throughout this document. A brief explanation of each is given here.
Term
Notes
Example
Dataset
A dataset is the SQL code which queries the PeopleXD database and returns results. It can be embedded (unique to a single .RDL file) or shared (available to re-use across multiple .RDL files).
“DataSet1” within any .RDL file contains the report SQL code.

Dataset (Shared) Shared datasets are SQL queries which are available to re-use across multiple .RDL files. We use shared datasets to return Lists of Values (LOVs) which power parameter drop-down lists.
LOV_Optional_DepartmentCode
Data source
A data source is a connection to a PeopleXD database (UOXC, UOXP, etc.).
Oracle_DS_UserCredentials
Deployment
The act of publishing a report (.RDL file) or a shared dataset to one of the HR Reporting environments.
Project
A project is a “sub-container” within a solution. The project is where your data sources, datasets, and reports are saved. A solution can contain multiple projects, but for HR Reporting, we have a strict 1-to-1 relationship between solutions and projects, such that each solution only contains a single project.
HR Reporting QA.sln contains project “HR Reporting QA”, which holds the data sources, shared datasets, and reports for the HR Reporting QA environment.

A report within Visual Studio is an individual .RDL file.

Details - What is changing?
Provide a brief explanation of what you are changing, and if possible, include the current SQL code and the new (amended) SQL code.
If you have made extensive changes to the SQL, it’s helpful to attach two .TXT files to your change: one containing the unchanged SQL, and one containing the amended SQL. If you do this, you should say “Refer to attachments” in your change description, rather than providing the SQL code inline.
Justification - Why is the change necessary?
Changes to reports are usually required to fix problems, e.g. error messages or a failure to return all the expected data – in those cases, the justification is “To resolve [brief description of problem]”. If there is a linked Incident, refer to it by number, i.e. “See linked Incident #X for details.”
If the request is for an enhancement rather than a “break-fix” request, then the justification should be provided on the Enhancement Form that users are required to submit.
Related Changes - Are there dependent changes?

If changing a report will have an impact on downstream services such as system integrations or HR processes (e.g. Payroll things), it’s worth detailing the impact here. Normally, however, you can just put “No impact on services”.
Impact - Specify downtime or at risk period
No downtime or at-risk period is entailed by a change to a report, so you can put “N/A”.
Impact - Effect of not applying the change?
Explain the problem which led to the report change, e.g. “Users will be unable to run the report successfully” or “Report will not return Fixed Term employees”.
Risk Assessment - What are the risks to the services?
It is very unlikely that a report change will ever pose a risk to services, so you can normally just put “N/A” here.

Background The SSRS reports developed by the Functional Analysis and HR Analytics teams are stored in the various HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE), where end-users may execute them as necessary. Two levels of security apply to every report: PeopleXD’s database security and HR Reporting’s “folder-based” security.
This how-to guide only addresses how to manage security within the HR Reporting environments. A brief note on PeopleXD’s database security is included for context.
PeopleXD’s database security
When a report query is executed, PeopleXD’s native security model is applied to the data within each .RDL file. This means that a given end-user will only be able to retrieve results which they have permission to view, based on the roles assigned to them within PeopleXD’s Security module. Security can apply to areas of the business, such as departments and divisions, or specific types of data, such as salary information.
Example: A user with permission to view all data in their current department runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for their own department.

epartment runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for their own department. Example: A user with permission to view data for Pay Group 20 (but not Pay Group 21) runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for Pay Group 20, and not Pay Group 21.
NB: Questions about Core’s database security must be handled by the HRIS Functional and Configuration Analyst (Michael O’Sullivan), who can confirm the security in place for individual users and amend it if required.
HR Reporting’s folder-based security
A second level of security has been imposed in the HR Reporting environments themselves, to ensure that users only see reports which are relevant to their line of work – for instance, a departmental user has no need to view Payroll or Pensions reports, but a Payroll user may need to view departmental reports.

of work – for instance, a departmental user has no need to view Payroll or Pensions reports, but a Payroll user may need to view departmental reports. This second level of security is “folder-based”. All the .RDL files in the HR Reporting environments are stored within a folder hierarchy, and each level of the folder hierarchy is shared with certain groups of users, depending on their reporting requirements. These user groups are managed via the Active Directory, and are therefore known as “AD Groups”. An AD group’s access to any level of the folder hierarchy is dependent upon the folders within that level being shared with the AD group.
Some contextual information about AD groups and the reporting folder hierarchy is given below.
The reporting folder hierarchy
The folder hierarchy is generically illustrated here:
Level 0 – Home: A user must have access to the Home folder of the reports server in order to access any of the folders or files located on the server. Access to the Home folder is assigned on the folder’s security profile. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to the Home folder, then that user will be able to access the reports server. Their access to the folders and files within the reports server depends on whether an AD group of which they are a member has been assigned to a given folder/file.

to the folders and files within the reports server depends on whether an AD group of which they are a member has been assigned to a given folder/file. Access to the Home folder is like having the key to the front door of a building. All the rooms in the building are locked and require their own keys, but a user must be able to get into the building itself before they can access individual rooms within it.
Level 1 – Navigation Folders: Once a user has accessed the Home folder, they can navigate to the reports they need via the Navigation folders. The Navigation folders contain broad groupings of reports according to their main audience and/or purpose, e.g. “Payroll” or “Recruitment”. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Navigation folder, then that user will be able to see the Navigation folder listed within the Home folder, and will be able to enter the Navigation folder to view its contents.
Level 2 – Subfolders: Once a user has entered a Navigation folder, the report they need may be present in a Report folder, or in a Subfolder. Subfolders are used to split very broad groups of reports into more granular categories; for instance Level 1 Personnel folder has three Level 2 subfolders: Current Reports, Monthly Reports, and Tracking Reports.

more granular categories; for instance Level 1 Personnel folder has three Level 2 subfolders: Current Reports, Monthly Reports, and Tracking Reports. Not every Navigation folder has Subfolders; however, where Subfolders exist, the same rules of access apply. To wit, if a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Subfolder, then that user will be able to see the Subfolder listed within the Navigation folder, and will be able to enter the Subfolder to view its contents.
Level 3 – Report Folders: Once a user has accessed a Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), they must select the report they wish to run by going to the appropriate Report folder. The Report folder contains the .RDL files which make up a report; a report may be comprised of one or many .RDL files. So long as a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Report folder, then that user will be able to see the Report folder listed within the Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), and will be able to enter the Report folder and access the .RDL files within it.
Note: Security is not applied at the level of individual .RDL files. If a user has access to a Report folder, they have access to all the .RDL files within that folder.

Background The SSRS reports developed by the Functional Analysis and HR Analytics teams are stored in the various HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE), where end-users may execute them as necessary. Two levels of security apply to every report: PeopleXD’s database security and HR Reporting’s “folder-based” security.
This how-to guide only addresses how to manage security within the HR Reporting environments. A brief note on PeopleXD’s database security is included for context.
PeopleXD’s database security
When a report query is executed, PeopleXD’s native security model is applied to the data within each .RDL file. This means that a given end-user will only be able to retrieve results which they have permission to view, based on the roles assigned to them within PeopleXD’s Security module. Security can apply to areas of the business, such as departments and divisions, or specific types of data, such as salary information.
Example: A user with permission to view all data in their current department runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for their own department.

epartment runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for their own department. Example: A user with permission to view data for Pay Group 20 (but not Pay Group 21) runs a report. PeopleXD’s database security ensures that when the user runs the report, they only retrieve results for Pay Group 20, and not Pay Group 21.
NB: Questions about Core’s database security must be handled by the HRIS Functional and Configuration Analyst (Michael O’Sullivan), who can confirm the security in place for individual users and amend it if required.
HR Reporting’s folder-based security
A second level of security has been imposed in the HR Reporting environments themselves, to ensure that users only see reports which are relevant to their line of work – for instance, a departmental user has no need to view Payroll or Pensions reports, but a Payroll user may need to view departmental reports.

of work – for instance, a departmental user has no need to view Payroll or Pensions reports, but a Payroll user may need to view departmental reports. This second level of security is “folder-based”. All the .RDL files in the HR Reporting environments are stored within a folder hierarchy, and each level of the folder hierarchy is shared with certain groups of users, depending on their reporting requirements. These user groups are managed via the Active Directory, and are therefore known as “AD Groups”. An AD group’s access to any level of the folder hierarchy is dependent upon the folders within that level being shared with the AD group.
Some contextual information about AD groups and the reporting folder hierarchy is given below.
The reporting folder hierarchy
The folder hierarchy is generically illustrated here:
Level 0 – Home: A user must have access to the Home folder of the reports server in order to access any of the folders or files located on the server. Access to the Home folder is assigned on the folder’s security profile. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to the Home folder, then that user will be able to access the reports server. Their access to the folders and files within the reports server depends on whether an AD group of which they are a member has been assigned to a given folder/file.

to the folders and files within the reports server depends on whether an AD group of which they are a member has been assigned to a given folder/file. Access to the Home folder is like having the key to the front door of a building. All the rooms in the building are locked and require their own keys, but a user must be able to get into the building itself before they can access individual rooms within it.
Level 1 – Navigation Folders: Once a user has accessed the Home folder, they can navigate to the reports they need via the Navigation folders. The Navigation folders contain broad groupings of reports according to their main audience and/or purpose, e.g. “Payroll” or “Recruitment”. If a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Navigation folder, then that user will be able to see the Navigation folder listed within the Home folder, and will be able to enter the Navigation folder to view its contents.
Level 2 – Subfolders: Once a user has entered a Navigation folder, the report they need may be present in a Report folder, or in a Subfolder. Subfolders are used to split very broad groups of reports into more granular categories; for instance Level 1 Personnel folder has three Level 2 subfolders: Current Reports, Monthly Reports, and Tracking Reports.

more granular categories; for instance Level 1 Personnel folder has three Level 2 subfolders: Current Reports, Monthly Reports, and Tracking Reports. Not every Navigation folder has Subfolders; however, where Subfolders exist, the same rules of access apply. To wit, if a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Subfolder, then that user will be able to see the Subfolder listed within the Navigation folder, and will be able to enter the Subfolder to view its contents.
Level 3 – Report Folders: Once a user has accessed a Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), they must select the report they wish to run by going to the appropriate Report folder. The Report folder contains the .RDL files which make up a report; a report may be comprised of one or many .RDL files. So long as a user is a member of an AD group assigned to a Report folder, then that user will be able to see the Report folder listed within the Navigation folder (or Subfolder, if applicable), and will be able to enter the Report folder and access the .RDL files within it.
Note: Security is not applied at the level of individual .RDL files. If a user has access to a Report folder, they have access to all the .RDL files within that folder.

Folder security for subscription-based reports A tiny number of reports within the HR Reporting environments are run on a “subscription” model, in which a report user “subscribes” to a report and the report is run automatically on the user’s behalf by the REPORT_POWERBI Service Account.
The Service Account has unlimited user sessions and unrestricted access to PeopleXD’s database, so it must be kept highly secure to prevent unwanted data breaches. This means that it will only be used to run reports in exceptional circumstances – namely, when a report consistently times out or fails to complete when run by an ordinary user.
An explanation of the special security measures for subscription-based reports is given below.
The Subscriptions folder
Navigate to: Home > Subscriptions
All subscription-based reports must be filed in a special Navigation folder called (unsurprisingly) “Subscriptions”. Access to this folder is tightly controlled to prevent unauthorised users from viewing any subscription-based reports. Only the HR Reporting “super-groups” and subscription-specific AD groups should be assigned to the Subscriptions folder.

If you have created a new subscription-based report, you must create a Report folder for it within the Subscriptions folder; for example Home > Subscriptions > PAYPAY25 National Minimum Wage Check:
Each Report folder within Subscriptions must only be shared with a single AD group, comprised of the user or users who have subscribed to that particular report.
Subscription-specific AD groups
Whenever you set up a subscription-based report, you will need to create a new AD group for the subscribers. As noted above, requests for the creation of new AD groups must be raised on OSM as Minor Changes and a task must be assigned to MPST with details of the new group. These details must include:
Group name – this must be in the format “HRIS-RR-SERVICE_[Report prefix]
Example: HRIS-RR-SERVICE_PERX14
Description – this must always be “Report run by the Service Account”.
MPST will create the group profile, and the HRIS Functional Analysis team can then add individual staff members.
Note: To prevent the possibility of data breaches, you must ensure that only those staff members who have subscribed to the report are added to the new AD group.

Overview The HR Reporting solution is a Microsoft-based user interface which allows users to run reports from the PeopleXD database within their web browsers. There are four environments (servers) for the HR Reporting solution, all of which are owned by the Microsoft Platform Services Team (MPST). MPST are responsible for any technical faults that arise in the environments, and for making any changes required to maintain the overall HR Reporting solution’s VPN connection to the PeopleXD database.
The day-to-day management of these environments is largely handled by the HRIS Analysis team, who own the report files, data sources, and datasets which are stored in each environment. This document focuses on the work carried out by the HRIS Analysis team.
NB: Software Solutions and Microsoft Platform Services manage a separate aspect of reporting via SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS); their processes are not detailed in this document. It’s important to note, however, that the password for the PeopleXD database service account is controlled solely by the HR Functional Analysis team, so if the SSIS connection to PeopleXD needs to be updated, the HR Functional Analysts are responsible for updating the service account password within SSIS.

Every HR Reporting environment relies on its data sources in order to connect to the appropriate PeopleXD database for report queries. The LIVE and QA environments look at the UOXP database, while the DEV and TEST environments can be configured to look at UOXU, UOXC, or UOXZ.

Context A parameter is technically “a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity”. Within the context of HR Reporting, parameters are values a report user can set before running a report. These values limit the query the report sends to the database, and therefore limit the data the report will return from the database.
Example: A report has a parameter for Department Code, which gives the user the option to select specific department codes for which they want to see results when they run the report. Let’s say they select code “AC”:
When the user clicks “View Report”, the report query will run. Because the user has selected code “AC”, the report query will only check the PeopleXD database for personnel records related to that department code. When the report is finished running, it will only display results for department code “AC”.
Example: A report has a parameter for Personnel Number, which gives the user the option to specify a personnel record for which they want to see results when they run the report. Let’s say they enter personnel number “2367246”:

the option to specify a personnel record for which they want to see results when they run the report. Let’s say they enter personnel number “2367246”: When the user clicks “View Report”, the report query will run. Because the user has specified personnel number “2367246”, the report query will only check the PeopleXD database for information related to that personnel number. When the report is finished running, it will only display results for personnel number “2367246”.
Report parameters are managed in three separate places:
The SQL code of the report query in the .RDL file: essential
The Parameters folder of the Report Data pane: essential
The Parameters textbox: optional (if the parameter values should be displayed at the top of the report each time it is run)
See below for detailed guidance.
Viewing a parameter
Parameters exist within report (.RDL) files, so to view the parameters for a report, you will need to open the .RDL file whose parameters you wish to view.
Within the SQL code
To see the parameters within a report’s SQL code, go to the Report Data pane. Expand the Datasets folder and select “DataSet1” – this is where the report query SQL code is held.
Double-click to open “DataSet1”. The Dataset Properties window will pop up. Go to the Query pane in the lower half of the window to see the SQL code for the report:

o open “DataSet1”. The Dataset Properties window will pop up. Go to the Query pane in the lower half of the window to see the SQL code for the report: If the report has parameters, they will be listed in “WHERE” clauses within the SQL code, and they will always be in the format :ParameterName.
In Oracle SQL, the colon (:) is what prompts the report query to check for a user-defined value before executing the query. All parameter names must be preceded by a colon.
You can scroll down the Query pane to find the parameters within the SQL code, or you can copy the contents of the Query pane into a Notepad file and do a search for “:” to jump quickly to any parameters in the code:
Within the Parameters folder
All the parameters present in the .RDL SQL query will also be present in the Parameters folder of the Report Data pane. Simply expand the folder to see the list of parameters:
You can click into each parameter to view its properties. You can also access parameters within the section at the top of the Design pane – simply double-click the parameter you wish to view:
Double-clicking a parameter in either the Report Data pane or the Design pane will open the Report Parameter Properties window for that specific parameter.

e-clicking a parameter in either the Report Data pane or the Design pane will open the Report Parameter Properties window for that specific parameter. There are three main aspects to any parameter: General, Available Values, and Default Values. You can view these by clicking the tabs at the side of the Report Parameter Properties window.
General: this tab defines the name of the parameter, the prompt a user sees when running the report, what type of data the parameter will accept, and whether or not the parameter should be visible to users.
Available Values: this tab defines the list of values (LOV) which can be passed to a parameter, e.g. a list of department codes. If Available Values are defined, the parameter will only accept values from that list.
Default Values: this tab defines what value(s) should automatically be passed to the parameter whenever a report is opened. Users can change the default value to something specific; the default is just present to save people time, so they don’t always have to select the most commonly-used values for a parameter.

Within the .RDL file’s Design pane, the textbox looks like this: To view how the parameters are set up in the textbox, right-click it and select “Expression”:
The Expression window will pop up. Within this window, you can see the VBA code which determines how each parameter is displayed within the textbox when the report is run.

What the code is saying
The VBA code here is just an IF-THEN-ELSE statement and can be understood as follows:
IF the DepartmentCode parameter is blank (Value = “”), THEN the textbox should display the string “Department code: ‘< All department codes >’”.
ELSE if the DepartmentCode parameter is not blank, the textbox should look at whatever values have been selected for the DepartmentCode parameter, and display the string “Department code: ‘[parameter value1, parameter value2,…]’”.

Creating a new parameter
Within the SQL code
To add a new parameter to the SQL code of the .RDL file, you will need to modify the appropriate “WHERE” clause within the code. Some reports contain only one “WHERE” clause, but complex reports may contain several, as conditions and parameters are applied to the query at different stages.
Decide where in the SQL you want to add the parameter, then add it to the “WHERE” clause in one of the following formats:
For parameters which use a drop-down LOV…
Format: (VIEW.ITEM IN (:Parameter) OR ‘-1’ IN (:Parameter))
Example: (prbi_appointment_history.department_description IN (:Department) OR '-1' IN (:Department))
For parameters which use a free-text field (single value)…
Format: (VIEW.ITEM = (:Parameter) OR (:Parameter) IS NULL)
Example: (prbi_hr_person_master.person_reference=(:PersonRef) OR (:PersonRef) IS NULL)
For parameters which use a free-text field (multi-value), see the Appendix.
Once you’ve modified the SQL, be sure to save your changes to the .RDL file.
