Naming standards for prompts
In order to maintain a consistent look and feel across the HR Reporting catalogue, parameter prompts must follow certain naming standards. These are outlined below.
The prompt for a person reference must always be Personnel number.
The word “description” is always omitted from prompt text; e.g. if the parameter is for “department description”, the prompt must be simply Department.
Prompts of more than one word should only capitalise the first word; e.g. a prompt for the “employee status” value should be Employee status, not “Employee Status”.

Appendix: Free-text multi-value parameters
Many reports have free-text parameters which will accept multiple values in a comma-separated list, e.g. a list of pay codes. This enables report users to type in a list of the exact codes they want to see in the report, without having to scroll through a long drop-down LOV to select each code.
The SQL which supports a free-text multi-value parameter is a little complicated, so here’s a worked example for the pay code parameter shown above.
The WITH clause
Free-text multi-value parameters rely on something called a “WITH” clause, which is a bit of SQL which defines a temporary dataset whose output is available to be referenced in subsequent queries.

(WITH temporary_dataset AS (SELECT :Parameter AS temporary_item FROM DUAL)
SELECT
…rest of SELECT statement… )
Example:

SELECT
PABI_PAY_HISTORY.PAYROLL_PERIOD as PAYROLL_PERIOD… )
The WITH clause here has created a temporary view called paycodetext which contains a temporary item called paycode_text. The values available for the paycodetext.paycode_text item are defined by whatever the report user enters in the :PayCode parameter free-text field.

Context This document outlines the release and deployment processes for reports in the HR Reporting catalogue. These processes were designed to support robust version control of all the report suites which comprise the HR Reporting catalogue, to ensure that:
users have access only to the most recent version of any report suite
there is only a single “active” version of any given report suite at any given time
previous versions of amended or retired report suites (where applicable) are available in case they need to be viewed or restored to active use
NB: The most important aspect of version control for the HR Reporting catalogue is this: versioning is done at the report suite-level, not the .RDL level.
This means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite.

his means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite. For example, say you are making a change to the report suite PERDEP01 Staff in Post. This report suite consists of 13 separate .RDL files. Even if you are only making a change to one of those 13 .RDLs, you must update the version number on all 13 .RDLs – that is, if you update e.g. the Full Data Set.RDL and promote it from Version 6.0 to Version 7.0, you must also promote the version numbers for the rest of the .RDL files within the report suite to the new version number.

What if you haven’t actually changed every .RDL file?
Generally speaking, when you update a report suite that contains multiple .RDL files, you will only be changing the SQL code in a few of those .RDLs, not all of them. If you’ve got some .RDL files in your report suite which have not been edited, use this Report Summary Header instead – it’ll make it obvious to anyone who opens the file that the code for this particular .RDL wasn’t updated when the report suite version changed:

Most importantly, users can also search for the Change ID on OSM and find the full details of and justification for the update – this is a major time-saver when reviewing SQL queries!
Note that for new reports, you will still need to include these details in the Report Summary header. The version will be “1.0” and the change request should detail both the function of the new report and the justification for creating it.

Live Reports Tracker The Live Reports Tracker is a spreadsheet which contains details of all active reports in the HR Reporting catalogue, including each report’s name, where it is filed in the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, and which AD groups it is shared with.

The report’s prefix (e.g. PERDEP01)
The report’s name (e.g. Staff in Post)
The report’s location within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy (e.g. Home > Personnel > Current Reports)
The AD groups which have permission to view the report in the HR Reporting_LIVE environment (e.g. HRIS-RR-PERDREP – Personnel).

A data source is technically the source of the data which is returned by a report query, i.e. the PeopleXD database which powers your reports (UOXC, UOXP, etc.). In Visual Studio, though, the term “data source” refers to something more like a connection profile – it’s where you both define which PeopleXD database you’re going to use, and provide the login credentials for accessing that database.

ction profile – it’s where you both define which PeopleXD database you’re going to use, and provide the login credentials for accessing that database. There are two shared data sources held in all of the HR Reporting Visual Studio solutions and used across the majority of reports:
Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount: This data source is linked to a PeopleXD service account rather than a standard user account. It is primarily used to run the SQL queries for the shared datasets which populate report parameters, e.g. to retrieve all department codes for use in a parameter’s drop-down list.

Context
Shared datasets are SQL queries which are available to re-use across multiple report (.RDL) files. In HR Reporting, shared datasets are used to retrieve reference data from PeopleXD, in order to populate drop-down lists for report parameters.
Example: Many reports have a “Department” parameter, which allows users to specify which department(s) they want to see returned in the report results. It looks like this:
The shared dataset LOV_Optional_Department.rsd is the source of information for the “Department” parameter’s drop-down list. The shared dataset queries PeopleXD’s database and returns a list of all active departments. This list is then attached to the “Department” parameter, so that users can select the departments in which they are interested.
Because LOV_Optional_Department.rsd is a shared dataset, it can be attached to any report which has a “Department” parameter.
Shared datasets are managed in two places: Visual Studio, where they are created and amended, and the HR Reporting environments, where they are deployed to run alongside reports. See below for detailed guidance.

A note on naming conventions All shared datasets are prefixed with the phrase “LOV_Optional”, because shared datasets return lists of values (LOVs) from which users can select the options in which they are interested. Shared datasets must adhere to the following naming conventions to make it easy to identify what sort of data a given dataset might return.
If the dataset returns reference codes, the convention is:
LOV_Optional + Reference item_Code
If the dataset returns reference descriptions, the convention is:
LOV_Optional_Reference item
If the dataset returns reference codes and descriptions, the convention is:
LOV_Optional + Reference item +_and_Description

The Shared Dataset Properties window will open.
All shared datasets have the following properties:
Name – the name of the dataset .RSD file (this must follow the naming conventions outlined above).
Data source – the shared data source for the dataset. This should always be Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount.

A shared dataset (.RSD) is like a report (.RDL): both run SQL code which queries the PeopleXD database to retrieve information. Just like reports, shared datasets need to be deployed from Visual Studio to the HR Reporting environments so that users can run the queries.

If a shared dataset does not exist in an HR Reporting environment, it won’t be able to populate drop-down lists for any report parameters which depend on that dataset.
For example, if a report has a parameter for “Department Code”, the shared dataset which retrieves the list of department codes from PeopleXD must exist in the HR Reporting environment, or the parameter will not work.

Editing a shared dataset
Generally speaking, you shouldn’t need to make changes to shared datasets, because they are set up to return data from reference tables within the database – this means that any changes made in the database should automatically be reflected in the shared dataset.
Example: The LOV_Optional_Department dataset is programmed to return a list of all department names from PeopleXD. Whenever a new department is added to PeopleXD, it automatically appears in the shared dataset – you don’t need to do anything to make this happen.
Some shared datasets, however, have hard-coded values or filtered results which may need occasional tweaking.

Some shared datasets, however, have hard-coded values or filtered results which may need occasional tweaking. Example: The LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason dataset is programmed to return a list of absence-related appointment reasons from PeopleXD. The SQL query for this dataset specifies that only appointment reasons which meet certain conditions should be returned, e.g. when the reason includes the term ‘ADOPTION’ or ‘SICKNESS’. If a new absence-related appointment reason is added to PeopleXD, you will need to hard-code it into the shared dataset!

Getting Started with SQL Developer Before you can create or edit reports, you will need to launch the Oracle SQL Developer application and connect to the PeopleXD database you wish to query.
SQL Developer is a remote desktop application. You can find it in your Start menu under “CONNECT Remote Services (RADC)”:
Double-click the entry in your Start menu to launch SQL Developer, and enter your CONNECT login details when prompted – these are necessary in order to access the CONNECT Remote Desktop:

You’ll land on the Welcome Page, which contains links to any databases to which you have previously connected, as well as links to Oracle resources for SQL Developer users. The only thing you’ll generally use here is the Database Connection pane:

If you’ve never used SQL Developer before, you will need to create the database connections you require. This is done by setting up something called a connection profile. See below for details.

Using SQL Worksheets
In order to run reports in SQL Developer, you need to use a worksheet. A worksheet is a page where you write (or copy-paste) the SQL code that you’ll use to query the PeopleXD database. When you launch SQL Developer and connect to a database, SQL Developer opens a worksheet for you automatically in a new tab:

ry the PeopleXD database. When you launch SQL Developer and connect to a database, SQL Developer opens a worksheet for you automatically in a new tab: If you’re building a new report (or simply running a small query of some kind), you can simply type your SQL code into the worksheet. If you’ve got the SQL code for an existing report, you can paste it into the worksheet.
Once you’ve got your code in place, click the little green arrow at the top of the worksheet to execute the code:
SQL Developer will read the code you’ve entered in the worksheet and will query the PeopleXD database for the information you’ve requested. This may take some time, depending on how complicated the query is, so you might see this progress bar whilst SQL Developer works:
Once SQL Developer has finished executing the code, the results of the query will be displayed in the Query Result pane at the bottom of the screen.
Exporting the results
You may wish to export the results of your SQL query to an Excel file for further analysis. To do this, right-click anywhere in the Query Results pane and select “Export…” from the pop-up menu:

You need to specify what file format you wish to export the results to, and where on the network you want the export to be saved. In the “Format” field, select “csv”, and in the “File” field, enter the file-path for the network location to which you are exporting the results:
Note: Never export results to the Desktop or C:\ drive.
SQL Developer is a remote desktop application – you would be exporting results to the remote desktop, not to your own PC! This is a security risk. It also makes it very difficult to access the file once it’s finished exporting!

It also provides a running count of how many rows of data have been exported, which may enable you to estimate when the export should be finished (e.g. if you know there are approximately 1,000 rows of data and the Task Progress pane shows that 500 rows have been exported in 30 seconds, you can safely assume that the remaining 500 rows will be exported in the next 30 seconds).

Tables are datasets organised by columns and rows. The columns are the “attributes” of the table – things like PERSON_REFERENCE and SURNAME. The rows are where the “records” are stored.

ORA-00932: inconsistent datatypes: expected DATE got NUMBER This error occurs if your SQL query is attempting to compare two dates within a calculation or a WHERE condition, and one of the dates is not in “Date” format.
Check for any TRUNC() functions wrapped around dates. The TRUNC() function attempts to read anything within the brackets as if it is in date format. If you feed a non-date variable into a TRUNC() function, such as a text string or an integer, TRUNC() can’t understand what you’re asking it to do.

A solution is effectively a “bucket” in which related files can be stored – there’s a lot more to this concept, but the important thing to remember is that each solution has its own data sources, datasets, and report files.

Context This document outlines the release and deployment processes for reports in the HR Reporting catalogue. These processes were designed to support robust version control of all the report suites which comprise the HR Reporting catalogue, to ensure that:
users have access only to the most recent version of any report suite
there is only a single “active” version of any given report suite at any given time
previous versions of amended or retired report suites (where applicable) are available in case they need to be viewed or restored to active use
NB: The most important aspect of version control for the HR Reporting catalogue is this: versioning is done at the report suite-level, not the .RDL level.
This means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite.

his means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite. For example, say you are making a change to the report suite PERDEP01 Staff in Post. This report suite consists of 13 separate .RDL files. Even if you are only making a change to one of those 13 .RDLs, you must update the version number on all 13 .RDLs – that is, if you update e.g. the Full Data Set.RDL and promote it from Version 6.0 to Version 7.0, you must also promote the version numbers for the rest of the .RDL files within the report suite to the new version number.

By updating the version numbers for each .RDL within a report suite, you ensure that the entire report suite is promoted from one version to the next. This prevents complications like having Full Data Set (Version 6.0) in the same report as Limited Data Set (Version 2.0).

Report Summary headers
The SQL query for every .RDL file contains a “Report Summary” header. This header identifies the following attributes of the .RDL file:
Attribute
Meaning
Name
The name of the report suite
Tab name
The name of the individual .RDL file
Version
The major version of the report suite to which this SQL query belongs
Last updated
Month and year of most recent update to report suite
Change ID
OSM Change Request number
NB

A completed example is shown here:
/*************** REPORT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes
** Tab name: Appointment Changes
** Version: 5.0
** Last updated: JULY 2021

RT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes
** Tab name: Appointment Changes
** Version: 5.0
** Last updated: JULY 2021 ** Change ID: 20012493
***************************************************/
Whenever you update the version number of a report suite, you must update the Report Summary header for every .RDL file within that report suite to reflect the new version number, the month & year the report suite was updated, and the OSM Change Request number relating to the update.
What if you haven’t actually changed every .RDL file?
Generally speaking, when you update a report suite that contains multiple .RDL files, you will only be changing the SQL code in a few of those .RDLs, not all of them. If you’ve got some .RDL files in your report suite which have not been edited, use this Report Summary Header instead – it’ll make it obvious to anyone who opens the file that the code for this particular .RDL wasn’t updated when the report suite version changed:
/*************** REPORT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes

** Version: 5.0

***************************************************/

***************************************************/ Providing these details in the Report Summary header enables any user reviewing the SQL query to quickly determine which version of the query they are looking at and when it was last updated. Most importantly, users can also search for the Change ID on OSM and find the full details of and justification for the update – this is a major time-saver when reviewing SQL queries!
Note that for new reports, you will still need to include these details in the Report Summary header. The version will be “1.0” and the change request should detail both the function of the new report and the justification for creating it.

There are four HR Reporting solutions (.sln files) in Visual Studio: DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE. The DEV solution is used for creating and testing brand-new reports, while the TEST solution is mainly restricted to project testing and testing updated reports against specific data in test environments. Version control in Visual Studio is managed in the HR Reporting_QA.sln and the HR Reporting_LIVE.sln.

The DEV environment is used for creating and testing brand-new reports, while the TEST environment is mainly restricted to project testing. Version control is managed in the HR Reporting QA environment and the HR Reporting LIVE environment.

Live Reports Tracker The Live Reports Tracker is a spreadsheet which contains details of all active reports in the HR Reporting catalogue, including each report’s name, where it is filed in the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, and which AD groups it is shared with.
Version control is not managed as such in the Live Reports Tracker, however this document must be updated whenever you create a new report, retire an existing report, or amend any of the following aspects of an existing report:
The report’s prefix (e.g. PERDEP01)
The report’s name (e.g. Staff in Post)
The report’s location within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy (e.g. Home > Personnel > Current Reports)
The AD groups which have permission to view the report in the HR Reporting_LIVE environment (e.g. HRIS-RR-PERDREP – Personnel).
Refer to the process below for further information on when and how to update the Live Reports Tracker.

Creating new report folders
Before you can file the .RDLs for your new report, you’ll need to ensure you’ve actually got a report folder in place for them. Follow this process to create a new report folder in any HR Reporting environment.
Please ensure that you are fully familiar with the use of folder access permissions within HR Reporting before you create a new folder. This is essential in order to avoid data breaches.
Where should your new report folder go?

Format switch(\*)
The Format field switch (\*) defines how to display field results. The format instructions determine the following:
The use of uppercase and lowercase letters
Number formats — for example, whether 9 is displayed as ix (roman numerals) or ninth (ordinal text)

Format switches also retain a field result's formatting when the field is updated.

Numeric format switch (\#)
The Numeric format switch (\#) specifies the display of a numeric result.
For example, the switch \# $#,##0.00 in { = SUM(ABOVE) \# $#,##0.00 } displays a result such as "$4,455.70." If the result of a field is not a number, this switch has no effect.
Note: Quotation marks are not required around simple numeric formats that do not include spaces — for example, { MarchSales \# $#,##0.00 }. For more complex numeric formats and those that include text or spaces, enclose the numeric format in quotation marks, as shown in the following examples. Word adds quotation marks to numeric format switches if you insert a field by using the Field dialog box or the Formula command in the Data group of the Layout tab (Table Tools contextual tab).

Back to formatting switches
Date-Time format switch (\@)
The Date-Time format switch (\@) specifies the display of a date or time. For example, the switch \@ "dddd, MMMM d, yyyy" in the field { DATE \@ "dddd, MMMM d, yyyy" } displays "Friday, November 23, 2007." Combine the following date and time instructions — day (d), month (M), and year (y); hours (h) and minutes (m) — to build a date-time format. You can also include text, punctuation, and spaces.
Date instructions:
Month (M)
The letter M must be uppercase to distinguish months from minutes.
M    This format item displays the month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit months. For example, July is 7.
MM    This format item displays the month as a number with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit months. For example, July is 07.
MMM    This format item displays the month as a three-letter abbreviation. For example, July is Jul.
MMMM    This format item displays the month as its full name.
Day (d)
The letter d displays the day of the month or the day of the week. The letter d can be either uppercase or lowercase.
d    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 6.

the day of the week or month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 6. dd    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a number with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 06.
ddd    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a three-letter abbreviation. For example, Tuesday is displayed as Tue.
dddd    This format item displays the day of the week as its full name.
Year (y)
The letter y displays the year as two or four digits. The letter y can be either uppercase or lowercase.
yy    This format item displays the year as two digits with a leading 0 (zero) for years 01 through 09. For example, 1999 is displayed as 99, and 2006 is displayed as 06.
yyyy    This format item displays the year as four digits.
Time instructions:
Hours (h)
A lowercase h bases time on the 12-hour clock. An uppercase H bases time on the 24-hour, or military, clock; for example, 5 P.M. is displayed as 17.
h or H    This format item displays the hour without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 9.
hh or HH    This format item displays the hour with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 09.
Minutes (m)

This format item displays the hour with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 09.
Minutes (m) The letter m must be lowercase to distinguish minutes from months.
m    This format item displays minutes without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit minutes. For example, { TIME \@ "m" } displays 2.
mm    This format item displays minutes with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit minutes. For example, { TIME \@ "mm" } displays 02.
Seconds (s)
s    This format item displays seconds without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit seconds. For example { TIME \@ “s” displays 5.
ss    This format item displays seconds with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit seconds For example { TIME \@ “ss” displays 05.
A.M. and P.M. (AM/PM)
This displays A.M. and P.M. To change the A.M. and P.M. symbols for Microsoft Windows, change the regional settings in Control Panel.
am/pm or AM/PM    This format item displays A.M. and P.M. as uppercase. For example, { TIME \@ "h AM/PM" } and { TIME \@ "h am/pm" } display 9 AM or 5 PM.

In April 2021, we discovered that some users were unable to run reports on the HR Reporting servers unless they took the steps outlined below – see OSM Problem Record #40002259 for full details.
These steps may prove useful for other browser-related issues.
If a user is experiencing problems with a browser-based process, e.g. running reports or doing work in the Portal, there are some common troubleshooting techniques you can employ to try to resolve the issue. This document explains how to: run an incognito browsing session, clear browsing history, and disable extensions on all common PC browsers.
Incognito browsing
If a user is having problems with a process and you suspect their browser may be to blame, it is useful to try running the process in an “incognito” browser session before you clear their history or disable their extensions.

may be to blame, it is useful to try running the process in an “incognito” browser session before you clear their history or disable their extensions. An incognito session is a temporary browser session that is isolated from the browser's main session and user data – that is, it is “unaware of” any of the cached data or extensions that are normally present when the browser is running.
To open an incognito browser session in any browser, follow the instructions below.
Browser
Directions
Google Chrome
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N
From the menu: Select “New incognito window”
Mozilla Firefox
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P
From the menu: Select “New Private Window”
Microsoft Edge
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N
From the menu: Select “New InPrivate window”
Microsoft Internet Explorer
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P
From the menu: Select “Safety” and then “InPrivate browsing”
The browser session may open in a new tab or a new window, depending on the browser you are using.
If your user is able to run their process successfully in an incognito browsing session, that indicates that you will need to clear their browser history and disable their extensions to allow the user to run their process in a normal browser session. Overview
The Shift Type configuration screen is available via Portal on the WFM Admin Dashboard.
The following menu profile should be assigned in order to gain access to the steps below.
WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES
A shift type determines the hours an employee is contracted to work. Departmental HR Administrators assign the appropriate shift types to appointments via People Management > Work Schedule, but can only assign shift types that have been created by HR Systems.
Shift Types and Daily Work Patterns
Shift Types are formed by assigning a work pattern to each day of the week. A work pattern is the number of hours worked in a day, the start and end times are irrelevant, so an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 08:00AM would require the same work pattern as an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 11:00AM.

ee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 08:00AM would require the same work pattern as an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 11:00AM. Work patterns are broken into 3 minute intervals (the lowest number that can be accurately decimalised). The largest work pattern available is a 13 hour day.
On days when employees are not required to work the ‘REST’ work pattern is used.
Rotating/flexible shift patterns
Most employees follow the same pattern each week. If an employee varies between different patterns each week see part B.
If an employee has a flexi-time arrangement, where there is no predefined pattern, they should be assigned one of the standard shifts based on their average daily hours. For example, if someone works 25 hours across 5 days, they should be assigned a shift type with a 5 hour work pattern on each day, Monday-Friday.
Departmental HR should request a new shift type via OSM service request and provide a copy of the Shift Code Generator for the shift type required.
Generating a shift type code
Each shift type has a unique code and a name (description). The codes for weekly shift patterns are generated using the Shift Type Code Generator, with each code represents a unique combination of daily work patterns. This prevents multiple shift types being created with the same pattern. Codes for Rotating shift types are linked to the employee appointments.

e 'Start Day' configured for the Company. For example, if the start day of the Company is Monday then the start date of the calendar must be a Monday. Overview
The Workgroup Override allows the user to override certain workgroup settings at an employee level.
Currently the only override setting being utilised is the Holiday Scheme. The Holiday Scheme calculates when an employee is allowed to book leave and this is derived from the workgroup as default. In certain circumstances where multiple employees share the same workgroup, but have differing holiday terms, then the Holiday Scheme against the workgroup can be overridden at employee level and these are the steps covered in this guide.
NB: To complete this process the following menu options must be enabled:
‘WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Work Group Override’
‘WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Add/Update Work Group Override’.

Login to PeopleXD
Navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Person Maintenance

1.12 Holiday Schemes
During Discovery it was highlighted that the different Departments within the University have different Public Holidays and Company Closure Days.
To ensure that employees are treated to these days off, the dates of the Public Holidays and Company Closure Days have been configured into the Holiday Schemes.
The hours relative to these have been deducted from the employee’s entitlement, leaving just the days left to take at their leisure.
There are three different Holiday Schemes for the different Departments and will only apply to those Departments where employees have been granted a Balance with Entitlements.
By adding the Holiday Scheme to the Annual Leave Balance, the system computes the Annual Leave Balance as follows:

ranted a Balance with Entitlements.
By adding the Holiday Scheme to the Annual Leave Balance, the system computes the Annual Leave Balance as follows: Balance Entitlement from Annual Leave Scheme + Public Holidays/Company Closure Days – any days taken = Remaining Entitlement.
The Holiday Scheme dates have been configured in accordance with those provided in the IG. However, this area of the system will require ongoing maintenance for future years for both the Company Closure Days and the Public Holidays.

Functionality has been enabled to allow Timesheets that have been submitted within a specific time frame that remain unconfirmed at the point of generating timesheets into pay to be allowed to roll over to the next month.

The system uses the ‘Countback’ weeks to determine how many months these hours can be rolled forward for and once exhausted will not include the hours in any roll forward periods.

3.4 Generate Timesheet – inc. Ignore Unconfirmed Hours The Generate Timesheet Process is the process from transferring Online Timesheet Claims from CoreTime to CorePay using a specific set of dates laid out within the User Defined Calendar.
There are two modes of generation – Test and Live explained below
3.4.1 Generate Timesheet – Test Mode
When generating the Timesheet in TEST Mode, the system will automatically draw in all Online Timesheet Claims for the open month within the User Defined Calendar.
In Test Mode, the Generate Timesheet process can be run as many times as required, and for all combinations of Work Groups:
Single Work Group
Selection of Work Groups
All Work Groups.

Navigation: CoreTime Roster > Period End > Generate Timesheets
3.4.2 Generate Timesheet – LIVE Mode
The Timesheets should never be generated in LIVE mode until the very last run and all checks have taken place ready for payment.
When the Timesheets are run in Live Mode, the system will:
Generate the Timesheets for Payment and transfer into CorePay
Update the User Defined Calendar to the next process period

Live Mode, the system will:

Once the Generate Timesheet process has been run in Live, there is not an option to reverse back to the previous month.

Background
A Holiday Scheme is a list of closure dates, such as public/bank holidays and departmental fixed closure days. These dates will be treated as non-working days for anyone linked to the Holiday Scheme (via their Balance). The system using employee work schedules to determine if the employee would normally work on the closure day and adjusts their entitlement accordingly.
A Holiday scheme can be linked to a Balance, but this is optional and Balances will function without a Holiday Scheme. Holiday Schemes should not be used with Accrual Balances.

Different FTE Hours
Different Long Service Schemes
Different leave years
Different Base Entitlement
All Balances linked to a Holiday Scheme must share the same:

What are Work Patterns Work Patterns define a daily work schedule. They identify the different work durations that exist within the organisation and capture the expected working hours for an employee. Selected work patterns are then used to configure an employee’s shift type. Work patterns are an integral part of the system linking to multiple areas.
Accessing the Work Patterns screen
The Work Pattern screen is where administrators can manage work patterns for their organisation. The screen lists all Work Patterns created and shows if they are active or not. This screen can be used to create new work patterns, copy existing work patterns and further configure patterns to organisational requirements.
To access the Work Patterns screen, navigate via
WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > select Work Patterns.
The following Work Patterns screen displays.
There is a search and filter option available on the Work Patterns screen, allowing you to search for a specific work pattern or filter by Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Active or Label.
The screen contains the following fields:

Calculation Method

Active Indicator
When the active indicator is enabled the work pattern is available to be added to a Shift Type.
How to Add a new Work Pattern
To add a new work pattern, complete the following steps:
1. Click Add at the top of the screen.
2. Fill in the mandatory fields Pattern Code, Description, Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Default Hours, Default Start Time, Default End Time, Earliest Start Time.
3. Click OK.
4. Your new Work Pattern will open for you to further configure, using the tabs on the left-hand side. For example, add Standard Hours and Breaks.
5. Once your Work Pattern is fully configured, click Save.
6. Your Work Pattern is now ready to be added to a Shift Type.

How to Copy a Work Pattern
To copy a work pattern, complete the following steps: 1. Select Copy from the 3-dot menu of the work pattern you wish to copy.
2. Fill in the Pattern Code.
3. Fill in the Description.
4. Click OK.
5. Your copied Work Pattern will open for you to further configure.
Configuration of a Work Pattern
The configuration screens allow you to customise and configure work patterns and can be accessed through the Work Patterns screen by selecting the 3-dot ellipses and selecting View/Edit Work Pattern.
General Parameters
At the current time only the General Parameters screen is utilised, however as further functionality such as Rostering is introduced the other areas are likely to require configuration.
The General Parameters screen contains the main information pertaining to the Work Pattern and allows to configure for example, default hours as well as start and end time. As with all of the other screens, the Start Time, End Time and Default Hours are displayed at the top of the screen.

The Workgroup Override allows the user to override certain workgroup settings at an employee level.

1. Introduction
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how employee allowance records are
managed on People Management.
Guidance will be provided on the following topics:
• Key concepts and terminology associated with allowances.
• Creating an allowance.
• Editing an existing allowance.
• Ending an existing allowance.
• Cancelling or deleting an allowance.
• The impact of salary amendments on existing allowances.
1.2. Allowances in HR vs Payroll
The allowances that are setup in People Management for the employee’s contract are ‘permanent
/ reoccurring allowances’. These are allowances that are assigned to the employee’s contract for a
fixed or open-ended period. Every time payroll is run for that employee’s contract , the allowance
amount is calculated and included in the employee’s pay.
For example: An employee is assigned a ‘Night Duty’ allowance of £25 per period (e.g. per month).

nt is calculated and included in the employee’s pay.
For example: An employee is assigned a ‘Night Duty’ allowance of £25 per period (e.g. per month). The allowance was assigned to the employee’s contract with a start date of 1st March 2019. This is
open-ended i.e. no planned end d ate exists for the allowances and the intention is that the
employee should continue to receive the allowance until further notice. Every month when Payroll
is processed, the allowance of £25 will be added to the employee’s calculated salary.
Once-off allowance payments are not recorded in People Management . These are once off
payments that will be made for the employee for the current pay period e.g. a bonus payment.
These are captured directly in Payroll.

1.3. Allowance Types
There are a number of types of allowances supported on CoreHR.
Allowance Type Description
Value
These Allowances will pay a single specified amount every pay period e.g. if
an employee is on a monthly pay group and has a standard value allowance
of £100, then £100 will be paid every month.
There are 2 types of ‘Value’ based allowances:
• Standard Valu e: A specified amount is defined on the Allowance
Pay Code and that set amount is paid for all employees lin ked to it,
for every pay period e.g. Night Duty allowance is set at £30 per

Pay Code and that set amount is paid for all employees lin ked to it,
for every pay period e.g. Night Duty allowance is set at £30 per period for everyone.
• Variable Value: The amount to be paid is specific t o the individual
employee. This is not captured at the Pay Code level but it specified
when setting up the allowance for the employee. This allows
different employees to receive varying values for the same
Allowance Pay Code e.g. Mary has a Night Duty allowance of £30 but
John has a Night Duty allowance of £40.
Please note: if an Allowance is required to have a standard value set up at
Pay Code level for the majority of employees, but it is required to capture
different values for that Allowance for a handful of employees, the Pay Code
standard value can be overwritten when it is being set up for each
employee. Please refer to Payroll user guides for further details on how
these Allowance Pay Codes are configured for the options listed above.
Percentage
These Allowances will pay a percentage of the employee’s actual salary
every pay period
e.g. Tom gets £1000.00 per week gross pay. He gets a shift allowance of 12%
of gross pay , so each week he is in receipt of and additional £120.00 shift

customer account within DocuSign e.g. hr@acme.com, johndoe@acme.com. Users initiating the
process from PeopleXD will be logged into this DocuSign account in a restricted preview and send
mode.

1.2. What are Requests?
1.2.1. Employee Requests
This allows employees to submit a request form within PeopleXD that can be routed to its
intended recipient via workflow process. For example, you can set up requests for a cycle to work
scheme, child care voucher or equipment.
1.2.2. Manager Requests?
This allows managers to submit a request form on behalf of an employee that can be routed to
its intended recipient via a workflow process. For example you can set up requests for a contract
change, notification of leaver, or change of access.

1. Overview
The employee bulk update functionality allows you to update employee records at scale, that
would otherwise require time-consuming individual updates or support from Optimisation
Services. This is a Data Migration process where you can download an available template, or
create your own template with a variety of contract elements.
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the employee bulk update
feature.
This includes:
• The available default templates
• Creating a custom template for contract bulk updates
• Processing a bulk update
• How to configure the system to support bulk updates

associated helper files, and manage contract specific templates. This can be accessed from the
People Management dashboard.

2.1. Default Templates There are various standard templates available on the widget, detailed in the sections below.
2.1.1. Bulk End Allowances
The Bulk End Allowances template allows you to bulk end active (approved) allowances. The file
requires you to provide the following details:
• Personnel number
• Appointment ID the allowance is linked to
• The allowance pay code to be ended
• An end date.
Note: It’s recommended to co-ordinate with your Payroll team when performing this
update, as once the records in the file are processed, it will automatically feed through to
PeopleXD Payroll.

2.1.2. Bulk Load Salary
The Bulk Load Salary template allows you to bulk upload new salary amendments against active
(commenced) contracts/employee records. This is beneficial where you currently do not use
PeopleXD Payroll, and therefore do not have access its facility to bulk update salary records.
The file requires you to provide the following details:
• Personnel number
• Appointment ID
• The updated salary
• An effective date.

2.2. Contract Templates
You can also bulk amend employee contracts. This applies changes in the same way as creating individual contract amendments within an employee’s record in People Management.
Only contracts that are commenced, or confirmed future can be updated, and updates can’t be
made to fields specified on the Organisation Structure.
There is no default template for contract amendments; you can create your own custom
template. The template file will require users to supply the effective date, the list of fields to be
updated, and their new values. This allows you to create a template specific to the fields that
need updating, and once created the template can be re-used or deleted if no long relevant.
Note: Before processing this file, it’s recommended to co-ordinate with your Payroll team.
By default, the upload process will bypass your existing salary approval process. This can be
disabled when processing the file so that the records supplied on the file follow your existing
salary approval process. See Advanced Settings for further details.

1.2. What are Transfers?
1.2.1. HR Access In CoreHR, the hr administrator’s access to employees on the system is restricted based on their
designated HR Access. This HR Access is aligned to an Organisational Unit e.g. this may be set to:
• Company = ABC Solutions
• Department = Human Resources
• Division = Shared Services
Every employee on CoreHR will be assigned to at least one contract. That contract will specify the
Organisation Units that the employee’s position is aligned to e.g.
• Company = ABC Solutions
• Department = Human Resources
• Division = Shared Services
If the user has access to the Department e.g. Human Resources, then they will be able to see the
employee record and their contract in that department.
However, if the user doesn’t have access to the Department e.g. Finance, then they will not be able
to see the employee record and their contract in that department.

1.2.2. Transfer Requests
If a hr administrator does not have access to an employee on CoreHR but requires the ability to
transfer them into a new contract within their organisation, then they need to complete a ‘Transfer
Request’.
For example:
• John has one active contract in the Accounts department.

For example:
• John has one active contract in the Accounts department. • Mary is a hr administrator and only has access to employees in the HR and Payroll
departments.
• John will be moving to a new position with a new contract in the Payroll department.
However, Mary cannot complete the Replace Contract steps that are usually used to replace
one contract with a new contract, because she doesn’t have access to the employee on
CoreHR.
• Therefore, Mary must initiate a transfer request which will request for John to be:
▪ transferred out of their current contract i.e. in Accounts.
▪ transferred into a new proposed contract in their organisation i.e. in Payroll.
• Barry is a hr administrator with access to the Accounts department. He must approve /
reject this request, in order for Mary to be able to create the new replacement contract in
Payroll.
Further Considerations:
• The request will always be initiated by the user who does not have currently have access
to the employee on CoreHR and who needs to create the new contract.
• The request is never initiated by the person who already has access to the employee but
will not be creating the new contract

automatically links an employee to the company’s Job Seekers /

1. Introduction
The purpose of this guide is to provide instruction on how to make an employee a leaver on the system.
The purpose of making an employee a leaver on People Management is to ensure that the:
• employee record is dormant on the system from a given leave date.

still be active on the system i.e.
• where a contract is ended and replaced immediately by another contract.
• where an employee has multiple active contracts and only 1 contract will be ended.

how to complete these activities.

1.2. How are Salary Records Created?
A salary record is created for an employee against their Contract / Post Appointment.
• Salary records are not directly associated with the employee record.
• It is not possible to create a salary for the employee on People Management, independent
of their contract record.
If an employee has multiple active Contra cts / Post Appointments, then they will have multiple
active corresponding salary records.
Assigning a salary to a Post Appointment / Contract is a consistent activity. This implies that every
time a new contract is created for an employee, the hr administrator is required to input / confirm
the associated salary information i.e. for a new starter, new contract (replacement or additional)
or a rehire.
• Salary type and grade will be defined on the Post Profile.
• If using ‘Authorised Post Appointments’, plann ed salary details may be captured in full
including the amount and multiplier.
• Full salary details are updated / confirmed when the Post Appointment / Contract is
appointed to the employee.
• The salary will only be available to view on the employee’s record on People Management,
when the contract has been ‘Commenced’ for the employee.

1.4. HR Access vs Salary Access
Salary records are treated as sensitive data on CoreHR which means that there is an additional
level of data access required for a hr administrator to access salary records for an employee. This
means that it is possible for a hr administrator to have access to view the employee’s contracts but
not have access to view the corresponding salary record.
The ‘Pay Access’ is defined at a Pay Group level. This means that the user account will need to be
granted access to see all of the salaries for a given Pay Group

ess’ is defined at a Pay Group level. This means that the user account will need to be
granted access to see all of the salaries for a given Pay Group For example:
• An organisation has 2 Pay Groups – ‘Monthly Payroll’ and ‘Weekly Payroll’.
• Granting access to the ‘Monthly Payroll’ Pay Group ensures that the user will see salaries
for employees in that Pay Group.
• However, they will not see the salary for any employees in ‘Weekly Payroll’.
Having Pay Group access has no impact on the user’s ability to see employees or their contract

only, then:
• They will only be able to see the salaries for employees that are in the IT Department and
are on the Monthly Payroll.

1. Introduction
The purpose of this guide is to provide detailed guidance on how to set up a new hire on People
Management.
There are a number of ways in which a new hire can be setup on People Management, depending
on the posts that an organisation will use as the foundation for the employee’s contract. Therefore,

hire can be setup on People Management, depending

Appointment types:
• Auto-Authorised Post Profile
• Auto-Commenced Post Profile
• Planned & Authorised Post Appointment
Note:
This guide will not cover the steps required to create or manage Post Profiles as part of this process.
Please refer to the Managing Post Profiles user guide for this information.

When using an Auto Authorised Post Profile to create the contract, the contract will initially be
created in an appointed status. This means that:
• the employee exists on the system and will return as active if using the employee search
on the People Management dashboard.
• the contract exists for the employee and is available to view on their employee record with
a status of Pending.

not be available to the payroll team to process. The act of commencing the appointed contract on
a specified Commenced Date will confirm that the employee has started in organisation and should
be paid the contracted salary amount from that date.
Follow these steps to commence the contract:
1. Go to the Contracts screen on the employee record.
2. For a new hire, the employee record should default to display the on ly contract for the
employee. However, if in doubt, select the drop-down option to confirm that the correct
contract has been selected. The contract will be flagged as Pending.

2.2. Auto-Commenced Appointment
To create a new employee from an Auto -Commenced Post Profile, please follow the guidance
provided in 2.1 Auto Authorised Appointment . The process will be almost identical. The key
difference here is that, on completion of the 4-step Create New Employee wizard, the contract will
be created in a Commenced status i.e. there is no further requirement to Commence the
Appointment.
This means:
• The employee exists on the system and will return as active if using the employee search
on the People Management Dashboard.
• The contract exists for the employee and is available to view their HR Employee

ive if using the employee search
on the People Management Dashboard.
• The contract exists for the employee and is available to view their HR Employee Dashboard/Contract Timeline with a status of Commenced.
• The Effective Date recorded on step 2 of the Create New Employee wizard will be their Date
Commenced.
• The employee and the contract will be immediately available to payroll administration to
complete onboarding.
2.3. Non-Auto Post Profiles
Creating a new starter using a non-auto Post Profile means that the employee’s Contract/Post
Appointment will be created from a standard Post Profile that has not been flagged for Auto-
Authorisation or Auto-Commencement. When using these Post Profiles, the Post will not be
automatically available to the hr administrator to select via the People Management dashboard >
Add Person option.
Firstly, the HR administrator needs to go the People Management tab to complete the following two
steps:
• Plan Appointment
• Authorise Appointment

1.2. What is a notice period? From an employer’s perspective, a notice period is the length of time that is given to an employee
before their contract of employment can be terminated. Likewise, an employee must give their
employer notice if they intend to leave their position.
The primary aim behind employment notice periods is to provide both parties with an opportunity
to plan for the impact of the termination of a working relationship. Notice periods help minimise
business disruption and protect employers against the risks of a sudden departure by a key
employee.
Note: Notice periods will display by default on the Process as Leaver screen. This can be
hidden if it is not required by your organisation. See section 2.3 Notice Period Parameter for
further detail.

earliest possible Leave Date, based on the Notice Period rule configured for this employee.

purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Employee Onboarding functionality
in People Management and how this is used. This includes: • What is Employee Onboarding and when it used by employees?
• The difference between ‘new starter onboarding’ and ‘existing employee cross-boarding’.
• An overview of the Social Hub dashboard.
• Detailed guidance on the main elements of the Social Hub dashboard and how they may
be used.
• Tracking employee onboarding progress as a manager or hr administrator.
Employee Onboarding is highly configurable to ensure that every organisation can manage the
onboarding and cross-boarding experience based on their own requirements. This document does
not cover configuration guidance. For full training on how to set up and configure each element of
Employee Onboarding, see the Employee Onboarding v28: How to Configure - User Guide.
1.2. What is Employee Onboarding?
Employee Onboarding is a platform that supports onboarding guidance for new joiners and re-
joiners, while also supporting continuous onboarding guidance for existing employees. For
example:
• New starter onboarding for employees joining or re-joining the organisation.
• Cross-boarding for existing employees who move to new contracts, appointments, and/or
teams.
• The requirement to release new Checklist Items to existing employees.

for existing employees who move to new contracts, appointments, and/or
teams.
• The requirement to release new Checklist Items to existing employees. • A platform encouraging existing employees to engage with their wider team.
Employees can commence onboarding before the join the organisation i.e. before their start date
or rehire date. If this is the case, the employee will need a CorePortal account (to be created in the
same way as you generally issue CorePortal accounts). However, they will only have access to the
Social Hub until their start date has elapsed. They will not be able to access any other part of the
CorePortal e.g. Employee Dashboard won’t be available to them until they have started.:

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This document provides guidance on how the Delegation widget on the Manager Dashboard can be
used by managers to automatically reassign some of their org roles to colleagues. This includes:
• What is organisational role (org role) delegation?
• Who can delegate org roles?

1.2. What is Org Role Delegation?
Org r ole delegation is available to managers, to allow them to delegate their or g role
responsibilities to another manager, to cover periods where they are unavailable e.g. during leave.
This allows the manager to redirect approval items to their colleagues, without the need for HR to
intervene. The manager can control:
• Which of their org roles will be delegated.
• Who they will be delegated to.
• How long they will be delegated for.
• Why they are to be delegated.
HR can control what org roles can be delegated e.g. it may be suitable to delegate annual leave
approvals but not salary approvals.
Note: The following delegation items are not covered in this document:
• Team Area (for roster)
• Hourly Timesheet (payroll)
• Expense

that employees can be engaged on the system to:
• Receive alerts and notifications.
• Complete approvals.
• Receive and update tasks.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This guide is used to explain how to use the Payroll Instruction Forms via People Management. In
order to capture and automatically share pay -affecting information with Payroll, as part of the
joiner/mover/leaver processes e.g. holidays to be paid to a leaver, student loans for a new hire etc.
Within this User Guide you will learn how to:
• Create a custom form.
• Add a new HR task list item of Payroll Instructional Form.
• Assign a specific Org Role to this task.
• View & action the task on Pay Portal.
1.2. What is a Payroll Instructional Form?
A Payroll Instructional Form is a method of communication that is sent to Payroll directly from HR
in terms of details that are going to affect the employee’s payroll record once processed. Examples
of these items include:
1. Balance adjustments needed for holidays owed to an employee.
2. Outstanding student loan payments.
3. PAYE / Tax Code changes.
4. Holiday/Average Pay calculations.
5. Hours (i.e. Overtime).
6. Adhoc Payments (i.e. Bonuses & once off payments).
7. Pension changes.

1.1. Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to provide detailed guidance on how to configure pay scales in
PeopleXD.
This includes:
• An overview of what pay scales are.
• Where pay scales can be configured

1.2. What are Pay Scales
A pay scale/grade/position in conjunction with the scale point defines the amount of pay an
employee will receive. These scales are typically categorised based on factors such as job role,
experience, length of service, and level of responsibility.
There are three components of a pay scale:
• Pay Scale (also known as grade or position) - the pay scale the employee is on.
• Pay Scale Point - the points/levels available on the pay scale.
• Pay Scale Rates - the rate of pay associated with each scale point.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Note This guide is only applicable if an organisation is managing the assignment of pension schemes for employees at contract level, rather than person level. Please refer to the relevant
Payroll training resources for guidance on managing pension scheme assignments at employee
level.
This document provides guidance on how to manage pension schemes for employees by directly
assigning these to their contract records. This includes:
• Linking pension schemes to post profile records.
• Assigning a pension scheme to contracts.
• Amending existing pension scheme assignments.
• How the assignment of a pension scheme is ended.
• The payslip impact of the ‘Pension by Appointment’ option.
This document does not provide guidance on how to manage pensions schemes for employees at
employee level.
1.2. Pension by Appointment vs Pension by Person
CoreHR provides the facility to capture Pension Scheme assignment s for employee at either
Person or Appointment level. An organisation will configure the CoreHR application to manage
pensions using either of these options. Only one option can be enabled at a time. It is not possible
to define a combination of these options
1.2.1. Pension by Person
Pension Schemes are assigned directly to the employee’s record.
• This is managed in Payroll and not in HR.

1.2.1. Pension by Person
Pension Schemes are assigned directly to the employee’s record.
• This is managed in Payroll and not in HR. • This is completely independent of the employee’s assigned contracts i.e. contract
amendments, new contracts etc. will not impact on the pension scheme assignment.

Note If this option is used, the Pension Contributions screen will be read-only. This means
that the screen:
• will display the details of any pension assigned to the person.
• will not provide the ability to update or amend the pension assignments, regardless of
the menu options assigned to the user.
1.2.2. Pension by Appointment
Pension Schemes are assigned directly to an employee’s contract.
• Different pension schemes can be assigned to different contracts.
• If an employee has multiple active contracts, it is possible to have pension schemes
assigned to all or some of these.
• If a contract is ended, the pension scheme assignment is also automatically ended.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure CoreHR to manage the
creation or input of employee numbers on employee setup.
This includes:
• How to define automatic number generation rules.
• How to select either automatic number generation or manual number entry for new hires.

format requirements, including prefix, suffix and length.

setup on CoreHR.

1. Overview
The purpose of this document is to explain how users can use the Post Restructuring functionality
to change the organisation structure of the company. This might be to regroup existing business
into fewer units, or for the creation of additional business units.
1.1. What is a Restructuring Profile
This contains the details for the move, including the old and new Post structure, the effective date,
the employees that will be affected etc. You can have as many restructuring Profiles as you like ,
and a profile can be edited and saved until is used. It will be locked down once processed.
A new profile is required for every unique movement taking place, for example:
• If everyone in a Section is moving to a new Section, then one profile will be required.

equired for every unique movement taking place, for example:
• If everyone in a Section is moving to a new Section, then one profile will be required. • If half are moving to a new department , and the other half to another department , then
two profiles will be required.
Note: Post Restructuring will:
• update the employees existing Appointment, replacing their current post hierarchy
(Department, Section etc.) with the new post hierarchy specified.
• End the current sequence of that Appointment only and creates a new sequence. So it
will not create a new appointment_id.
• not affect the employee’s existing Salary or Allowances. These will carry on as normal.
Note:
• Post Restructuring must be carried out on UAT and signed off prior to running on Live
• Post Restructuring will only process the latest Commenced appointment. Before
restructuring, you must extract any Confirmed Future appointments and Delete them
from the system. These can be recreated if required once the restructure is complete.
• If an employee has an outstanding Salary Approval, this must be deleted and
recreated via a Salary Amendment if required.
• All New Reference data must be added on first. All Linking in the Hierarchy Tree must
be done prior to Running.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This document provides guidance on how assign probation expiry details to an employee on
People Management.
This includes:
▪ Updating the Probation Expiry Date.
▪ Capturing probation review dates.
▪ Recording details of a probation extension.
Probation dates and details are captured on CoreHR against the employee’s contract. Guidance is
provided on how to:
▪ Directly input dates on the employee’s contract.
▪ Automatically set dates using Terms and Conditions.
1.2. Contract Probation Periods
Probation details are captured at the Contract level in CoreHR and not at the Person level. This
means that it is possible to capture probation periods for any contracts held on CoreHR for the
employee i.e. initial new hire contract, promoted contracts, ad ditional contracts and rehire
contracts.
1.3. Using Terms and Conditions Profiles
Probation details may be directly input on the contract record by the HR administrator.

1.3. Using Terms and Conditions Profiles
Probation details may be directly input on the contract record by the HR administrator. It is also possible to configure a Terms and Conditions Profile to include a default Probation Period
e.g. 6 months. This may then be linked to a Post Profile and will ultimately be inherited by all Post
Appointments/Contracts created for that Post Profile. The system uses that Probationary Period
and the contract start date to calculate the actual Probation Expiry Date.

For example:
• T&C Profile defined Probation Period of “6 Months”.
• New hire contract start date is 1st January 2017.
• Contract Probation Expiry Date is calculated to 30th June 2017.
HR administrators will still have the ability to directly input or amend Probation Expiry Dates, even
if the Terms and Conditions Profiles are used.

1.2. What is Reference Data
Reference Data refers to the data that is available to select by end users of the system on the
various pick lists / drop-down lists throughout PeopleXD. This includes the following reference
data categories:
• Organisational Structure e.g. Company and Department
• Contract e.g. Employee status and reason code.
• Employee / Person e.g. Title and qualifications
PeopleXD provides a set of pre-configured Reference Data lists. These are reviewed and updated
during an implementation to ensure that the data is aligned to an organisation’s specific
requirements, for record and reporting purposes.
Reference Data may also be updated on the system during the live running to support changing
business needs e.g. add a new Job Title or Reason Code.

2. Manage Reference Data
The majority of reference data items are created, updated, or deleted using the same steps.

To add reference data:
1. Go to the relevant reference data screen.

3. Fill in the Code
4. Fill in the Description (Max 40 alphanumeric characters)
5. Amend any non standard fields and toggles.
6. Enable the Active toggle where applicable.
7. Click Save.

1. Introduction
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the ‘Salary Approval’ process in CoreHR
and how this controls the creation and management of the salary and allowance records for

1.2. What are Salary Approvals?
This feature ensures that whenever a new salary or allowance record is created (regardless of how
it is created), it must be specifically reviewed and signed off at a number of approval levels, before
becoming fully “Approved” and available to Payroll to process.
• Salaries are initially created in a status of “Pending”. This is not available to payroll to
process.
• During approval i.e. once approved by at least one approver but still awaiting other levels
of approval, the status will be “In Approval”. This is still not available to payroll to process.
• Only once the salary has been approved at all levels of approval, it will have a status of
“Approved”. If the effective date is greater than today it will have a status of “Future”. This
is now available to payroll to process.
• If a salary is rejected at any stage in the approval process, it will have a status of “Rejected”.
This will not be available to Payroll.
Salaries that have not been approved will be searchable in HR as “Pending”, “In Approval ” or
“Rejected” but these will not be visible to payroll.
Salary Approvals are not mandatory on CoreHR. It is possible to create salary amendments on the

r

Salary Approvals are not mandatory on CoreHR. It is possible to create salary amendments on the system that are automatically set to “Approved” and available to payroll to process. However, it is
strongly recommended to use this feature to apply an additio nal level of control to managing
employee salaries, in order to minimise the risk of incorrect or unapproved amendments
becoming available to Payroll and being processed.
Note: This document covers use of Salary Approvals in XD Portal only.

1.3. Salary Approval Options
There are 2 specific ways that Salary Approvals may be configured on CoreHR. A summary of these
options is available in this section. If using Salary Approvals, a decision must be made to use either
of these options. It is not possible to use both. Please refer to the corresponding configuration
guide for details on how to enable these options.
1.3.1. Standard Salary Approvals
This is the standard Salary Approval functionality. This typically requires a 2 -level approval
structure:
• Level 1: HR Approval
• Level 2: Payroll Approval
These levels are aligned to organisational or employee attributes on CoreHR e.g.
• HR Approval at Department Level.
• Payroll Approval and Pay Group Level.

levels are aligned to organisational or employee attributes on CoreHR e.g.
• HR Approval at Department Level.
• Payroll Approval and Pay Group Level. The approvers are assigned an organisational role for the required organisational level e.g.
• Mary has the Org Role of “HR Approver” for “IT Department”.
• John has the Org Role of “Payroll Approver” for the “Monthly Payroll” Pay Group.
Using the above example, if a new salary is created for Michael in the IT Department:
• Mary will first review this, and flag as “Approved” or “Rejected”.
• Only if this is first approved by HR, John will then review the salary and flag as “Approved”
or “Rejected”.
All salaries will be required to be approved at both levels in order to have a status of “Approved”
and be visible to Payroll.
It is possible to amend this default approval process to suit each organisation’s requirements e.g.
add new levels, revise the org role setup and level for each approval level. Details of how to amend
this are covered in the Configuring Salary Approvals user guide.

It is possible to define a bespoke approval process for salary amendments that will operate
completely separately to the ‘Default Salary Approval’ process.

possible to define a bespoke approval process for salary amendments that will operate

• The approval levels i.e. organisational or employee attributes.
It is possible to define more than o ne approval workflow if required. Each workflow may then be

It is also possible to exclude employees from any Salary Approval process i.e. identify employees

If using this option, it is important to ensure that that all employees are catered for in the workflow

1.1. Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how salary increments are managed on

1.2. What is the Increment Process?
This process is used to automatically create a new salary record for an employee , which moves
them to the next point on their pay scale.
This is applicable only to employees who have a “Pay Scale ” salary. Increments cannot
automatically be created for “Personal” rate salaries.
This process r emoves the requirement to manually create a salary a mendment for standard
annual / periodic salary increments:
• This can happen for all / a group of employees in an organisation on one common date in
a year.
• This may be applied on a date specific to the employee’s Post Appointment e.g. 12 months
from the Commenced Date, or on turning 18 etc.
It is typical to define a set number of days in advance to process the increment due date e.g. 30
days. This means that when the process runs each day, it will look for any Increment Due Dates in
the next 30 days and create the required salary amendment.
For example:
• On 1st August 2015, Mary was setup as a new hire and her salary was created on that date
as Point 1 of Grade 5 i.e. £35,000

1.2. What are HR Process Task Lists?
Task Lists are used to define a set of steps that must be completed as part of a New Starter, New
Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire or Leaver process.
Once a new contract has been assigned to an employee as part of the ne w hire, rehire or new
contract steps on People Management, the task list pops up on screen. This presents the user with
a list of mandatory steps to be comp leted. The user can then click on a step and be redirected to
the screen required to input the data e.g. if the step is ‘Allowances’, clicking on this opens the ‘Add
Allowances’ screen.
Different task lists can be created for each process type.
The advantage of using the task list feature includes:
• Ability to direct the user to ensure the required employee and contract details are updated.
• One central location is provided to allow the user to jump directly to the required screens
to update the data.
• The task list can be closed and reopened as many times as necessary before completion.

1.2. What are Terms and Conditions Profiles?
Terms and Conditions (T&C) Profiles are templates of contracted terms and conditions that can be
associated with Posts and Contracts.
Rules can be defined as to when a profile is relevant to a Post Profile e.g. based on status, location
etc.
The following contract elements can be defined:
• Probation Expiry
• Employee and Employer Notice Periods
• Increment Due Date and Hold Indicator
• Allowances
• Balances
1.3. How are T&C Profiles Assigned to Contracts?
Once a T&C Profile is defined on CoreHR, it must be linked to a Post Profile.
Once the template is linked to the Post, the T&Cs can be further updated to be more specific to
the chosen Post.

1.2. What are User Defined Fields?
1.2.1. UDFs Explained User Defined Fields (UDFs) are used to hold data where the system doesn’t provide this as
standard. These would typically be items that are specific to an individual organisation and will
differ from company to company.
For example, a company may wish to store a record of standard company equipment that has
been given to an employee. This can be cap tured in a UDF that is configured to display the exact
equipment list specific to that company.
UDFs can be created against:
• An employee
• A post
• A contract
XD People Management: User Defined Field (UDF) Configuration – User Guide

UDFs may be configured using the following elements:
• Up to 12 standard fields:
o Text
o Number
o List
o Date
o Text Area
• Start Date & End Date
There is no limit to the amount of UDFs that can be configured.
1.2.2. Access to UDFs
UDFs are configured via the People Management dashboard. UDFs are available as standard to all
HR administrators via People Management. However, for each UDF created, it is possible to define
if managers and employees should also see it.

The purpose of this document is to provide detailed guidance on the ‘Wage Warnings’ feature

1.2. How do the Wage Warnings Work?
1.2.1. What are Wage Warnings?
PeopleXD provides an option to validate the rate entered for an employee’s salary, against
minimum, living and / or apprentice wage rates. This is to inform the user if the salary they
are providing for the employee’s contract is too low.
Rates for minimum wage, living wages and apprentice wages can be setup on PeopleXD (see

ary they
are providing for the employee’s contract is too low.
Rates for minimum wage, living wages and apprentice wages can be setup on PeopleXD (see 2. Configuring the Rates). These can be added to on an annual basis, as new rates are
released for each new tax year.
PeopleXD will calculate if the salary supplied for an employee’s contract meets the minimum
/ living / apprentice wage rates based on:
• The rates defined on PeopleXD and their effective date.
• The employee’s date of birth.
• Contracted hours and weeks (or FTE Weeks per Year).

• Where multiple countries are setup, the appropriate rates for the employee’s Pay

Minimum wage & apprentice rates are not mutually exclusive. The system will first check to
see if the employee’s contract is an apprentice type contract.
• If it is - apprentice rates are used in validation.
• If it isn’t - minimum wage rates are used in validation

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure and manage Additional
Superannuation Contributions (ASC) in Payroll.
1.2. What is Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC)?

1.2. What is Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC)? Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC) came into effect on 01st January 2019, replacing the
Pension Related Deduction (PRD).
The ASC is a deduction from the remuneration of public servants to fund existing pension benefits.
No additional pension benefit accrues from this deduction. While PRD was a temporary measure,
ASC is a permanent contribution.
Unlike PRD, ASC is only chargeable on pensionable remuneration. Pensionable remuneration
includes:
• Basic Pay (excluding non-pensionable overtime) due to the public servant in respect of that
period, and
• Allowances, emoluments and premium pay (o r it's equivalent) which are treated as
pensionable pay.
1.3. Who is Liable to pay ASC?
ASC is a deduction from the pensionable pay of a public servant employed by a public service
employer.
ASC applies to individuals who receive pensionable pay and meet any of the following criteria:
• is a member of a public service pension scheme.
• receives a payment in lieu of membership in such a scheme.
• is entitled to an ex-gratia retirement gratuity (annual or lump sum) on retirement.
Note:
Employees who are retained in a non -pensionable position under Department of Public

tia retirement gratuity (annual or lump sum) on retirement.
Note:
Employees who are retained in a non -pensionable position under Department of Public Expenditure and Reform Circular 21/2017 etc. are not be liable for ASC.

1.5. Calculating ASC
1.5.1. When is ASC Calculated?
ASC is calculated and deducted from the gross pay before calculating income tax. ASC is a statutory
deduction and takes priority over any non-statutory or voluntary deductions.
Gross Pensionable Remuneration:
• ASC only applies to pensionable remuneration. This m eans that non -pensionable
allowances and non-pensionable overtime are not subject to ASC.
• ASC appl ies to all pensionable remuneration , whether taxable or otherwise. Th erefore,
non-taxable, pensionable allowances and payments are liable for ASC.
The following are not liable for ASC:
• Benefits in Kind.
• Non-pensionable payments, such as the reimbursement of expenses.
• Statutory Redundancy.
• Termination payments, whether taxable or non-taxable.
Salary Sacrifice

• Statutory Redundancy.
• Termination payments, whether taxable or non-taxable.
Salary Sacrifice Salary sacrifices, such as travel pass or bike to work, can be deducted from pensionable pay
before calculating ASC.
Enable the ASCable indicator on salary sacrifice pay codes to ensure ASC calculates on the
reduced payment value.
Multiple Employments:
Where an employee has multiple public-sector employments, pensionable remuneration is
calculated as the combined pensionable remuneration from each employment

1.5.2. How is ASC Calculated?
ASC is calculated on all pensionable payments. Including, wages or salary, arrears, pensionable
allowances, holiday pay, maternity pay, paternity pay, occupational sick pay, etc.
ASC is calculated on an employee's pensionable pay as reduced by any approved salary sacrifice
but before deductions for pension contributions, AVCs, PAYE, PRSI and USC.
Tax relief is allowed on ASC at the employee's marginal rate , i.e. ASC is deducted from an
employee's gross pay befor e calculating Income Tax. ASC does not qualify for employee PRSI or
USC relief but qualifies for full employer PRSI relief.

When a grossing up payment is processed, Payroll calculates the correct amount to gross up.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure and manage Additional
Superannuation Contributions (ASC) in Payroll.
1.2. What is Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC)?
