1.2. What is Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC)? Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC) came into effect on 01st January 2019, replacing the
Pension Related Deduction (PRD).
The ASC is a deduction from the remuneration of public servants to fund existing pension benefits.
No additional pension benefit accrues from this deduction. While PRD was a temporary measure,
ASC is a permanent contribution.
Unlike PRD, ASC is only chargeable on pensionable remuneration. Pensionable remuneration
includes:
• Basic Pay (excluding non-pensionable overtime) due to the public servant in respect of
that period, and
• Allowances, emoluments, and premium pay (or its equivalent) which are treated as
pensionable pay.
1.3. Who is Liable to pay ASC?
ASC is a deduction from the pensionable pay of a public servant employed by a public service
employer.
ASC applies to individuals who receive pensionable pay and meet any of the following criteria:
• is a member of a public service pension scheme.
• receives a payment in lieu of membership in such a scheme.
• is entitled to an ex-gratia retirement gratuity (annual or lump sum) on retirement.
Note:
Employees who are retained in a non -pensionable position under Department of Public
Expenditure and Reform Circular 21/2017 etc. are not liable for ASC.

1.5. Calculating ASC
1.5.1. When is ASC Calculated?
ASC is calculated and deducted from the gross pay before calculating income tax. ASC is a statutory
deduction and takes priority over any non-statutory or voluntary deductions.
Gross Pensionable Remuneration:
• ASC only applies to pensionable remuneration. This means that non -pensionable
allowances and non-pensionable overtime are not subject to ASC.
• ASC appl ies to all pensionable remuneration , whether taxable or otherwise. Th erefore,
non-taxable, pensionable allowances and payments are liable for ASC.
The following are not liable for ASC:
• Benefits in Kind.
• Non-pensionable payments, such as the reimbursement of expenses.
• Statutory Redundancy.
• Termination payments, whether taxable or non-taxable.

1.5.2. How is ASC Calculated?
ASC is calculated on all pensionable payments. Includin g, wages or salary, arrears, pensionable
allowances, holiday pay, maternity pay, paternity pay, occupational sick pay, etc.
ASC is calculated on an employee's pensionable pay as reduced by any approved salary sacrifice
but before deductions for pension contributions, AVCs, PAYE, PRSI and USC.
Tax relief is allowed on ASC at the employee's marginal rate, i.e., ASC is deducted from a n
employee's gross pay before calculating Income Tax. ASC does not qualify for employee PRSI or
USC relief but qualifies for full employer PRSI relief.

2.7.1. Change of ASC Status Mid-Year
As ASC is a cumulative calculation, a change of status mid-year results in a recalculation.

One basis. To do this, see Setting ASC to Week 1.
2.7.2. Part-Time PRSI & Irregular Claims
Part-Time PRSI and Irregular Claims software cater to ASC. The key change is that, as ASC is on a
when paid basis, the ASC calculation is always for the current period.
2.7.3. Grossing Up
When a grossing up payment is processed, Payroll calculates the correct amount to gross up.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of This Guide
This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for implementing and managing Ireland's
Auto Enrolment (AE) pension system within PeopleXD Payroll.
1.2. Who Should Use This Guide
This guide is designed for:
• Payroll Administrators – responsible for processing payroll and managing employee
pension deductions
• HR Professionals – overseeing employee benefits and pension scheme administration
• System Configurators – setting up and maintaining PeopleXD system parameters
• Compliance Officers – ensuring adherence to NAERSA and Department of Social

3.5.2. Common Questions
Q: Do I need to retrieve AEPNs if all my employees are already in a company pension?
A: Yes. The Department requires all employers to call AEPNs before every payroll run, even if you
expect zero enrolments. If the call returns "no records found," you can proceed normally without
submitting a contribution file.
Q: What if I have multiple pay groups with different frequencies?
A: Retrieve AEPNs every time you process a payroll. For example:
• Retrieve AEPNs for weekly staff every week
• Retrieve AEPNs for monthly staff every month
• Submit separate contribution files for each pay group
Q: Can I test the API connection before going live?
A: No. NAERSA does not provide a test environment due to GDPR restrictions. All API calls
connect to the live production system. However, PeopleXD prevents you from transferring
contribution files from non-production environments to avoid accidental submissions.

3.5.2. Common Questions
Q: Do I need to retrieve AEPNs if all my employees are already in a company pension?
A: Yes. The Department requires all employers to call AEPNs before every payroll run, even if you
expect zero enrolments. If the call returns "no records found," you can proceed normally without
submitting a contribution file.
Q: What if I have multiple pay groups with different frequencies?
A: Retrieve AEPNs every time you process a payroll. For example:
• Retrieve AEPNs for weekly staff every week
• Retrieve AEPNs for monthly staff every month
• Submit separate contribution files for each pay group
Q: Can I test the API connection before going live?
A: No. NAERSA does not provide a test environment due to GDPR restrictions. All API calls
connect to the live production system. However, PeopleXD prevents you from transferring
contribution files from non-production environments to avoid accidental submissions.

1.4. What is a CSO EHECS Return?
The CSO EHECS Return is a survey that produces an index of labour costs per hour worked. The survey requires collecting wages & salaries, employers' social contributions, other non-wage costs,
and hours worked.
All E.U. member states are obliged to compile Labour Cost indices. They provide vital information
for future social and economic planning, such as wage agreements, etc.
Each quarter, employers receive a questionnaire relating to the number of people employed in
their business during that quarter. Each employee is categorised into one of the following three
occupational groups:
1. Managers, Administrators, Professionals & Associate Professional (Legislators and senior
officials, corporate managers, managers of small enterprises, professionals, and
associate professionals)
2. Clerical, Sales & Service Workers (Clerks, office workers, service & sales workers).
3. Production, Transport Workers, Craft & Tradespersons and Other Manual Workers (Plant &
machine operators & assemblers, skilled craft & trade workers, and other manual
occupations)
Employers need to provide the total labour costs, the total hours worked, and the total hours not
worked (e.g., annual leave) for each employee category. Enterprises with small numbers employed
are only required to send data for a set number of quarters.

2.1. Central Business Register
Current System
• Some enterprises return more than one CSO EHECS Return to the CSO . This is primarily to
facilitate a separate return for Executive staff or payrolls split across different payroll systems.
• Up to now, "dummy" enterprises were set up on the CSO system, with a different enterprise
ID, and surveyed as if they were a separate enterprise.
• Enterprises are identified using a Company Business Registration ( CBR) number. The CBR
number is the unique permanent identifier assigned to each enterprise .
New System
Following E.U. best practice, the CSO has now implemented a new Central Business Register (CBR).
The new CBR requires enterprises to make the following changes :
• From Quarter 2, 2021, the CBR can no longer facilitate “dummy” enterprise ID ’s. This means
that all CSO EHECS Returns for an enterprise now need to use the same enterprise ID.
• To support this change, the CSO are introducing the ability to complete a second EHECS survey.
This is referred to as a “Supplementary Survey” and will be returned using the same enterprise

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to set up and maintain CSO reference
data in Payroll.
1.2. What is a CSO EHECS Return?
The CSO Earnings, Hours and Employment Costs Survey (EHECS) is a survey that produces an index
of labour costs per hour worked. The survey require s collecting wages & salaries, employers ’ social
contributions, other non-wage costs, and hours worked.
All E.U. member states are obliged to compile Labour Cost indices. They provide vital inf ormation for
future social and economic planning, such as wage agreements, etc.
Each quarter, employers receive a questionnaire relating to the number of people employed in their
business during that quarter. Each employee is categorised into one of the following three occupational
groups:
1. Managers, Administrators, Professionals & Associate Professional (Legislators and senior
officials, corporate managers, managers of small enterprises, professionals, and associate
professionals)
2. Clerical, Sales & Service Workers (Clerks, office workers, service & sales workers)

small enterprises, professionals, and associate
professionals)
2. Clerical, Sales & Service Workers (Clerks, office workers, service & sales workers) 3. Production, Transport Workers, Craft & Tradespersons and Other Manual Workers (Plant &
machine operators & assemblers, skilled craft & trade workers, and other manual
occupations)
Employers need to provide the total labour costs, the total hours worked, and the total hours not worked
(e.g. annual leave) for each employee category. Enterprises with small numbers employed are only
required to send data for a set number of quarters.

employee payments to Revenue on or before each payday . This reporting requirement is

expense group then assuming it contains relevant payment items, the weekly expense group
payment information must be returned to Revenue on or before each weekly payment that
employees receive.

2.1.2. What are the Submission Files? At the end of every payroll, transmit an Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) Submission File
to report the latest payment information to Revenue. This transfers through an automated feed
that connects seamlessly with Revenue to exchange the required information.
A key feature of the ERR Submission File is that it reports ‘this period only’ values to Revenue. From
these periodic values, Revenue accumulates the totals from each periodic submission, thus
removing the requirement for an end of year submission.
A ERR Submission File should be generated:
• Every payroll run, where there is a relevant payment made during the run. If no relevant
payment has been made then no file needs to be generated/transferred.
• After the Complete Update task.
• On or before the payment date.

2.1.2. What are the Submission Files? At the end of every payroll, transmit an Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) Submission File
to report the latest payment information to Revenue. This transfers through an automated feed
that connects seamlessly with Revenue to exchange the required information.
A key feature of the ERR Submission File is that it reports ‘this period only’ values to Revenue. From
these periodic values, Revenue accumulates the totals from each periodic submission, thus
removing the requirement for an end of year submission.
A ERR Submission File should be generated:
• Every payroll run, where there is a relevant payment made during the run. If no relevant
payment has been made then no file needs to be generated/transferred.
• After the Complete Update task.
• On or before the payment date.

3.1.2. What is the Transfer Submission File Process?
At the end of every payroll , where ERR qualifying payments are paid, you need to directly report
the latest ERR details to Revenue. This is done by transferring the ERR Submission File to Revenue
from within the PeopleXD application.
Revenue validates the file, and if they find any issues, they notify this to Payroll via the Submission
Status and provide a report of any exceptions. Should any errors be found, these need to be
resolved in PeopleXD; a new Normal Submission file generated and transferred again to Revenue.
This submission file includes only the records that changed e.g.
• 1st Normal Submission only 8/10 records completed successfully.
• 2nd Normal Submission only includes 2/2 records, i.e. the two records that were invalid on
the previous submission.

2.1. When ERR is required
What payments are included in ERR Phase 1?
ERR Phase 1 includes the following three types of payments:
1. €3.20 remote working allowance: Revenue operates an administrative practice which
allows an employer to make payments up to €3.20 to employees, for each day worked
from home, subject to certain conditions being satisfied, without the need to deduct PAYE,
PRSI or USC. Guidance for this measure is available in Tax and Duty Manual (TDM) Part 05-
02-13 Remote Working Relief.
2. Travel and subsistence payments: Where an office holder or employee, in the
performance of the duties of his/her office or employment, incurs expenses of travel and
subsistence, such amounts can, subject to conditions, be reimbursed without deduction of
PAYE, PRSI and USC. Guidance for th is measure is available in TDM Part 05 -01-06 Tax
treatment of the reimbursement of expenses of travel and subsistence to office holders
and employees .

measure is available in TDM Part 05 -01-06 Tax
treatment of the reimbursement of expenses of travel and subsistence to office holders
and employees . 3. The small benefit exemption: The small benefit exemption provides that employers may
make tax-free benefits to employees in the form of vouchers or other benefits within the
remit of section 112B TCA 1997. Guidance on this measure is available in TDM Part 05-01-
01e -The small benefit exemption .
If benefits are paid by company credit card is it correct that we don’t have to file an ERR
return?
Yes, Revenue have clarified that there is no requirement to file an ERR where benefits are paid via
Company Credit card. This is as the employee is not being directly reimbursed.

ERR is the reporting of non-taxable benefit payments. As such taxable expense payments would
not be reported. If payments were reported incorrectly then a cancel/manual payment would be

3.3.5. Reference Period
The holiday pay regulations set out that, the holiday pay reference period should start from the
last complete working week that was worked, ending on or before the first day of leave, starting
on a Sunday and ending on a Saturday.
There is an exception for workers whose pay is calculated weekly by a week ending on a day
other than Saturday. In such cases, a week is treated as ending with that other day. For example,

e pay is calculated weekly by a week ending on a day
other than Saturday. In such cases, a week is treated as ending with that other day. For example, if a worker’s pay is calculated by a week ending with a Wednesday, then the employer should
treat a week as starting on a Thursday and finishing on a Wednesday.
For all other pay frequencies, the holiday pay must be broken down on a weekly basis where a
week is defined as starting on a Sunday and ends on a Saturday.
Within the system
• The annual leave transaction date determines when the Annual leave day is for.
• The system then looks at the pay group frequency.
• If the pay group is weekly the system uses the week as defined for that pay group when
calculating the historical average pay
• For any other pay group frequency, the system will identify the transaction date for the
annual leave claim and check what the previous holiday pay week (Sunday-Saturday) was
and count back from there to identify the relevant 52 weeks to use when calculating the
average pay.

1.2. Irish Statutory Sick Pay
1.2.1. SSP Requirements
• Sick pay will be paid by employers at a rate of 70% of an employee’s wage, subject to a

1.2. Irish Statutory Sick Pay
1.2.1. SSP Requirements
• Sick pay will be paid by employers at a rate of 70% of an employee’s wage, subject to a daily threshold of €110 which is based on 2019 mean weekly earnings of €786.33 which
equates to an annual salary of €40,889.16 (weekly salary of €786.33 divided by 5 days
multiplied by 70% = €110.08).
• It will start with three days payable per year in 2023. Only certified sick days are eligible
for SSP.
• The entitlement for payment of sick pay is subject to the employee having worked for their
employer for a minimum of 13 weeks.
• Once entitlement to sick pay from their employer ends, employees who need to take more
time off may qualify for illness benefit from the Department of Social Protection subject to
PRSI contributions.
• The legislation does not prevent employers offering better terms or unions negotiating for
more through a collective agreement.

2. SSP Eligibility
The following eligibility checks must be passed for the system to deem an employee eligible for
SSP.
• Employee Service
An Employee must have a minimum of 13 weeks continuous service. The system checks
for the first match of an employees:
o TUPE Date - if the Enable TUPE Date parameter is enabled
o Latest Start Date
o Employee Start Date

for the first match of an employees:

o Latest Start Date
o Employee Start Date
• SSP Days o An employee is eligible for up to 3 SSP days per calendar year.
o From day 4 no SSP will be paid.
• Duplicate Claim
o SSP can only be claimed once for a transaction date.
o If a record is created with a transaction date where SSP has already been paid the
system will not pay SSP again.
• Pre 1st January 2023 Records
o SSP cannot be claimed pre 1st January 2023.
o If a SSP transaction date is before 1st January 2023 SSP will not be paid.
• SSP Override

calculation is made.

Certified SSP can be recorded in People Management, WFM or Payroll. It is the recording of

Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) has no basis or instruction from Revenue around how to link SSP claims to
previous illnesses. This is important as it means that each sick record is treated as a separate illness
which means that rolling into a new tax year will result in SSP being paid for the first number of

t each sick record is treated as a separate illness
which means that rolling into a new tax year will result in SSP being paid for the first number of SSP days claimed within that tax year for sick days recorded, up to the allowed max number of SSP
days for that tax year.
• PeopleXD operates based on the transaction date, making it clear whether the illness falls
within the previous or current tax year.
o If the transaction date is from the previous year, it will be treated as last year's
sickness, and if it falls within the current year, it will be considered for the ongoing
tax year.
• Therefore, each new tax year will see SSP paid for new illnesses recorded, up to the allowed
number of SSP days for that specific tax year.
• To get around this there is the flexibility to record timesheets to adjust or override the
system if you wish to prevent SSP being paid in a new tax year.

employee’s rostered hours.
• Daily Rate (2 d.p.) = Hourly Rate * Rostered Hours
3. SSP is calculated using the Daily Rate figure.

3.2. SSP Calculation Task
Once a sickness absence is recorded using certified sick Pay Codes SSP will be calculated when the
Payroll Validation task is run as part of the Payroll Process.
The SSP calculation task completes the following:
1. Calculates the number of SSP days.
2. Calculates a daily rate of payment based on an employee’s category:
a. Category A (Salary Employees)
b. Category B (Paid by Timesheet Employees)
c. Category C (User Defined Rule Employees)
3. Calculates the SSP Payment Total.
4. Compares the total to the daily payment cap.
5. Creates an SSP timesheet.
3.2.1. SSP Days Calculation
An employee is eligible for up to 3 SSP days. The system will calculate how many SSP days the
sickness record contains and compare to the total number of SSP days the employee has taken in
the calendar year.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the year end for 2024 and
prepare for the 2025 tax year. This document covers the following:
• Legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget.
• Software changes introduced as part of the year end delivery.
• Tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.
• Tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task.
• Steps required to configure your system correctly for the 2025 tax year.
1.2. What is Year End?
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks:
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the company into a new tax year.
• Resets the employees' cumulative figures.
• Moves the employees ' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the End of Year
table.
• Creates a new payroll company calendar for the next two years.
The year end software delivery provides our customers with the following:
• Preloaded rate changes as outlined in the Budget.

The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the year end for 2023 and

• Resets the employees' cumulative figures.
• Moves the employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the End of Year
table.
• Creates a new payroll company calendar for the next two years.

1.2. What is LGPS?
The LGPS is a public service pension scheme and its rules are made with the approval of
Parliament. The Scheme is administered locally by pension funds across the country who make
decisions about your pension. Those pension funds decide how pension contributions are
invested. A Local Pension Board helps each pension fund administer the LGPS and comply with
the Scheme rules. For further details on LGPS rules and regulations, please see
https://www.lgpsregs.org/
1.3. LGPS in PeopleXD Payroll

separately on the monthly and annual return.

on the LPGS return then to facilitate this you would need to hold any additional contract
payments as allowances on the employees Substantive/main contract.
In Payroll the LPGS solution pensions are processed at post & appointment level. This meets the
LPGS requirements where for the new scheme different employee contribution rates can be in
force for different jobs. In addition, an employee could be in the main scheme for one job and

5. FTE Calculations
5.1. Overview
This section outlines the four distinct calculation methods, and the associated rules used to
determine an employee’s Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) salary for pension purposes by appointment.
These methods ensure accurate salary calculations based on different employment scenarios.
5.1.1. Calculation Methods
The following calculation methods are:
1. LGPS Hourly Paid – Used for employees paid on an hourly basis, where FTE salary
calculations are derived directly from hourly rates.
2. LGPS Hourly Paid Average – Determines the FTE salary based on an average hourly rate
over a defined period.
3. LGPS Salary Paid – Applied to employees with a fixed salary, ensuring pension
calculations align with contracted pay.
4. LGPS Salary Paid with Average Hours – Calculates the FTE salary by incorporating average
hours worked over a specified period.
Each employee’s pension record stores the applicable calculation method for their relevant
appointment.
5.2. Calculation Pay Codes

exclusion from the relevant calculation method.

salary.

1.2. About SEPA Changes (ISO20022)
The SEPA (ISO 20022) schema changes are being introduced as part of a European Directive
aimed at enhancing payment processing across Europe. These changes, originally set to become
mandatory from October/November 2025, are designed to facilitate instant and more
efficient payments, benefiting both businesses and individuals.
In November 2024, the European Payments Council (EPC) announced a change to the
implementation timeline:
• The adoption of ISO 20022 messaging remains mandatory from October 2025.
• However, the structured address requirement has been delayed to November 2026
to give organizations more time to comply.
Employers should consult their banks to determine whether early adoption of structured
address reporting is recommended.
New SEPA Method Portal - User Guide

The October 2025 vs. November 2026 deadlines for SEPA ISO 20022 changes are due to
different regulatory and implementation timelines:
1. October 2025 Deadline
• This is the general deadline for the adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging
format for SEPA credit transfers and direct debits.

. October 2025 Deadline
• This is the general deadline for the adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging
format for SEPA credit transfers and direct debits. • It is set by the European Payments Council (EPC) and applies to all SEPA
participants, including banks, payment service providers, and businesses
processing SEPA payments.
• By this date, organizations must ensure their systems are compatible with the
new format.
2. November 2026 Deadline
• This is a separate deadline specifically for the structured address reporting
requirement.
• Initially, this requirement was part of the October 2025 changes, but it has
been delayed by the EPC to November 2026 to give businesses and banks
more time to adapt.
• Most banks, however, recommend implementing structured addresses
alongside the October 2025 migration to avoid additional system changes
later.
Note:
It is critical that you have a conversation with your Bank regarding their plans for supporting
ISO20022 and what they recommend you do.

2.4. Local Instrument Code
2.4.1. Overview
In SEPA ISO20022 payment messages, the Local Instrument Code specifies the type of payment
instrument being used for a transaction. This code defines how the payment should be
processed, including any specific rules or formats that apply in different count ries or for various
transaction types.
The Local Instrument Code ensures that:
• Processing Rules: Payments adhere to country-specific regulations.
• Payment Types: Different payment instruments, such as credit transfers or instant
payments, are correctly handled.
Location in XML Messages
The Local Instrument Code is included in the payment instruction under the <PmtTpInf>
(Payment Type Information) element. It is typically represented as follows:
Example XML Structure:
<PmtTpInf>
<LclInstrm>
<Cd>INST</Cd>
</LclInstrm>
</PmtTpInf>
• <Cd> Element: Represents the code for the local instrument.
• INST: Indicates instant payments as per the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst)
scheme.
Purpose
The specific Local Instrument Code used depends on the payment method and applicable
country regulations. It enables banks and payment systems to:
• Correctly interpret the payment.

1.2. About SEPA Changes (ISO20022)
The SEPA (ISO 20022) schema changes are being introduced as part of a European Directive
aimed at enhancing payment processing across Europe. These changes, originally set to become
mandatory from October/November 2025, are designed to facilitate instant and more
efficient payments, benefiting both businesses and individuals.
In November 2024, the European Payments Council (EPC) announced a change to the
implementation timeline:
• The adoption of ISO 20022 messaging remains mandatory from October 2025.
• However, the structured address requirement has been delayed to November 2026
to give organizations more time to comply.
Employers should consult their banks to determine whether early adoption of structured
address reporting is recommended.

The October 2025 vs. November 2026 deadlines for SEPA ISO 20022 changes are due to
different regulatory and implementation timelines:
1. October 2025 Deadline
• This is the general deadline for the adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging
format for SEPA credit transfers and direct debits.

. October 2025 Deadline
• This is the general deadline for the adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging
format for SEPA credit transfers and direct debits. • It is set by the European Payments Council (EPC) and applies to all SEPA
participants, including banks, payment service providers, and businesses
processing SEPA payments.
• By this date, organizations must ensure their systems are compatible with the
new format.
2. November 2026 Deadline
• This is a separate deadline specifically for the structured address reporting
requirement.
• Initially, this requirement was part of the October 2025 changes, but it has
been delayed by the EPC to November 2026 to give businesses and banks
more time to adapt.
• Most banks, however, recommend implementing structured addresses
alongside the October 2025 migration to avoid additional system changes
later.
Note:
It is critical that you have a conversation with your Bank regarding their plans for supporting
ISO20022 and what they recommend you do.

2.4. Local Instrument Code
2.4.1. Overview
In SEPA ISO20022 payment messages, the Local Instrument Code specifies the type of payment
instrument being used for a transaction. This code defines how the payment should be
processed, including any specific rules or formats that apply in different count ries or for various
transaction types.
The Local Instrument Code ensures that:
• Processing Rules: Payments adhere to country-specific regulations.
• Payment Types: Different payment instruments, such as credit transfers or instant
payments, are correctly handled.
Location in XML Messages
The Local Instrument Code is included in the payment instruction under the <PmtTpInf>
(Payment Type Information) element. It is typically represented as follows:
Example XML Structure:
<PmtTpInf>
<LclInstrm>
<Cd>INST</Cd>
</LclInstrm>
</PmtTpInf>
• <Cd> Element: Represents the code for the local instrument.
• INST: Indicates instant payments as per the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst)
scheme.
Purpose
The specific Local Instrument Code used depends on the payment method and applicable
country regulations. It enables banks and payment systems to:
• Correctly interpret the payment.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on processing the P11D for Employees’
expenses and benefits. This includes:
• Loading P11D data.
• Compiling P11D data.
• Create and Maintain P11D data.
• Producing P11Ds and P11D(B)s – paper-based and XML file.
• P11Ds on Portal.
1.2. What is a P11D?
A P11D is a statutory form sent to HMRC by UK employers outlining the following:
• The Cash Equivalent Value of any Taxable Benefits Employees received over the tax year
– a P11D may include benefits paid for through a salary sacrifice arrangement.
• Expenses paid for by an Employee which are reimbursed by the Company – exclude
Exempt Expenses.
1.2.1. Expenses Covered by an Exemption
You don’t have to report certain Business Expenses, which are:
• Wholly, exclusively, and necessarily incurred by Employees in the performance of their
duties – the Employee must incur a cost and keep receipts.
• Calculated and paid in an approved way (actual or scale rate).

n the performance of their
duties – the Employee must incur a cost and keep receipts.
• Calculated and paid in an approved way (actual or scale rate). There must be a system in place for checking the Expenses incurred.
Note:
HMRC amend Employees’ Tax Codes to account for the Income Tax due and issue updated
coding notices.
P11D - Configuration and User Guide

Examples of some Expenses that may not have to be included on a P11D are:
• Business travel.
• Phone bills.
• Business entertainment.
• Uniform and tools for work.
To qualify for an exemption, you must be either:
• Paying a flat rate to your Employee as part of their earnings – this must be either a
benchmark rate or a special (‘bespoke’) rate approved by HMRC.
• Paying back the Employees’ actual costs.
1.2.2. Deadline for filing P11D’s
A P11D should be submitted to HMRC and provided to your Employees by 06th July following the
end of the tax year – if you choose not to provide a P11D to your Employees, they should be
made aware of what information was returned.
P11D Internet submissions drop -dead timestamp is 06 July 23:59:59 as defined by the HMRC
gateway. There is no deviation from this.

1.3. What is a P11D(B)?
This form tells HMRC the number of Taxable Benefits and the amount of Class 1A National
Insurance due. Note the following: • If a benefit is subject to PAYE, Class 1A National Insurance is payable.
• Class 1A National Insurance is an employer only liability.
• If no tax is due on a benefit, Class 1A National Insurance is not payable.
• Class 1A National Insurance is set percentage of your taxable benefit total.
Note:
You must deduct and pay tax and NI on all other Expenses you give to your Employees,
and report them to HMRC as normal.

Types of benefits that attract Class 1A National Insurance include:
• Private medical insurance provided to an Employee.
• Assets transferred to an Employee.
• Company cars.
• Beneficial loans.
• Relocation expenses.
1.3.1. Deadline for filing P11D(B)’s
P11D(B)s needs to be submitted to HMRC by 22nd July following the end of the tax year.

6.1. What is Payrolling Benefits?
Payrolling Benefits allow employers to account for the tax on benefits provided to Employees
through the PAYE system, by adding notional pay to the Employees’ taxable income.
Note the following:
• Payrolled benefits are often referred to as Benefits in Kind (BIK).
• If intending to Payroll Benefits (including Vehicle BIK), then you must register your intention
to do so with HMRC before the start of the new tax year.
• You must also give your Employees a letter explaining that you’re Payrolling Benefits,
and what it means for them.
• Payrolling Benefits and Expenses remove the need submit a form P11D.
• You are still required to work out the Class 1A National Insurance contributions on the
cash equivalent (notional value) and return a form P11D(b).
• If you choose to payroll company car benefits, you do not need to submit a
form P46(Car). The PeopleXD system does not currently support the production of a
P46 Car return.
Note 1:
You can payroll all benefits except:
• Employer provided living accommodation.
• Interest-free and low-interest (beneficial) loans.
You must still report these benefits on a P11D, even if you’re payrolling other benefits for
the same employees.

8. FAQ’s
8.1. Corrections Question: Can incorrect data be amended easily?
Answer: Yes. A Create/Maintain P11Details section has been developed to facilitate changes.
Updates can also be carried out via the CSV file.
Question: I have submitted P11Ds to HMRC – what can I do to amend my P11D return?
Answer: If you have completed your submission to HMRC and you realise that there were errors
or omissions in the data that has been sent, you will need to submit a revised version of the form(s)
in which the error(s) occurred.
Note 1:
HMRC require all amendments be submitted in paper form.
Note 2:
If you’re correcting a P11D form include all the benefits and expenses for the tax year, not
just the ones you want to change.
For example, if a P11D had data in Section F and Section I, and the correction is only to Section
I, submit a P11D that includes Section F and Section I, not just the modified Section I.
Note 3:
The amended form needs to clearly show that it is an amendment (traditionally handled by
writing the word “Amendment” across the form) and must show the tax year to which it relates.

1. PAYE Modernisation Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Section
Since January 2019, the introduction of PAYE Modernisation requires real time reporting to Revenue. The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on all of the steps involved in this
process.
1.1.1. Real Time Reporting to Revenue
Real time reporting requires employers to submit the details of each employee's pay to Revenue
on or before each payday.
1.2. Summary of the Payroll Process
The below illustration outlines the steps involved in the real time reporting process and the
sequence to follow:
Step 1: Request Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN)
The Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) provides you with the necessary information to deduct the
correct Tax, USC, and LPT from the employee.
Below are some points to note about the request RPN process:
• Since 1st January 2019, before every payroll run an employer starts by requesting the latest
RPN for all employees i.e. any changes since the last payroll run. Payroll makes this request
directly to Revenue.
• Revenue receives the employer’s request and automatically sends the updated RPN
to the employer in Payroll.

This section guides how to manage the RPN (Revenue Payroll Notification) process . This includes:

2.1.2. What is the RPN Process?
RPN stands for “Revenue Payroll Notification” and includes the information required to deduct the
correct Tax, USC, and LPT from the employee.

RPN option.
• Request a new RPN for new employees that are commencing employment and being paid
for the first time.
Revenue receives the employer’s request and sends the updated RPN to the employer
electronically.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to manage the RPN (Revenue Payroll
Notification) process. This includes:
• Employment IDs for employees.
• Retrieving RPNs for employees before every payroll run.
• Review and resolving RPN exceptions.
• Updating employee RPN details.
• RPN cleardown.
1.2. What is the RPN Process?
RPN stands for “Revenue Payroll Notification” and includes the information required to deduct the
correct Tax, USC, and LPT from the employee.
Each payroll run requires you to:
• Request the most up to date RPNs for existing employees from Revenue through a Request
RPN option.
• Request a new RPN for new employees that are commencing employment and being paid
for the first time.
Revenue receives the employer’s request and sends the updated RPN to the employer
electronically. Updated RPNs are made available via this process. Any of the following may trigger
updates:
• Revenue updates, e.g. initial annual RPN creation.
• Employee updates, e.g. PAYE services.

can only be generated where an employee has a PPSN.
If an employee has multiple employments with a company, they have unique Employment IDs per
employment, e.g.

2. State Pension Contribution
2.1. Overview
A change is being made to the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) for the inclusion of a new
indicator called State Pension Contributory (SPC). This new indicator is enabled for employees in
receipt of their State Pension Contributory (SPC). This indicator can be viewed in the following
screens:
• Payroll Dashboard > Uploads > Load Employee RPN Certificates
• Payroll Dashboard > Employee > View > View Tax Certs
2.2. What is deferring the State Pension (Contributory)?
The State Pension (Contributory) is paid to people from the age of 66 who have enough (PRSI)
contributions. From January 2024, you can choose to start claiming your State Pension
(Contributory) anytime between the ages of 66 and 70. Choosing a later start date is called

2024, you can choose to start claiming your State Pension
(Contributory) anytime between the ages of 66 and 70. Choosing a later start date is called deferring your pension. You can defer your start date up until you turn 70.
2.3. Why would I defer the start date for my State Pension (Contributory)?
During deferral, you can continue to work and make PRSI contributions to:
• Increase your personal rate of payment, or
• Meet the qualifying condition of 520 (10 years) contributions for State Pension
(Contributory).
This means that deferring your State Pension (Contributory) can help you to:
• Qualify for State Pension (Contributory) if you didn't qualify at age 66
• Get a higher rate of State Pension (Contributory) than what you would have got at age 66
2.4. Who can defer their State Pension (Contributory)?
If you were born on or after 1 January 1958, you can choose to claim the State Pension
(Contributory) anytime between the ages of 66 and 70. Once you start claiming your State Pension
(Contributory), you can no longer choose to defer your pension claim, even if you keep working.
This is because you don’t pay PRSI once you start getting your pension.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to manage the RPN (Revenue Payroll
Notification) process. This includes:
• Employment IDs for employees.
• Retrieving RPNs for employees before every payroll run.
• Review and resolving RPN exceptions.
• Updating employee RPN details.
• RPN cleardown.
1.2. What is the RPN Process?
RPN stands for “Revenue Payroll Notification” and includes the information required to deduct the
correct Tax, USC, and LPT from the employee.
Each payroll run requires you to:
• Request the most up to date RPNs for existing employees from Revenue through a Request
RPN option.
• Request a new RPN for new employees that are commencing employment and being paid
for the first time.
Revenue receives the employer’s request and sends the updated RPN to the employer
electronically. Updated RPNs are made available via this process. Any of the following may trigger
updates:
• Revenue updates, e.g. initial annual RPN creation.
• Employee updates, e.g. PAYE services.
• Employer updates, e.g. payroll submission.

2. State Pension Contribution
2.1. Overview
A change is being made to the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) for the inclusion of a new
indicator called State Pension Contributory (SPC). This new indicator is enabled for employees in
receipt of their State Pension Contributory (SPC). This indicator can be viewed in the following
screens:
• CorePay > Employee > ROS Interface > Load Employee RPN Certificates
• CorePay > Employee > Cumulatives > View Tax Certs
2.2. What is deferring the State Pension (Contributory)?
The State Pension (Contributory) is paid to people from the age of 66 who have enough (PRSI)
contributions. From January 2024, you can choose to start claiming your State Pension
(Contributory) anytime between the ages of 66 and 70. Choosing a later start date is called

2024, you can choose to start claiming your State Pension
(Contributory) anytime between the ages of 66 and 70. Choosing a later start date is called deferring your pension. You can defer your start date up until you turn 70.
2.3. Why would I defer the start date for my State Pension (Contributory)?
During deferral, you can continue to work and make PRSI contributions to:
• Increase your personal rate of payment, or
• Meet the qualifying condition of 520 (10 years) contributions for State Pension
(Contributory).
This means that deferring your State Pension (Contributory) can help you to:
• Qualify for State Pension (Contributory) if you didn't qualify at age 66
• Get a higher rate of State Pension (Contributory) than what you would have got at age 66
2.4. Who can defer their State Pension (Contributory)?
If you were born on or after 1 January 1958, you can choose to claim the State Pension
(Contributory) anytime between the ages of 66 and 70. Once you start claiming your State Pension
(Contributory), you can no longer choose to defer your pension claim, even if you keep working.
This is because you don’t pay PRSI once you start getting your pension.

until a new RPN instruction is received.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The Purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the software and configuration for an
employee Social Welfare entitlement for Sickness days.
The Social Welfare Guide and module relates to the calculation of Social Welfare for Sickness
absence only and does not cover other calculation of social welfare entitlements for other

1.2. Costing
In terms of costing by default all Social Welfare Sickness calculations are posted to the employee
default appointment cost centre. In PeopleXD Payroll there is a facility to allocate non ‘Salary and

Sickness calculations are posted to the employee
default appointment cost centre. In PeopleXD Payroll there is a facility to allocate non ‘Salary and Permanent Allowance’ type transactions i.e. Social Welfare, Hourly Payments/once off timesheets
etc over split codes but this currently works on the following basis:
One timesheet is created for all the Social Welfare periods of absence for the employee i.e. assume
an employee in a monthly payroll is sick for week 1, back to work in week 2 and sick again in week
3 and that the employee has a split costing set up to only start in week 3.
Because ONE payment record covering week 1 and week 3 is generated (as opposed to 1 for each

1.3. Waiting Days
The following are example of Social Welfare waiting days in practice:
• If the employee has been employed for less than the SSP qualifying weeks (13), then the
standard waiting days (3) will apply.
• Where the employee qualifies for SSP, and the employee is absent for the first time in the
tax year, the SSP Days (5) will apply as waiting days for this absence.
• For the next new absence and subsequent new absences, the SSP Days (5) will be reduced
by the number of sick days taken in the tax year giving the current absence waiting days.
If the current absence waiting days are greater than the standard waiting days (3) then
those waiting days are applied.
• Where the current absence waiting days are less or equal to the standard waiting days,
then the standard waiting days will be applied.
These values are the 2024 parameters for SSP and Social Welfare. These values may change
annually.
For further information please see the Government website.

A number of offset days at Pay Group level. The offset days will be added to the sickness date and

8.2. Service Lines

• Salary is at a point in time for all eligible employees by appointment/post level.
• Any changes are made to Salary within the relevant year.
• Eligibility is determined by Category/Staff Type (Teacher, Researcher, Academic, etc).
• An employee must be returned if they fall into an eligible category for the Teachers Pension
Scheme (TPS), regardless of whether they have actually contributed to the scheme.
For the purposes of the return, a Leaver is also defined as follows:
• Someone who either leaves the appointment/post with eligible staff type or leaves the
organisation.

Days excluded are output for full time employees where they have an unpaid absence. I.e. unpaid

The unpaid absence pay codes need to be identified in the pay code configuration tab of the TPS

excluded so the KIT pay codes also need to be identified on initial set up. Then if the TPS program

employees. For part time employees it will reduce the part time pay and days excluded will be 0.

1.2. Overview of Total Reward Statements
The purpose of the Total Reward Statements module is to allow employees to understand and value
their total rewards package. An employee’s total rewards package may be made up of things like:
• Salary
• Incentives
• Benefits
• Prerequisites
• Learning and Development
The Total Reward Statements module allows employers to communicate the value of an employee’s
total rewards package in a personalised way. The benefits of communicating employees’ rewards
packages include:
• Increased employee engagement.
• Increased employee understanding of their value to your organisation.
• Increased staff retention.
• Increased morale.
The Total Reward Statement s updates once the employees’ cumulatives update. The employees’
cumulatives update once the Complete Update task is complete.

1.2. What is Year End? At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to:
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.
• Run the Year End Cleardown task.
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.

• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’
table.
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years.
The UK Year End Software Release provides our customers with the following:

3.4.3. Change 2 — Removal of the Lower Earnings Limit
3.4.3.1. What was the Lower Earnings Limit?
The Lower Earnings Limit (LEL) is the minimum level of weekly earnings an employee must have
to qualify for SSP. For 2025/26 the LEL was £125 per week (£6,500 per year). Employees earning
below this threshold — however many hours they work — were entirely excluded from SSP,
regardless of how long they had been employed. This disproportionately affected part-time
workers, zero-hours contract workers, and lower-paid employees, many of whom had no
entitlement to sick pay at all.
3.4.3.2. What changes from 6 April 2026?
The LEL for SSP purposes is completely removed. All employees will be eligible for SSP from 6
April 2026 regardless of how much they earn, provided they meet the other qualifying conditions

3.4.3.3. Who is newly eligible?
Approximately 1.3 million additional workers gain SSP eligibility from 6 April 2026. The groups
most affected include:
• Part-time employees earning below £125/week
• Zero-hours contract workers with variable or low weekly earnings
• Casual workers on short-term or seasonal contracts

3.4.4.3. How is Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) calculated?
AWE uses the same 8-week reference period already used for other statutory payments (such as SMP). The calculation uses earnings in the 8 weeks immediately prior to the 'relevant date' —

as per the above divided by 52.

3.4.5. Transitional Protections
Employees who were already off sick and receiving SSP before 6 April 2026 are protected from
any reduction in their SSP payment because of the new rules. These transitional protections are
intended to prevent mid-absence disruption.
3.4.5.1. Who is protected?
Transitional protection applies to employees who:
• Were already off sick and in receipt of SSP before 6 April 2026, AND
• Are earning between £125.00 and £154.05 per week (the range where 80% of AWE is less
than the flat rate), AND
• Remain continuously absent on and after 6 April 2026

not transitionally protected. 3.4.5.2. What does transitional protection mean in practice?
A transitionally protected employee continues to receive SSP at the uprated flat rate of £123.25
per week for the remainder of their absence, rather than switching to the 80% AWE calculation.
This ensures they do not see a reduction in their SSP payment mid-absence.
3.4.5.3. When does transitional protection end?
Protection ends on whichever of the following occurs first:
• The employee returns to work (because they are fit for work)
• The 28-week SSP entitlement is exhausted
• The employee's contract of employment ends
• The start of the SMP/MA exclusion period (pregnancy-related)
3.4.5.4. What about employees serving waiting days on 6 April 2026?
Employees who are off sick and serving their waiting days (days 1-3 of absence) at the point 6
April 2026 arrives become entitled to SSP from that date onwards, since waiting days are
abolished. They do not need to have been in receipt of SSP prior to the changeover — the
abolition of waiting days is applied immediately.

1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2023/24
and prepare for the 2024/25 tax year. This document covers the following:
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget.
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release.
• The tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.
• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task.
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2024/25 tax year.
1.2. What is Year End?
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to:
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.
• Run the Year End Cleardown task.
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.
• Issue Employees with a P60.
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks:
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.
• Moves the Employees' cumulative figures from the completed tax year to the ‘End of Year’
table.
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2022/23
and prepare for the 2023/24 tax year. This document covers the following:
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget.
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release.
• The tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.
• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task.
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2023/24 tax year.
1.2. What is Year End?
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to:
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.
• Run the Year End Cleardown task.
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.
• Issue Employees with a P60.
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks:
• Closes out the old tax year and moves the Payroll Company into a new tax year.
• Resets the Employees' cumulative figures.

• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years.
The UK Year End Software Release provides our customers with the following:

6.5.2. Employment Allowance
The Employment Allowance (EA) allows businesses and charities to reduce their Employer's Class
1 NIC liability by up to £5,000 per tax year.
The EA is only available to businesses and charities with an Employer's Class 1 NIC liability of below
£100,000 in the preceding tax year.
The EA is considered a form of de minimis state aid. There is a ceiling on how much state aid any
Organisation can receive under the de minimis rules. For most businesses, this ceiling will be
£200,000 over a three -year rolling period (different levels apply to agriculture, fisheries, road
transport, and industrial sectors).
Note:
If claiming the EA, it is your responsibility to check:
• Your Secondary Class 1 NICs liability for the previous tax year was less than £100,000.
• You have space to accommodate the full £5,000 within your relevant three-year ceiling,
regardless of how much EA you claim each year , if you receive any other form of de
minimis state aid.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the new features and
functionality introduced to absence pay in Payroll.
The new features and functionality are applicable to payroll occupational or statutory absence
types, such as:
• Maternity Pay • Paternity Pay
• Adoptive Pay • Shared Parental Pay
This new functionality is applicable doesn’t apply to non-payroll absences, such as:
• Annual Leave
• Privilege Day
• Innovative Thinking Days
• Jury Service Leave

o Information Per Absence Type – displays the key absence information for each of the
employee’s absence types and absence rules.
• The Occupational Detail screen is an enhanced version of the Back Office Absence Manager
Maintenance screen, which allows you to:
o To View Historical Occupational Absence details.
o To View Predicted Occupational Absence details.

2. Absence Period Daily Rate
The Absence Period Daily Rate introduces new methods for calculating an employee’s absence
daily rate. The absence daily rate can now be derived by dividing the period salary by the number
of days in the period. Note the following:
• The absence period daily rate calculation method can be configured at the following levels:
o Company Level.
o Pay Group Level.
o Absence Rule Level.
• The number of days in the period can be derived from:
o Calendar Days.
o Monday to Friday Days.
o Workforce Management Work Days.
• Allowance Groups allow you to select non-percentage allowance pay codes to include in
the calculation for deriving the employees’ absence daily rate.

The Absence Rate Override screen allows you to override an employee’s daily or hourly rate from
a specified effective date. Note the following:

4. Absence Pay Prediction
The Absence Pay Prediction task is a new overnight task which calculates future occupational
absences based on the WFM absence start and end dates. The Absence Pay Prediction task predicts
the date the occupational pay is expected to drop or increase, based on:
• The absence entitlement rule assigned to the employee.
• The employee’s FTE.
For example, full pay to half pay or half pay to zero pay.
The Absence Pay Prediction task can be manually run for a single employee via Employee Dashboard
in Payroll.
5. Absence Reversals
If the cancelled absence relates to the previous payroll period, payroll can now reverse the
transactions related to the absence.

5. Absence Reversals
If the cancelled absence relates to the previous payroll period, payroll can now reverse the
transactions related to the absence. There are two reversal solutions available:
• Fully Automatic Reversals: Allows the system to reverse the payment automatically ,
while informing you of the reversal via a Payroll Message.
• User-Triggered Reversals: Requires user intervention to reverse an absence payment,
giving you control over what payroll transactions are processed.
6. Absence Entry
The Absences screen is the WFM Person Absence screen accessed via the Employee Dashboard in
Payroll. Use the Absences screen to:
• Add a New Absence.
• View or Edit an Existing Absence.
• Delete an Existing Absence.
• Link an Existing Absence to a Statutory Absence.
• View, Edit or Delete the Statutory Details Linked to the Absence.

1.2. What Bank File Settings can be Configured
A bank file is the instruction sent to the bank to pay employees, this can be in varying formats. The
Bank File is used to select the type of file generated, as each bank has different file requirements.
When a bank file is generated at the end of each payroll period 3 files are created:
1. PDF
2. CSV
3. File to send to the bank
The new bank file settings functionality allows a user to customise the file sent to the bank and the
.csv. It does not customise the .pdf file. It customises:
1. File Name (bank file and .csv).
2. File extension (bank file).
3. Location of bank file (report centre or server location).
• The server location requires DBA set up and incurs costs.
• Customers can configure only one server location.
Note:
SEPA configuration is currently not included in this new feature and the file name and extension
cannot be amended at this time.

The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure the absence pay
parameters relating to the occupational absence module in Payroll.

• General Parameters.

• Absence Rules.

1.2. What is the Occupational Absence Module?
The Occupational Absence module allows organisations to set up their occupational absence
(absenteeism) policies so that pay can be assigned to employee absences per the organisation's
requirements.
Note the following points:
• An organisation may have different absence procedures for different profiles of employees ,
such as:
Employee Category Entitlement
Permanent Employees Entitled to 30 days sick leave at full pay over a 12-month period.
Fixed-Term Employees Entitled to 21 days sick leave at full pay over a 12-month period.
• An employee's Absence Category determines which absence rule (absence policy) applies to
them, and can be used to calculate the employee's occupational pay per absence day/hour.
• Multiple Absence Leave schemes may apply to the same employee. For example, different

alculate the employee's occupational pay per absence day/hour.
• Multiple Absence Leave schemes may apply to the same employee. For example, different maternity schemes may apply depending on whether the employee is returning to work, or
the employee may be able to choose between two different schemes. The pay code used to
record the leave controls which scheme is applied.
• The Occupational Absence module is generally implemented in conjunction with the Statutory
Payments Feature (UK Only) so that an employee 's pay for an absence taken is calculated per
the organisation's occupational absence policies and UK Statutory policies.
• Occupational Absences may be recorded by:
o A manager using the Team Schedule widget.
o An administrator using Workforce Management.
o An administrator using the Payroll – Go to Payroll Dashboard > Empl oyee > View >
Absence Entry.
Example:
The Occupational Absence module can be configured to ensure that full -time permanent
workers who have taken over 30 sick leave days during a 12 -month period, only receive half
pay for the next sick leave day taken.

1.2. What is an Analysis Code?
Analysis Codes are used to group a set of Pay Codes that are configured with similar
characteristics.
For example:
• A pay code for adoption leave would be assigned to an Analysis Code of “Absence
Management.”
• A pay code for basic hours would be assigned an Analysis Code of “Basic Pay”.
All Pay Codes must be associated with an Analysis Code. You can add Analysis Codes as required,
but they must be associated with one of the following specific Analysis Types :
▪ GP - Gross Pay
▪ BK – Benefit in Kind
▪ NT - Non-Taxable

The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure auto enrolment. This

1.2. What is Auto Enrolment?
Auto Enrolment is a government initiative and requires every employer of staff normally working
in the UK to put their qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and to make contributions
towards their employee's pension.

f normally working
in the UK to put their qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and to make contributions
towards their employee's pension. Employees will be automatically enrolled into the workplace pension scheme if they are not
already active members of a workplace pension scheme that meets a set of minimum standards.
The employer must make pension contributions to the pension scheme , and the worker may also
have to contribute. Workers who do not want to join the scheme may opt -out for a three-year
period. But, employers are required to continue automatically enrolling el igible workers who’ve
opted out, every three years.
Eligible employees are workers who:
• Are aged between 22 and State Pension Age;
• Earn over the earnings threshold, and
• Work, or ordinarily work in the UK and have a contract of employment (i.e. so is a worker
and not a self-employed contractor), or who have a contract to provide work and / or
services personally (so can’t sub-contract to a third party).

1.2. What are Cost Centres?
A cost centre is a unit within your company, to which costs may be allocated for cost accounting
purposes. These should be in line with the cost centres set up in your financial system. A cost
centre is a code to which an employee's costs (salary, expenses etc.) are charged. Points to note:
• The cost centre codes are interfaced into your Financial Management System (FMS).
• Each employee is assigned a cost centre associated with their contract when they are set
up in HR.
• PeopleXD system also provides the option to configure additional/alternative cost centres
to be used to charge the employees' costs.

to be used to charge the employees' costs. Cost Allocations, Timesheet Current Period, and Pay Code configuration allow you to allocate an
employee's pay to a cost centre(s) other than what is on the employee's contract.
For example, a marketing executive has his/her costs assigned to a marketing cost centre.
However, that employee is asked to cover for a sales executive to cover a period of leave. The
company can re-assign their salary / costs to the sales department for the duration of that
period.

Project Codes allow an organisation to charge employees costs to specific projects. A project is
typically a temporary endeavour with a defined beginning and end.

allow you to allocate an employee’s pay to a project code(s) other than what is on the
employee's contract.
• Project Codes are typically used for cost centre sub-analysis in Financial Management
Systems (FMS).

Statutory payments are payments that are made to employees to cover earnings lost when they

• Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP)
• Additional Statutory Paternity Pay (ASPP)
• Ordinary Statutory Sick Pay (OSSP)
• Adoption Pay (SAP)
• Shared Parental Leave
• Redundancy

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Payroll Calendars for
a company.
Items covered include:
• How to add a Payroll Calendar.
• How to edit a Payroll Calendar.
• How to duplicate a Payroll Calendar.
1.2. What is a Payroll Calendar?
A payroll calendar must be generated for each company within an organisation. The following points
should be noted:
• A payroll calendar must be generated for each company within an organisation.
• The calendar consists of the year broken up into week numbers, e.g. 202001, 202002,
202003 etc.
• The calendar tracks the period end date for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay
groups. The period end date for monthly pay groups will always be the last day of the
month.
• The payroll calendar does not track the payment date.
• Period end dates can be offset at a pay group level.
• The calendar will always contain at least the current year and future years.

1. Introduction
1.1. Purpose of this Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the new Joiners and
Rejoiners feature in PeopleXD Payroll including:
• How to view and process salary approvals
• How to join employees into Payroll individually and in bulk.
• How to rejoin employees into Payroll individually and in bulk.
• Increased transparency on how to action rejoiners in Payroll.
1.2. What is the Enhanced Process?
1. Salary Approvals
• Provides improved visibility of outstanding salary approvals.
2. Joiners
• Allows you to efficiently bulk join employees into Payroll after set up in People
Management.
• Gives you the ability to select default values for all mandatory fields required to
add employees into Payroll.
• Where required you can still use the Tax Details screen for joining employees.
3. Rejoiners
• Allows you to efficiently bulk rejoin employees into Payroll after set up in People
Management.
• Allows you to change a rejoiner’s Pay Group before rejoining them into Payroll.
• Provides full transparency around rejoiners processed within People
Management.
• Action is required to process rejoiners on Payroll for the current payroll run.

1. Introduction
1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use and configure Payroll Messages
in Payroll. This document also covers the new Unprocessed Employees screen and how to use it.
1.2. What are Payroll Messages?
Payroll Messages replace the current process of checking Observation Messages. Payroll Messages,
once generated, detail all Errors, Warnings and Notifications for the current Payroll Period.
Note:
• Payroll Messages are now interactive.

Messages,
once generated, detail all Errors, Warnings and Notifications for the current Payroll Period.
Note:
• Payroll Messages are now interactive. • Payroll Messages generate and can be configured at a Pay Group Level.
• All Payroll Messages, except for System Messages, can be:
o Enabled or Disabled.
o Classified according to their urgency.
o Customised to meet your organisation's requirements.
o Categoried to customise your organisation's control checks.
• You can review Payroll Messages at an Employee Level.
• You can view which Payroll Messages other Payroll Users have actioned, providing you
with confidence that all Payroll Messages have been reviewed and Actioned.
• Previously, running the Payroll Validation task cleared all Observation Messages from
previous Payroll Periods.
• Payroll Messages generated in previous Payroll Periods, and their current Status, are
now carried forward and available to view at Employee Level through the OneView
screen.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide This document outlines the data and procedures to enable PeopleXD process input from an
External HR System. This interface caters for downloading of data from the External HR System
and the validation of this data on PeopleXD. No restriction is put on the number of times the
interface may be run e.g. hourly, daily, weekly etc.

Employee Personnel/Master File (EMP&&PAYGROUP.DAT)
This file is used to load up employee personnel and master file information. It should contain one entry at most for an employee.
2.1.1. Payroll Requirements
There are a number of controls that must be built into this interface flat file. They are as follows:
• For employees who are leaving the payroll, their leaving date will be passed across from
the external HR interface in the particular period that they are leaving. Payroll will then
terminate the employee as normal (status of Z). It is important however, that, from this
point onwards the leaving date be passed across as blank, for the employee. In other
words it should not be held permanently on their record; it acts as a trigger in the particular
period that they are leaving.
• For employees who are rejoining the payroll, their rejoin date will be passed across from
the external HR interface in the particular period that they are rejoining. Payroll will then
reinstate the employee as normal. It is important however, that, from this p oint onwards
the rejoin date be passed across as blank, for the employee. In other words it should not
be held permanently on their record; it acts as a trigger in the particular period that they
are rejoining.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how PeopleXD posts payroll
transactions into a General Ledger for integrating data into your Financial Management System
(FMS).
This guide includes the following:
• Standard General Ledger (GL) principles.
• The costing hierarchy within PeopleXD.
• The main integration points between PeopleXD and your FMS.
• How to develop an interface, to transfer all necessary financial data (GL), from PeopleXD
into your FMS.
Where applicable, the above will be supported by flowcharts, detailed steps and screenshots.
1.2. What is the PeopleXD FMS Integration?
PeopleXD facilitates posting of payroll transactions to third party Financial Management Systems
(FMS). This is achieved in PeopleXD by creating a General Ledger for payroll transactions.
1.3. What is the General Ledger?
The General Ledger is the main accounting record for a company or organisation.

eral Ledger for payroll transactions.
1.3. What is the General Ledger?
The General Ledger is the main accounting record for a company or organisation. Note 1: A company’s FMS may be referenced to as a General Ledger, so for this guide all
references to the General Ledger will exclusively mean the General Ledger (GL) produced in
PeopleXD.
Note 2: The GL in PeopleXD is a record of payroll transactions that uses double entry
accounting rules.

2. General Ledger Principles
2.1. General Ledger Terminology
Every transaction in double-entry accounting affects at least two accounts. The double-entry has
two equal and corresponding sides known as “Debit” and “Credit”.
2.1.1. What are Debits and Credits?
Accountancy/payroll transactions are recorded in terms of Debits and Credits.
The below table contains the basic rules that dictate whether a posting is a Debit or Credit:
Debit (Dr) Credit (Cr)
To increase an Asset To decrease an Asset
To increase an Expense/Cost To decrease an Expense/Cost
To decrease a Liability To increase a Liability
To decrease Earnings/Income To increase Earnings/Income
What is the difference between an “Expense” and a “Liability”?
Expense/Cost
Cost incurred by the business, e.g. gross pay to an employee, overtime, employer
pension.
Liability

tween an “Expense” and a “Liability”?
Expense/Cost
Cost incurred by the business, e.g. gross pay to an employee, overtime, employer
pension.
Liability Money owed by the business , e.g. nett pay to the employee, PAYE to
HMRC/Revenue, employer pension to a pension company.
Note: In double-entry accounting the total value of Debits and the total value Credits will
always equal. Therefore, the GL should always balance.
.
Note: A payroll transaction will generally involve increasing a cost/expense in the P&L
(Debit) and increasing a liability in the Balance Sheet (Credit).

new functionality, accessible via the employee self-service (ESS) login, will provide staff with an
early look at their payment details, fostering transparency and allowing any discrepancies to be
addressed promptly.

2.2. What is Benefit in Kind?
Benefits in Kind (BIK) are benefits which employees or directors receive from their employment,
but which are not included in their salary or wages.
"Benefit in Kind" or "Payrolling Benefits" involves adding the cash equivalent of the employees'
benefits to their pay and then taxing them through the payroll.
They include things like:
• Company cars.
• Private Medical Insurance.
• Cheap or free Loans.
BIKs are initially created as pay codes under Settings > Codes > Pay Codes.
Note:
For more information, see the Maintain Pay Codes user guide.

2.3. Generate / Transfer Real Time Information (RTI)
Once payroll has been completed, you must generate and transfer the Real Time Information (RTI)
file to HMRC. You can choose from the following file types:
• Full Payroll Submission (FPS)
• Employer Alignment Submission (EAS)
• Employer Payment Summary (EPS)
• Earlier Year Update (EYU)
2.3.1. RTI File Types
Full Payroll Submission (FPS)
The FPS is the submission you must make to HMRC each time you pay your employees and
contains:
• Details of all payments made to employees in the pay run.
• Employee income tax and NI contributions in the pay run.
• Details of any starters or leavers from the pay run.
PeopleXD Payroll: Maintain Payroll Outputs
Access Limited Distribution Page 11 of 20

• Details of any starters or leavers from the pay run.
PeopleXD Payroll: Maintain Payroll Outputs
Access Limited Distribution Page 11 of 20 • Employee details, such as name, NI number and tax code.
HMRC tracks this information throughout the tax year to confirm that each
employee’s PAYE and NIC liabilities are being deducted correctly.
Employer Alignment Submission (EAS)
If you have 250 employees or more, your first submission must be an Employee Alignment
Submission (EAS), which simply contains the details of all your employees, allowing HMRC to align
their records with yours.
Employer Payment Summary (EPS)
Your regular FPS submissions after each pay run , generally provide HM RC with the information
they need to confirm throughout the year that each employee’s tax and national insurance (NI)
liabilities are being deducted correctly. It also determines the amount you owe HMRC at the end
of each tax reporting period. The payment due to HMRC for this liability is known as a P32
payment.
You would normally submit an employer payment summary (EPS) when you recover statutory
payments, which reduces your liability and the amount you owe HMRC. It includes supplementary
information about your company’s tax and NI liability, such as employment allowance.

Earlier Year Update (EYU) EYU stands for Earlier Year Update. It is required if an adjustment needs to be made to a previous
RTI tax year. This will only apply for corrections in previous years where a client was returning
PAYE using RTI.
An FPS can only be sent up until 19th April following the end of a tax year. After this any corrections
need to be made on an EYU. Non-RTI years will still be corrected via amended P35/P14s as per the
existing PAYE arrangement.

1.2. What is a Deduction
A deduction is a process whereby an employer deducts a specified amount from an employee's
pay and puts the funds toward insurance, healthcare, investment account etc . Most deductions
are based on either a specific monetary value or in other cases may be a percentage of salary.

e, healthcare, investment account etc . Most deductions
are based on either a specific monetary value or in other cases may be a percentage of salary. A deduction can take many forms and be for many reasons which will be covered later in this
document in the 1.3 Deduction Types section.
Once-off Deductions
One-off deductions can be made using a timesheet.
For example:
• Late for work.
• Overpayment correction from a previous pay period.
Timesheets are covered in the Timesheet Current Period lesson in this course.
Permanent/Reoccurring Deductions
These deductions are included every time payroll is run, for a defined period or the duration of the
employment (open-ended).
Most deductions are based on either a specific monetary value or in other cases may be a
percentage of salary.
For example:
• Tax allowable: Payroll Giving
• Non-allowable: Savings

1.3. Deduction Types
The type of deduction is set at pay code level.
This document covers the following deduction types:
• Standard Value Deduction

• Fixed Period Deduction
• Scaled Deduction
• Annual/Periodic Max Deduction (Increasing)
• Spreadable, Instalment Deduction
• Court/Voluntary Order Deduction

1.3.1. Standard Value Deduction A Standard Value Deduction is the simplest form of deduction. It is u sed to deduct a periodic
amount in each payroll run.
There are two types of ‘Value’ based deductions:
Standard deductions: A specified amount is defined on the deduction pay code, i.e. the value is
the same for all employees.
Variable deductions: The amount to be deducted is specific to the individual employee. These are
not captured on the pay code but instead captured when adding the deduction to the employee's
record.
Note:
Deductions are created as pay codes. For more information please see the Configuring Pay
Codes user guide.

An example of a Standard Value Deduction may be “Social Club”.
The value of a standard value deduction can be updated at pay code level. This will update all
employees with the standard value assigned to reflect the configured standard value.

A Standard Percentage Deduction is used to deduct a percentage value amount, calculated based
on different elements defined at the pay code level. Like a value deduction, the percentage value
can be specified on the pay code or when applied to an employee's record.

An example of a percentage deduction may be “Savings”.
1.3.3. Reducing Balance Deduction
A Reducing Balance Deduction is used to a deduct a standard value or percentage each period
until a specified sum is repaid. The balance due on the deduction is reduced every time the
deduction is processed for the employee. The deduction automatically cease s when the balance
due value reaches zero.
If the deduction cannot be taken in full, then the full deduction amount can be held as unpaid and
can be added to the employee’s following deduction when next paid.
Note: When assigning the value to a person, it is the percentage value that is assigned and
not a monetary value e.g. Entering 5 represents 5%.

Some points about Fixed Term Deductions:

‘Deduction Record’.

If a Value is assigned it is the periodic value that needs to be assigned and not the capital sum.
This represents the Total Annual Value to be deducted. The balance due is automatically set to

1.3.6. Spreadable, Instalment Deduction
A Spreadable Installment Deduction takes an annual figure and divides it over a specified
number of periods. If a deduction period is missed, it recalculates the periodic amount by the
remaining number of instalments. This will ensure that the deduction is always paid by the end
of the year.
