1.3.7. Court/Voluntary Order Deduction
This type of deduction is used to control the processing of Court / Voluntary Orders.
• A Court Order will take precedence over all non-statutory deductions (excluding
pension) and is subject to a user-specified Minimum Earnings.
• A Voluntary Order is taken after all Statutory, Court Order and Non-Statutory
deductions. It can be subject to user-specified Minimum Earnings.
These deduction types may only be for a specified periodic value and may be split over a number
of user-specified payees.
If the minimum earnings are insufficient to meet the total amount of the order, the system will
deduct as much as possible subject to the Minimum Earnings. Where the full amount cannot be
taken, and the order is payable to a number of payees, the deduction is split pro-rata over all
payees.
Amounts not taken in any period (because of minimum earnings ) are not taken in subsequent
periods.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Pay Code Wizard functionality in
Payroll and how to use the Pay Code Wizard to create pay codes. This includes:
• What is the Pay Code Wizard?

1.2. What is a Pay Code?
Pay codes are used to define each pay element/type within Payroll. New pay codes may be defined
and configured as required. When creating new pay codes, it is common practice to clone a similar
existing pay code. Once a pay code is defined, it becomes available within all areas of payroll, i.e.
within all pay groups and companies.
Note: It is best practice to code Pay Codes in line with Analysis Codes. For example, if non-
statutory deductions are designated analysis code 700, then all non-statutory deductions are
in range 700-799.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure and process
retrospection in PeopleXD Payroll.
Items covered include:
• Configure a Pay Group to calculate retrospection.
• Configure retrospection Pay Codes

1.2. What is Retrospection
Retrospective pay, also known as back pay , is where an employee’s rate or position/point has
changed, and the effective date is in the past. Therefore, it is necessary to reimburse the employee
and calculate their retrospective pay.
Retrospection can be generated by Payroll in many different situations. For example:
• Where a pay award is agreed in October but effective from the previous July.
• Where an employee’s pay increase is back dated.
PeopleXD Payroll differentiates between salary and hourly paid employees for retrospective pay:
1.2.1. Retrospective Pay for Salary Paid Employees:
Once configured, retrospective pay for salary employees is calculated automatically as part of the
Payroll Process. The Generate Salaries and Allowances task will calculate any retrospective pay for
the Period.
For this to be processed you need to:
1. Configure the Pay Group to calculate retrospection.

2. Set-up arrears pay codes for each pay code, for example, basic pay arrears, holiday arrears,

2. Set-up arrears pay codes for each pay code, for example, basic pay arrears, holiday arrears, overtime arrears, etc. All retrospective pay will be calculated against a relevant arrears pay
code.
3. Run the Generate Salaries and Allowances and Payroll Validation tasks.
1.2.2. Retrospective Pay for Positive Input (i.e., Timesheet Paid) Employees:
Positive input employees will not automatically get back pay unless the Positive Input
Retrospection process is run.
For this to be processed you need to:
1. Configure the Pay Group to calculate retrospection.
2. Set-up arrears pay codes for each pay code, for example, basic pay arrears, holiday arrears,
overtime arrears, etc. All employees retrospective pay will be calculated against a relevant
arrears pay code.
3. Run Positive Input Retrospection.

3. Frequently Asked Questions 3.1. Supplementary Payroll
The Scheduled task feature cannot be used when in Supplementary Mode.
3.2. Is There a Limit to the Number of Tasks I can Schedule?
You can schedule one task or combination of tasks, per pay group, at any one time.
3.3. Can I Schedule a Task to run Overnight?
When setting the time, you must choose one of the 30-minute intervals between 8.00 am and 10.00
pm. This limitation is in place to avoid interrupting Workforce Management tasks which run
overnight.
3.4. What Happens if a Task is Still Running at 10.00pm?
If a job is running at 10.00pm, it will continue to run until completion.
3.5. Can I Still run Tasks While a Pay Group is in Schedule Tasks Mode?
Yes, you can still run tasks while a pay group is in Schedule Tasks Mode.
3.6. Does Schedule Tasks Affect the Workforce Management Module?
Yes, the Confirm Timesheets task should not be run if absences are scheduled to come into payroll
overnight, as Confirm Timesheets closes the current Timesheet Input Period.
The recommended process is to schedule the Confirm Timesheets task (or any combination of tasks
that includes Confirm Timesheets) for the following morning.

1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Single Processing task in
Payroll.
1.2. Overview of Single Employee Processing
The Single Processing task, which replaces the previous Trial Payroll task, allows you to calculate
payroll for a single employee, by processing the following task(s):
• 5-Step Payroll: The Salaries & Allowances and Payroll Validation tasks.
• 3-Step Payroll: The Calculate Payroll task.
The Single Processing task eliminates the need to rerun the Payroll Validation task for the entire pay
group when a single employee is recalculated. Therefore, speeding up the overall payroll process.
Previously to this change:
• Running a Trial Payroll for a single employee cleared out any gross to nett details populated
by the Payroll Validation task, replacing them with gross to nett details populated by
employee’s Trial Payroll.
Note:
The Single Processing task does not allow you to change the sequence in which payroll tasks are
processed, e.g. you cannot process a single employee once the Confirm Timesheet task is
complete.

1.2. Introduction to the Payroll Cutoff Date
The Payroll Cutoff Date provides transparency by allowing you, the Payroll User, to control the flow of Salary, Allowance, and Pension changes transferring from People Management to Payroll. The

Current Payroll Period.

4. Leavers
4.1. Overview
Where an Employee's Contract is ended, the associated Allowances and Pensions are automatically
ended. Leavers are not automatically sent to the Staged Changes screen. This is to avoid the
common scenario where Leavers are incorrectly paid their full Salary. Instead, Leavers’ Salary,
Allowance and Pension end dates are sent directly to the Unprocessed Employees screen. See
section Unprocessed Employees.
4.2. Staged Changes – Leaver
In HR, after the Payroll Cutoff Date, any subsequent changes of Salary, Allowance, or Pension
entered for a Leaver are Staged. A Leaver chip displays in the Staged Employees Screen to inform
you that the Employee is leaving in the Current Payroll Period, and these changes should be
Advanced.

original contract, along with its associated Allowances and Pensions, are sent to Payroll. The

To add a tab:
1. Quick jump to Dashboard Configuration
2. Select Dashboard = Administrator Dashboard.
3. Click Add Page Tab.
Note:
It is recommended that all widgets required to support the data migration functionality are configured
on a Data Migration tab on the Administrator Dashboard. This configuration is defaulted on install
of CoreHR.

3. User Access
3.1. Default Data Migration Menu Profile
A pre-configured menu profile is available. This includes all of the necessary V1 (previous data migration
tool) and V2 (enhanced V28 data migration tool) menu options required for a user to:
• Complete data migration uploads
• Process Updates
Menu Profile
CorePortal_DataMigration_User
3.2. Access to the Data Migration Widgets
Each of the 3 data migration widgets are controlled using a single menu option:
Menu Option Description
CoreHR - Data Migration CoreHR - Data Migration
Once the user has this option, they will have full access for each of the following widgets:
• Data Migration Templates.
• Data Migration Options.
• Data Migration Update Facility.

Account Activity.

.8. Menu Profile Matrix
The Menu Profile Matrix feature provides a way to identify groups of employees and
automatically assign menu profiles to them. There are 2 types of assignments available:
• Employee Organisation Role
Menu profiles are assigned to employees based on an Organisational Role that they are
assigned to. A nightly process identifies any employees with an Organisational Role that
is defined in the rule matrix. If the Org Role assignment is effective that day, the process
will assign the menu profile. If the Org Role is no longer active, the process will unassign
the role.
• Employee Account Provisioning
Menu profiles are assigned to employees as part of the registration process. If the
employee’s current substantive contract meets the requirements in one of these rules,
they will be awarded the corresponding menu profile.
To learn how to configure the menu profile matrix read the user guide.
Note: This has an immediate impact for any users that are assigned to that menu profile.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to manage the process of assigning
security roles and privileges to joiner, movers and leavers (JMLs) in PeopleXD. It gives information
on what can be carried out to make the JML process more efficie nt and clearer for both a HR
administrator and system administrator.

gives information
on what can be carried out to make the JML process more efficie nt and clearer for both a HR
administrator and system administrator. This guide outlines configuration actions that need to be carried out to ensure any JML process
can be rolled out quickly. It also explains how task lists work and how they can be used to copy a
user and assign a menu profile to a number of users. The following tasks are explained throughout
this document:
• Joiner process – through the task list you can copy an existing employee or assign a profile
• Mover process (New Contract, Additional contract, Rehire) – through the task list you
can copy a user or assign a profile
• Leaver – through the task list you can assign a leaver profile
• Ad-hoc changes – through the actions list on the employee record
• Bulk updates – run a report to get a list of employees based on your criteria.

employee PeopleXD accounts, directly from within People Management when managing employee
contract updates as part of JML processes i.e. assign menu profiles, organisational roles and/or
access to PeopleXD system data.
Access can be managed in a number of ways:
• Copy access from an existing similar employee.
• Assign access via a security profile.

5.1. What are Menu Profiles?
Menu Profiles are used to control and restrict user's access to system functionality. Various
elements of the system are controlled by Menu Options including:
• Dashboards
• Screens
• Buttons
• Menu options
• Widgets
A Menu Profile is a defined set of Menu Options that can be assigned to a user in bulk. These are
typically aligned to a user's role in the organisation e.g. a profile for 'HR Administrators', another
for 'Payroll Administrators', another for regular employees etc.
When the profile is assigned to the employee, they will get access to all the system functionality
controlled by the corresponding Menu Options.
Employees will require at a minimum one Menu Profile to access the system. However, they may
have many, depending on their role e.g.
• Employee Menu Profile to access the Employee Dashboard.
• Manager Menu Profile to access the Manager Dashboard (if they are a manager) .
• HR Admin Menu Profile to access the People Management dashboard if they are an HR

Profile to access the Manager Dashboard (if they are a manager) .

(2fa) in PeopleXD. This includes:
• How to use 2fa

1.2. Overview
Two factor authentication is an additional layer of security in the authentication process for
PeopleXD Portal. This issues an SMS code to a user’s registered mobile device.
1.3. Who should read this document
This document is intended for the following:
• Any member of XD projects, delivery and implementation team.
• XD customer support division.
• Customers making a decision to two factor authentication for PeopleXD.
• Independent Security Audit individuals.

• The solution outlined here is for customer configured to use standard XD Employee Self
Service (ESS) authentication. If you are using SSO via an IdP this setup is not applicable
as 2FA/MFA would be managed via your IdP solution.

3. Administrator Configuration
For employees to use 2fa, an administrator needs to enable it for the organisation. This can be
done in two ways:
1. Allow the employees to set up 2fa themselves. The employee has the choice to
enable/disable the 2fa in their account profile.
2. Forced 2fa. In this scenario, the employee cannot disable the authentication. When this
option is set by the administrator, any mobile numbers associated with the employee
are automatically set up as trusted numbers. The employee can add more, or delete
some, but will not be allowed to delete the last remaining number. If an admin in HR
adds or amends any contact numbers of the person, this change will also be reflected in
the trusted numbers.
Note: In the scenario where Forced 2fa has been configured, and no mobile contact
numbers exist for an employee, there will be no 2fa enabled for that employee.

1.3. What are Themes?
The Themes feature on PeopleXD allows you to change the appearance of the Portal UI, to align
this to your organisation’s own branding requirements.
PeopleXD provides a number of built-in themes. You can decide to use one of these themes or to
create new themes, specific to your organisation.
If an organisation comprises of more than one company, different themes can be created and
assigned to each company as required.
The following items can be defined per theme:
• Primary Colour
• Secondary Colour
• Card opacity level
• Background opacity level
• Upload a background image
• Upload customer logo
These items are reviewed in greater detail in 2.2 Create a New Theme.
Note: This is applicable to Modern UI only.

The purpose of this document is to provide examples of basic SQL functions within PeopleXD

1.2. Insight Overview
Insight is PeopleXD’s operational reporting tool. Insight utilizes our XD BI layer, which is a collection
of database views built from the PeopleXD tables.
Reports are built by choosing the columns from joined views, and applying appropriate filtering to
limit the returned data set.
As well as adding data directly from the data columns, it is possible to apply Oracle SQL database
functions to manipulate the data . These are referred to as calculation columns . Within the Edit

columns, it is possible to apply Oracle SQL database
functions to manipulate the data . These are referred to as calculation columns . Within the Edit mode of a report, to open the new Calculation screen, click Add, then Calculation:
PeopleXD Insight: Basic Calculations - User Guide

You can return various types of data with calculations, for example:
• Hardcode Values (e.g. Yes, X, Y etc.)
• Dynamic Values (e.g. sysdate)
• Conditional values (e.g. Age > 40 return A)
• Formatted data from reporting columns ( e.g. substring, rounded numbers, conversions
etc.)
• Aggregated data, and logical and conditional operations to the data.
o Additions, subtractions etc.
o Case Statements, Decodes
o Counts, Sums
1.3. Oracle PL-SQL Functions
Insight runs on an Oracle database . Calculated columns provide you with the ability to call the
Oracle SQL functions as part of your report writing.
SQL report writing is a large area, however it is possible to use these functions to format and put
some logic in your reports. This requires report writing/BI Developer expertise and experience to
apply calculations to achieve advanced reporting requirements.
SQL functions are not unique to Insight, and exist within every database and other softwa re (e.g
excel). Using the complex functions requires experience in SQL report writing. Further details are

reporting skills.
1.3.1. Document Scope
This document does not cover the full suite of available SQL functions, or more advanced uses or
combinations of functions and logic. This resides in the realm of general SQL reporting writing
experience, and not the Insight application usage.
Note: Only Simple Oracle SQL functions are available through Insight calculated columns.
Full procedural SQL (PLSQL) usage is not possible . For example, variables, cursors, IF
statements, and other procedural elements are not available in Insight.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to outline various best practice principles to follow when writing
a report for simplicity and better performance. This includes:
• Planning and building the report
• Performance considerations for data and views
• Aggregation reports
• FAQs and avoiding common issues
1.2. Prerequisites
This document is a best practice guide with an emphasis on report writing for optimal
performance. Before reading this guide, it is beneficial to have:
1. A working knowledge of Insight and some experience or training.
2. Familiarity with Insight user guides, including the following. These can all be found in the
Insight user guide library within the Help Centre.
• Insight Fundamentals
• Insight Key Concepts
• Admin Area
• Calculation Builder
• Insight User Security
• Useful Functions
• Basic Calculations
• iCues

3. Familiarity with creating tabular and pivot reports in Insight.
1.3. Insight Overview
Insight is PeopleXD’s operational reporting tool. Insight utilises our XD BI layer, which is a collection
of database views built from the PeopleXD tables. A business area is a collection of related

XD Insight Folders , also known as views, refer to specific reporting blocks. Examples of views
include:

A join is a relationship between two views, which allows you to combine data from more than one
view in your report. Each business area contains at least one master table, which has many of the
key attributes for the employee. These master views have joins to the other key views within that
business area.
As you add columns to a report, the list of available views and columns dynamically filters to display
the views that are available you based on what is already added to the report.

2. Good Practice
2.1. Overview
As an operational reporting tool using live data , it is the report writer’s responsibility to create
reports in an efficient manner so they can run in a reasonable time. Reports using the larger
transactional views (for example appointment, pay history, calculate hours etc.) require particular
attention.
It is recommended to follow good practice guidelines:
1. Limit the number of columns and views used so the report only includes the required
information.
a. Avoid adding unnecessary hidden columns, as they add to the report complexity
as much as a visible column.
b. When editing a cloned report, remove any columns that are not necessary for the
new report.
2. Filter up-front as much as possible to reduce processing time.
a. It is possible to filter not just on columns in your report, but any other columns
from the views referenced in your report. Up-front filtering is the recommended
method to ensure efficient performance.

4.1. Overview
Aggregation enables you to apply calculations to data in order to summarise the information (e.g.
Sum, Count, Max etc). In a tabular report you may want to use aggregation to group information about an employee into
one row. Every column needs to be common, or else it cannot roll up to a single row. If this is not
the case, the calculations for sums etc. will need to ‘partition over’ in your calculations, so that the
value groups as required (e.g. person reference, or person reference, payroll period). See the
practical examples below:
If the purpose of a report is to get the sum of all pay history for each employee across a set of pay
codes and pay periods, you cannot have either pay code or pay period in the report columns. This
is because there will be a number of different combinations of these , and the report will break
them out to multiple rows.
Another example would be if a report focused on total absence days, you could not include either
absence codes or reason codes on the report as they may differ across the data.

reports are aggregation reports, they are generally the recommended method for building reports
with sum, totals, sub totals etc.

4.3. Pivot Reports
4.3.1. Overview Pivot reports are by nature summary/aggregation reports and can be an easier way to summarise
data. They can have better performance than large aggregation in tabular reports and require less
complex calculations and no partition over logic.
Pivot tables consist of three elements:
1. Row: This can be thought of as the grouping for the line/row you want to display on the
report.
2. Column: This is how you want the data summari sed horizontally on the columns (e.g.
departments, pay codes, absence type etc.) This is dynamic in nature as in you’ll get a
column for each department, paycode etc. found in the results set. This is also a n
advantage of using pivot tables.
3. Value: This is the data you are interested in aggregating. Expand the three-dot menu on
this column to set the aggregation type (e.g. count, Sum, Average, Min etc.). Typical
examples:
a. Count: Person References,
b. Sum: Pay Code Values
c. Average: Age
Note: The value function defaults to count, so ensure to update it correctly if another
function is required, e.g. sum or max.

5. FAQ and Avoiding Common Issues
This section contains some general advice on avoiding common issues when building Insight
reports.
5.1. How do I get the most recent record out of a view?
Some views (example training, leave, absences, etc.), have multiple records per employee and
often you want to report on the most recent. A practical example of this would be if some
employees have completed the same training course twice (therefore, there are two rows of data
in the training log view for the same employee and course code ), and you want to report on the
latest records only.
The basic approach is to use the training start date in the report and create a calculated column
to return the max start date. Then, filter the report to only return rows where the start date column
= max start date. See the steps below for further detail on this approach:

te. Then, filter the report to only return rows where the start date column
= max start date. See the steps below for further detail on this approach: 1. Create the report, making sure to include the required data columns (in this example,
training record start date and course code).
2. Add a calculated column to get the max start date (in this example, it could be named
neweststartdate). For example, the below calculation uses the max SQL function to return
the latest start date based on employee, course code:
max (TRCI_TRAINING_LOG.START_DATE) over (PARTITION by
TRCI_TRAINING_LOG.PERSON_REFERENCE, TRCI_TRAINING_LOG.COURSE_CODE)
At this stage, multiple rows will still be returned for each employee.
3. To only return the latest record, use the Filter by Column toggle to only return rows where
start date = neweststartdate

5.2. Error caused by dividing by zero
When using division in a calculation, if the data ever results in the divisor being 0, this will result in
an error during report execution. For example: ‘ORA-01476: divisor is equal to zero’
A simple division calculation can cause this error, for example:
CTCI_PERSON_BALANCES.CURRENT_BOOKED/CTCI_PERSON_BALANCES.CURRENT_BALANCE*100
To avoid this error, it is recommended to update the calculation, so it only attempts the division

ENT_BOOKED/CTCI_PERSON_BALANCES.CURRENT_BALANCE*100
To avoid this error, it is recommended to update the calculation, so it only attempts the division when the divisor is not 0. Therefore, the example above could be updated as follows:
CASE WHEN CTCI_PERSON_BALANCES.CURRENT_BALANCE !=
0 THEN CTCI_PERSON_BALANCES.CURRENT_BOOKED/CTCI_PERSON_BALANCES.CURRENT_BALANCE*10
0 ELSE 0 END
5.3. Filter Prompts and Calculation
When you use a filter prompt (e.g. date effective) and reference in it in a calculation, this results in
a dependency on the filter within the calc ulation. It is recommended not to change the name of
the filter prompt or delete it without first removing it from the calculation, as this can cause errors.
If you want to rename or replace the filter, ensure to add the filter prompt back into the calculation
again.
5.4. Referencing calculation in other calculations
Referencing a calculation within another calculation introduces a dependency. For example, Calc
A is referenced in Calc B, and you want to remove or rename Calc A. Best practice would be to
remove the references to Calc A in Calc B , before making an y amendments to Calc A. You can
reintroduce the references as necessary, after making the amendments.

5.5. Pivots and Row Counts
The row settings in an Insight report allow you to set a max of 100,000 rows. For pivot reports, the max record count is the flat no. of data rows that are used to create the pivot table . This record
count is displayed on screen when you run the report . The record count does not refer to the
number of rows you are seeing in the pivot table; this will be less than the record count.

If you are writing a pivot table and hit 100,000 records, be aware that these are the only rows that
will be used in your calculation. For example, if there are 110,000 rows the additional 10,000 will
not be reflected, it is recommended to keep the record count under 100,000.
5.6. Outer joins on reports
For performance reasons, reports written in Insight by default do not use outer joins by default.
This means if a report uses more than one view (e.g. Views A, B, C) a matching record will need to
exist on each view, else that row will not return on the reports.
If necessary, outer join issues can be avoided by using a relevant function where available. This is
also a useful approach if you’re reporting from a view that does not have a join to the view that

employee name or email address).

1.2. What is Insight?
Insight is an in-application reporting tool to help employees and managers gain perspective on their business operations. It encompasses the process of transforming your People XD
data into reportable datasets and visualising that data into reports, graphs and tables that
expose valuable insights.
XD Insight is about visualising, understanding, and acting on data and provides users with
the following features:
• A reporting homepage to view recent reports that you have created, view reports
that have been shared with you, have a full searchable l ist of all reports you have
access to, Users can view, edit, and clone reports with the ability to launch the Create
Report Wizard.
• Users can create standard listing reports or cross tab reports. A report can be created
from the various areas that are available to the user. E.g. Recruitment, Payroll, etc.
The user can then select the fields they want as part of that report from the
designated views within that area. If applicable, a user can edit, print, or export the
report to excel.

possible to search fields and remove from the visual field list. The grid can be

• Reports can be filtered based on columns that are part of the reporting area.
Prompting can also be activated so a user can enter a value when a report is being

• Reports can be shared in read only mode to a list of users available in the sharing

2.2. Gender Pay Gap Guidance
XD Insight calculates the Gender Pay Gap using a number of functions and data fields from the
PACI_APPOINTMENT_HISTORY table. The Gender Pay Gap calculations can be used on any UK or
Irish payroll within People XD.
For the calculations, the functions use the max period in the specified period range for the
employee’s last pay group’s pay frequency for Hourly Pay.
Bonus are calculated by specifying the Pay Period ranges for the Start Period and End Period.
2.2.1. Hourly Pay
All employees who were paid their usual full pay in their pay period that included the snapshot
date.
2.2.2. Bonus Pay
Bonuses paid to each relevant employee (including full pay relevant employees) in the 12 months
to the snapshot date.

2.3. CEO vs Employee Pay Gap (UK Only)
Executive pay ratio reporting requires companies to identify employees’ average pay across
different quartiles in comparison to the CEO’s pay.

K Only)
Executive pay ratio reporting requires companies to identify employees’ average pay across
different quartiles in comparison to the CEO’s pay. 2.3.1. Calculating the CEO Pay Ratio
To calculate each ratio, divide the CEO’s remuneration by that of the employee at each percentile.
For example, the CEO’s STFR is 3,200,000 and the remuneration of the employees at the 25th, 50th
and 75th percentiles are 20,000, 40,000 and 100,000, respectively. Therefore, the ratios to report
are 160:1, 80:1 and 32:1. In this example, it would take 160 years for a worker at the 25th percentile
to earn the amount that the CEO earns in a single year.
2.3.2. Calculating the Figures
The CEO’s remuneration figure must be the latest Single Total Figure of Remuneration (STFR),
which is already part of the directors’ report, calculated according to existing regulations. Where
there has been a change of CEO during the year, the total pay, and benefits paid to each post
holder must be considered (but not their pay and benefits from other roles held during the year).
To calculate each ratio, divide the CEO’s remuneration by that of the employee at each percentile .

1.2. What are iCues?
iCues are intelligent trigger-based reports, designed to proactively send alerts to stakeholders,
when certain thresholds are breached/events are occurring.
Examples of how iCues could be used include:

ed to proactively send alerts to stakeholders,
when certain thresholds are breached/events are occurring.
Examples of how iCues could be used include: • Alert a manager when one of their employees is approaching the sick leave threshold.
• Alert a manager of overlapping leave.
• Alert an HRD when attrition rates spike.
• Alert the FD when costs are increasing.
• Alert an employee when they have a large annual leave balance remaining.
• Alert an employee/manager of an important date e.g. anniversary, birthday etc.
The foundation for an iCue is an intelligent report built in Insight or downloaded from the Report
Store, which is used to trigger a notification to a specified recipient.
• The report includes complex calculations that are used to determine when these
thresholds are breached, or events are about to occur.
• PeopleXD runs the iCue report on a specified frequency (daily/weekly/monthly).
• Pre-configured alerts can be sent to a specified recipient via a number of methods
o Feed alerts from Access button (only available in PeopleXD Evo)
o Notification Centre or iCue widget.
o Email
o Mobile App Alerts (Home screen)

Interface reports are intended to be consumed by a 3rd party application. They run on a scheduled
basis, producing a flat delimited file which is then encrypted and sent via SFTP to destination
locations. For example, you might want to take the data in the Insight report, and make it available
to another program, in which you want to manipulate the data.

configuration is required to set up the interface, such as t he file generation, name, headers,
scheduling etc.

files to be uploaded to.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the available XD Payroll functions in
Insight reports.
1.2. XD Functions Overview
XD functions are standard functions built into Insight. They perform operations using the provided
parameters based on XD data fields (e.g. get email address, active pension scheme appointment
data etc.). XD functions enable you to define logical columns returning the data without needing
knowledge of the underlying data or internal logic.
XD Functions are used in the following scenarios:
1. Abstract some of the logic for complex operations and data retrieval.
2. Getting data that may not accessible from the views in your report (for example, employee
name or email address).
Note: This guide is for reference purposes; information on how to use functions and build

n your report (for example, employee
name or email address).
Note: This guide is for reference purposes; information on how to use functions and build reports is not included.
Note: To avoid complexity and improve performance, i t is recommended to get data
directly from data views where possible. Before using functions, check to see if the desired
information can be returned through the standard views and columns.
Note:
• A function isn’t capable of retrieving more than one information; that means if you have
two different data matching the parameters, the result will be either null or one of
them.
• You will need data access to be granted for the function to return a result, for example
Payroll functions would only return results for the pay groups you have access to.

1 Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Predictive Analytics screen
in Insight, to configure the Leavers Analytic algorithm. This includes
• How to configure the algorithm.
• How to create a report using the algorithm.

in Insight, to configure the Leavers Analytic algorithm. This includes
• How to configure the algorithm.
• How to create a report using the algorithm. 1.2. What are Predictive Analytics and what is the Leaver Algorithm?
The Predictive Analytics tool enables your organisation to use your own data to create reports
which discover key profile/employee attributes when employees leave.
• This powerful tool generates a risk score for current employees by analysing leavers in a
selected date range.
• This risk score can be used to predict potential future retention risks.
For example, you can analyse all your leavers in 2018 and use this data to help identify any
potential leavers based on common attributes.

2.1. Configure the Leaver Algorithm
You must configure the leaver algorithm to identify which leavers you wan t to analyse and what
employee / contract attributes should be taken into account.
For example: Analyse all leavers in 2018 where the employee resigned.
Follow these steps to configure the leaver algorithm:
1. Navigate to the Insight dashboard.
2. Click the Predictive Configuration tab.
3. Enter the algorithm parameters:
a. Select Leavers from the Prediction Type drop-down menu.

2.2. Report on the Leaver Score
Follow these steps to create a report to view the results of the analysis i.e. the employee Risk Score. 1. Navigate to the Insight dashboard
2. Click the Home tab.
3. Expand the actions drop-down menu and click Create Report.
4. Select Table as the type of report to create.
5. Enter a Name.
6. Click OK.
7. Add the required columns:
a. Ensure to add Leaver Score. This is the risk score calculated for the individual
employees.
Note: You must run predictions at least once in order to generate a risk score.
• The predictions will automatically re-run every 30 days from the last run date.

1.1. Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the available XD Recruitment functions

1.2. XD Functions Overview
XD functions are standard functions built into Insight. They perform operations using the
provided parameters based on XD data fields (e.g. get email address, active pension scheme
appointment data etc.). XD functions enable you to define logical columns returning the data
without needing knowledge of the underlying data or internal logic.
XD Functions are used in the following scenarios:
1. Abstract some of the logic for complex operations and data retrieval.
2. Getting data that may not be accessible from the views in your report (for example,
employee name or email address).
Note: This guide is for reference purposes; information on how to use functions and
build reports is not included.
Note: To avoid complexity and improve performance, it is recommended to get data
directly from data views where possible. Before using functions, check to see if the desired
information can be returned through the standard views and columns.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This document provides guidance on how to setup and use the Report Store in Insight. This

1.2. What is the Report Store?
The Report Store is a central repository of pre-configured reports, similar to an ‘app store’. These
reports are created by other users in the PeopleXD community and uploaded to the cloud. You
can:
• Browse the reports.
• Download reports for use on your own instance of PeopleXD.

users in the PeopleXD community and uploaded to the cloud. You

These are essentially report templates. They do not contain any data i.e. the template includes the
fields, calculations, filters, formatting etc used to create the report. However, if you download this
and run on your environment, the report data will reflect your own organisation’s data and your
own designated access to data on PeopleXD. You can even choose to edit the downloaded report
to further suit your own requirements.
Who can download reports?
Once you have access to the Report Store, you can browse the store and download any reports
you require. You can then run these in your version of Insight and edit these as required.

1.2. XD Functions Overview XD functions are standard functions built into Insight. They perform operations using the provided
parameters based on XD data fields (e.g. get email address, active pension scheme appointment
data etc.). XD functions enable you to define logical columns returning the data without needing
knowledge of the underlying data or internal logic.
XD Functions are used in the following scenarios:
1. Abstract some of the logic for complex operations and data retrieval.
2. Getting data that may not accessible from the views in your report (for example, employee
name or email address).
Note:
• Some functions are only used for legacy report import purposes.
• To avoid complexity and improve performance, it is recommended to get data directly
from data views where possible. Before using functions, check to see if the desired
information can be returned through the standard views and columns.
• Ensure you use the Master table for the business area in your report. This will ensure
you have maximum visibility of views and data for the business area.
• Some functions may not support multi-post sites, these are not included in this guide.

3. General Guidelines
3.1. Security
Some XD functions require security access, depending on the area (e.g. HR system access, pay
user, user defined fields access etc.). If you are missing the required permissions, the column may
display without data.
For example, if a HR report contains a payroll function in a calculated column, and you only have
access to 50% of the employees in payroll, that column will be blank for those employees who you
do not have access to, but will be populated for the other 50%.

3. Data Mapping
3.1. Overview
You need to map your PeopleXD data for it to appear in People Analytics and be categorised appropriately. This is a required step, because People Analytics uses a set of standardised terms,
attributes, and metrics (e.g. Voluntary Resignation vs Involuntary Resignation) that relate, but do
not match the customer definable reference lists held within PeopleXD.
To ensure that data displays correctly in People Analytics, certain fields need to be mapped in
PeopleXD. The field types that can be mapped are detailed in the following sections.
3.1.1. Exit Type
All PeopleXD leaving reasons need to map to the following Exit Types in People Analytics:
• Resignation
• Retirement
• Termination
• Reduction in Force
• Disability Exit
• Maternity Exit
If a leaving reason is unmapped, it is by default mapped to Uncategorised.
3.1.2. Pay Types
PeopleXD pay code reference data needs to map to the following Pay Types in People Analytics:
• Agency Cost
• Base Pay

4. Select a default currency from the Select Default Currency dropdown. Your solution will
now show in the default currency.
4.3. Currency Rates
4.3.1. Overview
When converting values to a single currency, the solution uses a process called constant
currency. This means that only one exchange rate (per currency) is used for a calculation, even if
it spans multiple periods. The exchange rates used are based on the last day of the selected
period in the Time picker.

sed for a calculation, even if
it spans multiple periods. The exchange rates used are based on the last day of the selected
period in the Time picker. The constant currency method allows for effective analysis of the change in costs over time. If a
varying exchange rate were used, then differences in values could be caused by different rates of
exchange. These fluctuations would be invisible in the analysis as they are applied to values prior
to them being displayed. Using constant currency ensures that trends, such as changes in costs
or the slope of a trend line, are represented using a common exchange factor. This approach
provides a clearer and more reliable view of cost changes between periods.
Note: By default, the solution’s currency is set to GBP.

4.3. Currency Rates
4.3.1. Overview
When converting values to a single currency, the solution uses a process called constant
currency. This means that only one exchange rate (per currency) is used for a calculation, even if
it spans multiple periods. The exchange rates used are based on the last day of the selected
period in the Time picker.
The constant currency method allows for effective analysis of the change in costs over time. If a
varying exchange rate were used, then differences in values could be caused by different rates of
exchange. These fluctuations would be invisible in the analysis as they are applied to values prior
to them being displayed. Using constant currency ensures that trends, such as changes in costs
or the slope of a trend line, are represented using a common exchange factor. This approach
provides a clearer and more reliable view of cost changes between periods.

PeopleXD. People Analytics is an embedded solution that gives you access to instant, actionable
people insights with in-built metrics and off-the-shelf guidebooks.

4. Guidebooks
4.1. Overview The Guidebook area is where you can view prebuilt out-of-the-box People Analytics dashboards.
The content within a guidebook is a collection of related topics and analyses that provide insight
into business questions and workforce data.
The Guidebooks available are:
• Standard Dashboards
• People Management
• Payroll
• Time & Attendance
• Manager Dashboard
• Data Validation
4.2. Topics
Once you click into a Guidebook, you will see a list of related topics. Topics are categories used to
organise a collection of analyses. Each topic contains at least one analysis.
4.3. Analyses
The analyses in the topics of the Guidebooks are designed to answer complex business
questions by telling viewers a story with data visualisations. A typical analysis is made up of
business questions (headers), charts, text, and links to other analyses.

How accurate are the responses provided by Copilot?
Copilot always tries to give the best answer it can, using the context that it has available
to it i.e. your question; the data in the large language model (LLM) and the data in
PeopleXD that it has access to (if you use a PeopleXD Skill). It then uses these collectively
to respond with how it can best meet the user’s intent.
To get the most accurate responses from Copilot, be specific and provide context in
your question. Clear, detailed prompts help the model understand exactly what you're
looking for. If you’re unsure of the answer provided, you can ask Copilot to tell you how
it sourced that answer.
Will Copilot always give me the same answer?
Not necessarily. Copilot is powered by a large language model (LLM) that mimics how a
human brain works and responds based on the available context. It therefore may
respond differently to the same or similar questions, just as a human brain would.

• Their assessment scores.

GDPR gives individuals the right to ask organisations to delete their personal data. In the
scenario where a candidate has registered on an organisation’s website e.g. Careers Portal, or
has submitted an application but been unsuccessful, they may request the right to be forgotten.
The Right To Be Forgotten feature in PeopleXD Recruitment allows users to action this request by

ccessful, they may request the right to be forgotten.

address. Alternatively, click OK to view all available candidates.

stages of the recruitment process. For example, the candidate’s name, address information, and
contact details can be hidden.

Organisations require the right people, with the right skills in the right jobs at the right time.
Recruitment is critical to this goal. To remain competitive in the area of recruitment, organisations

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This guide gives an overview of the integration between PeopleXD Recruitment & DocuSign
eSignatures. This integration:
• Allows an organisation to create pre-defined envelopes that can contain several different

leXD Recruitment & DocuSign
eSignatures. This integration:
• Allows an organisation to create pre-defined envelopes that can contain several different documents that a user can select from PeopleXD without the need start a document from
scratch or store documents locally or on shared drives.
• Allows PeopleXD data to be passed up in the form of merged fields which populate s the
document template with key information relating to the candidate. Name, start date,
salary, job title
• Allows as many templates to be created in Docusign as required.
1.2. DocuSign Integration Overview
The integration allows a user within PeopleXD Recruitment to send a Document to a candidate
that they can review and sign via DocuSign e.g. an NDA or a Contract of Employment to a successful
applicant.

DocuSign. However all DocuSign envelop es initiated within PeopleXD are sent from the one
customer defined account within DocuSign e.g. hr@abcsolutions.com or
johndoe@abcsolutions.com. Users initiating the process from P eopleXD are logged into this
DocuSign account in a restricted preview and send mode.

1.2. What are 360 Reviews
360 reviews are feedback opportunities that enable a group of colleagues to provide feedback on
an employee’s performance and facilitate continuous evaluation.
The feedback is generally asked for by the manager to whom the employee reports into.
Colleagues who participate in the 360 usually include the persons line manager, several peers,
reporting staff, and functional managers with whom the employee works regularly with.
The goal of the feedback is to provide a balanced view to an employee of how others view his or
her contribution and performance in areas such as leadership, teamwork, interpersonal,
communication, management, contribution, work habits, interpersonal interaction, accountability,
vision and more, depending on the employee's job.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this guide is to outline the steps needed to create and set up 360 reviews on the
talent dashboard to be assigned to employees and managers for feedback.
1.2. What are 360 Reviews?
360 reviews are feedback opportunities that enable a group of colleagues to provide feedback on
an employee’s performance and facilitate continuous evaluation. Talent management
administrators can create 360 review questionnaires and assign these either to all employees
across the organisation or to employees that belong to a specific organisational group, e.g. all
employees in Division A. Employees can select from a list of the colleag ues, within their defined
organisational group, and request that they provide feedback for them, using the assigned 360
review form.
The feedback is generally asked for by the manager to whom the employee reports into.

The feedback is generally asked for by the manager to whom the employee reports into. Colleagues who participate in the 36 0 usually include the persons line manager, several peers,
reporting staff, and functional managers with whom the employee works regularly with.
The goal of the feedback is to provide a balanced view to an employee of how others view his or
her contributi on and performance in areas such as leadership, teamwork, interpersonal,
communication, management, contribution, work habits, interpersonal interaction, accountability,
vision and more, depending on the employee's job.
Key characteristics of the 360 review include:
• Availability to assign and request feedback for a specific period.
• Visibility of feedback can be set for HR, the manager and the employee ; therefore
controlling who has access to review submitted feedback.
• The anonymity of feedback can be set for HR, the manager and the employee hiding the
name of the employee who provides feedback.
• Review questionnaires can be created unique to each review, with the facility to define a
number of mandatory or optional questions using multiple choice & free text style
answers.

1.3. What are Peer Reviews
The Peer Review functionality allows a manager to send a review questionnaire to other employees
in the organisation and to request feedback from their team members . Talent management
administrators can create peer review questionnaires and assign these either to all man agers
across the entire organisation or to managers that belong to a specific organisational group , e.g.
all managers in Division A.
Key characteristics of the peer review include:
• The availability to assign and request feedback for a specific period.
• The visibility of feedback can be restricted for either HR, the manager or both.

helps organisations retain high performers.

The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the appraisals functionality as
an employee and a manager. This is broken down into three areas:
1. Employee Appraisals
2. Employee Talent Profile
3. Manager Appraisals
This guide includes how to navigate the dashboards and widgets available to Portal users for
Talent.
Note: This guide does not include:
• Steps on how to use objectives.
• Steps on how to use competencies.
• Steps on other lesser used features in the Talent module.
• Configuration of appraisals.

Calibration
In appraisal calibration, you apply a company standard when reviewing a manager’s direct reports’
performance at work.
The calibration screen details what the expectations are for appraisals, and compares how
employees are performing against expectations. It provides a graph when populated, showing
three categories:
1. Below Expectations
2. Meets Expectations
3. Exceeds Expectations

1.2. What are competencies
A ‘competency framework’ is a structure that sets out and defines each individual competency (i.e.
personal attributes or behaviours) that an employee has.
Individuals must have, or must acquire, these competencies to perform effectively at work.

2.2.4. General Competencies

1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This document provides an Admin user with configuration steps on how to build and roll out
Succession Plans to an organisations management structure within the XD Talent Management
product suite. Through using this document users gain an understanding on how to impl ement
this feature to meet an organisation's talent strategy. This can be used in conjunction with other
features within the XD Talent Management suite to meet an organisations talent strategy.

1.2. What is Succession Planning? Succession planning is the process of identifying and developing potential future leaders and senior
managers, as well as individuals, to fill business -critical roles. The aim is to be able to fill key roles
effectively if a current post holder leaves the organisation. (CIPD, 2020)
Within this functionality in XD Talent Management, users h ave the ability to find successors,
identify key positions and build succession profiles. Succession Planning allows the organisation
to ensure leadership continuity, retain & develop knowledge & intellectual capital for the future
and encourage individual employee growth and developme nt. It also helps set career objectives
and determine appropriate educational and developmental programs to further develop the skills
required to achieve short term and long term career objectives.

standard configuration details.

A badge can be created for an employee to allow automatic tracking of their clockings via a device(s). Badges can be created manually via the WFM Admin Dashboard or in Bulk via the Data
Migration tool, in the Administrator Dashboard. This guide will walk you through the processes of
managing an employee’s badge.
The guide will cover:

Note: Once a badge number is issued, it cannot be assigned to another staff member. A
person can only have one active badge at a time. They can have multiple badge numbers
assigned to them but only one can be Active, which must have a valid issue date.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Balances are a key element of the PeopleXD WFM system allowing the user the flexibility to
monitor many situations such as Annual Leave, Time in Lieu, Flexi Time, Study Leave, Parental
Leave, Sick Leave and Holiday Entitlement Accrual for temporary workers.
PeopleXD WFM allows any number of balances to be set up. Each balance will have its own rules.
• What is to happen when a balance entitlement is exceeded?

Balances are comprised of ‘Entitlements’ where are assigned to employees. As staff record and
request leave the taken and booked are update which are in turn subtracted from the person’s
entitlement balances remaining including and excluding booked values.
The purpose of this guide is to show how to manage Balances and their configuration to aid
Administrators complete their day-to-day tasks and explain the various configuration screens.
1.2. Terminology
Balances are assigned to employees and/or employee appointments. Balances are comprised of
Set-up (Parameters/Calendars etc...), Entitlements (Balance Elements), Pay code/hours (taken and
booked transactions), Adjustments (manual override) and Period Ends (balance period close
downs)

1.2.2. Pay Codes
Within PeopleXD Pay/Time codes are required to operate the balances where each pay code
represents a leave or absence type (e.g. 3400 Annual Leave). The appropriate pay code(s) are
attached to the various ‘affecting’ elements of a balance, example may include:
• Annual Leave - Annual Leave pay code is assigned to the ‘Taken’ element
• Parental Leave - Parental Leave pay code is assigned to the ‘Taken’ element
• Time in Lieu - Time in Lieu Worked & Taken codes are assigned to the ‘Balance’ element
Any number of pay codes can be linked to a balance. Every time a new leave pay code is set up it
must be considered if the particular pay code needs to be assigned within the balance
configuration.

1.2.3. Balance Parameters
Balances must be set up with a unique balance code and description. The balance parameters required certain parameters/rules to be configured to control how the balance will operate after
been assigned to employees, examples include:
• What is the balance code and the description to describe the balance?

• What elements are affected by the pay codes?

• Is the balance based on a rolling period or a fixed calendar
1.2.4. Balance Calendars
The balance duration e.g. Annual Leave calendar year, flexitime monthly or 4 weekly. All balances
require their own calendars. The calendar specifies the start and end dates of each balance
period. In addition, when creating the calendar, you can impose any required restrictions that are
required, for example you might want to restrict the number of hours that are ‘Carried Forward’
into the next flexitime accounting period.

1.2. Bank Holiday Rule Considerations
An hour for hour premium payment or time off in lieu can be generated for hours worked on
bank holidays by employees. This is configured to be in line with the organisations Bank Holiday
working rules. This feature is compatible with the retail calculation only.

2.2.2. Approve or Reject employees’ leave requests in bulk
The Multi-Select toggle allows you to filter leave requests by Pay Code and Status which can then
be approved or rejected in bulk. To do this:

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Due to requests from several customers to load absences, and work patterns/shifts/schedules into
Workforce Management from 3rd party systems, new integration options are required to satisfy
these requirements. The requirements from these customers are varied, so the interface has been
designed to cater for all requirements raised to date E.g.
• Load absences into WFM for reporting purposes
• Load absences into WFM to enable the calculation of statutory and occupational absence
payments in PeopleXD Payroll
• Load work schedules into WFM for employees that have absences recorded against them
to ensure that the absence calculations are based on the correct working patterns, and to
ensure that the correct work schedules are in WFM to facilitate the recording of leave or
the calculation of timesheets based on clocking transactions recorded by employees

3. Calculation of Flexitime
Based on the employee’s clockings, the total time in work is calculated. This total time is then
compared against the default hours on the work pattern. If the total exceeds the default hours,
the difference is written at the positive flexitime pay code. If the total is less than the default
hours, the different is written at the negative flexitime pay code.
Any time worked in a ‘lapsed’ time frame does not contribute towards the total time in work.
Refer to the sample clockings below, which are based on the work pattern on the previous page.
• Monday: Worked a standard day – 8 hours basic.
• Tuesday: Worked 8.30 hours – giving 30 minutes positive flexitime.

• Thursday: Worked 8.30 hours, but 30 minutes is in a Lapsed time frame (6am – 8am) - this
30mins is generated as overtime based on out pattern.
o Also, the person did not clock out for lunch, so the 30-minute break plus the 1hr
penalty (specified on the pattern) is also deducted. So, total time in work = 6 hours,
giving 2 hours negative flexitime.
• Friday: The Employee Started & Finished as normal but left for 15 minutes during the core

negative flexitime.

5.5. Generate Timesheet Processing and Employee not on Payroll
In previous versions of the Generate Timesheets to payroll, the system stopped processing for
future dated employees in WFM that had not been onboarded into payroll.
From V28 the stop has been altered to ‘warn’ where future date employee exists and no attendance
has been recorded (i.e. start date is after the end of the current WFM period)
Examples of Employee Not on Payroll:
• If employees are starting in the future (i.e start date later than the end of the period being
processed)
• If there are no attendance hours entered for the period.
• Issuing of a warning message to allow the generate timesheet process to continue.
• Warning message text “Warning - No Employee record on Payroll (Future new starter)
Additional Considerations
• Work Group is set to ‘Live’ and marked as Generate Timesheets.
• Employee is not set as non-generate timesheets at person level.
• If future dated employees have attendance recorded in the period being closed, the
existing stop process remains.

1.3. What is the Parallel Mode?
Generate Timesheets in Parallel Mode. As mentioned in the previous section, Generate Timesheets has been moved from the back office
to Portal. In order to support the transition, the portal version of Generate Timesheets runs a
parallel mode to support the re-generation of a previously transferred period that was completed
via the back office.
The features within the Parallel Mode are the following:
• WFM company: Parallel Mode can be enabled per WFM company. If a client has more
than one company using Portal, the parallel mode can be run separately for each.
• Validation: Parallel mode is run to validate those calendars or periods which have
previously been migrated to show that there are no discrepancies found.
• Leavers: Parallel Transfers do not impact the live mode. Employees are not marked as
leavers.
• Analysis and Review: Parallel Run details are stored into backup tables for analysis and
review. For further information see Tables for Parallel Run.

• Insight reporting and analysis: This includes listings of the hours transferred in parallel
mode. Exceptions reports are generated on the parallel lists and are compared

nd analysis: This includes listings of the hours transferred in parallel
mode. Exceptions reports are generated on the parallel lists and are compared highlighting differences between the back-office run and portal runs.

1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this guide is to introduce Geofencing Clocking solution and to explain the

1.2. What is Geofencing?
Geofencing is a virtual defined boundary which sets a perimeter, or geofence, around a specific
location such as an office or store.
You define the Geofence when you specify:
• The latitude and longitude co-ordinates of the point of interest.
• The required radius in meters of the geofence.
Once the clocking app on a device has been activated and is within the Geofence it allows the
user to clock in and clock out.
By using Geofencing, the system can stop employees from clocking in when they are outside the
allowed radius or Geofence.
The accuracy of the location reported depends on the following factors:
• The phone being used (i.e., GPS chip, model/operating system)
Note: The Geofence solution only applies to clocking via the Native App. It does not apply

e phone being used (i.e., GPS chip, model/operating system)

• Cellular network
• Wi-Fi network
• Battery saving mode on/off
• Weather
• Interference with the device such as trees etc.
In general, the radius of the Geofence should be wide enough to compensate for these factors.
Note: It is usually recommended that the minimum size of the geofence is 80 metres.

The authentication for clockings is based on oAuth 2 Client Credentials. To authenticate,

access token is provided on successful authentication. This access token is required for each

either approve or reject it, before it is an official absence.
• An Absence can be directly entered on an employee record, by a manager.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this guide is to explain the Irish Annual Leave Carryover legislation introduced in
January 2024 and a provide a step-by-step guide to configuring this in PeopleXD.
The guide will cover:
• An overview of the legislation
• Setting a balance code to use this legislation
• An example of the legislation in use
1.2. Legislation Overview
The Irish Civil Service Annual Leave Carryover was introduced in part of the circular Annual
Leave in the Civil Service and is part of the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 (as
amended) and Section 86(1) of the Workplace Relations Act 2015.
In PeopleXD Workforce Management it is Part 3: Carryover of Annual Leave that is relevant
and that this feature covers.
For the purposes of this legislation and feature annual leave is divided into two categories,

ual Leave that is relevant
and that this feature covers.
For the purposes of this legislation and feature annual leave is divided into two categories, statutory and non-statutory. Unused statutory annual leave is not normally carried over, and if a
specific exception is made for an individual then this need to be handled by a manual
adjustment. The new legislation covers the carryover of unused non-statutory leave. Unused
non-statutory leave should be carried over into the following year and must be used within that
year. This process can repeat each year, allowing for unused non-statutory leave for that year to
be carried over to the following year.
When an individual takes annual leave, the order this is taken is:
1. Statutory annual leave which has been carried over due to exceptional circumstances.
This will need to be managed manually.
2. Any non-statutory annual leave which has been carried over from the previous year.

3. Statutory annual leave entitlement accrued during the current year.
4. Any non-statutory annual leave which has been accrued during the current leave year.

5. Clocking Behaviours
• Kiosk will force the employee to clock out before they can clock into another
appointment.
• When an employee clocks in and log back into the app, at the end of their shift, that
appointment will display and the clock out button will be enabled.
• An employee can't clock in or out in the same minute.
• The app, portal and mobile all share the same clocking parameters, so if an admin sets
the kiosk to register time, then portal and mobile will be set to register time, all three will
behave the same and be consistent.
• When the kiosk is in offline mode, it does not support in/out selection. Users can

register time, all three will
behave the same and be consistent.
• When the kiosk is in offline mode, it does not support in/out selection. Users can still clock, but only the registered time is recorded, without indicating whether it
is an "in" or "out" event. Once the device reconnects and clockings are uploaded
to the database, the appropriate in/out status will be automatically assigned in
WFM.
• PINs are downloaded from the database to the kiosk once per day. If a user
changes their PIN and the kiosk goes offline before the new PINs are
downloaded, the user will not be able to clock using their updated PIN. The
device must be brought back online and the latest PINs downloaded before the
new PIN can be used.

1.1. Timesheet Claims Summary
The following describes a high-level working of Timesheets claims & the approval process.
• Where employees enter timesheets and return to the timesheet claims summary screen
the system automatically sums the hours by the grouping identified and the timesheets
have a saved for later status.
• Where a claim is not submitted for approval e.g. Saved for later, the employee can
continue to enter/maintain timesheet details whereby the summary screen continues to
sum the timesheet entries by the defined grouping.
• Once an employee submits a timesheet claim, the claim is formed and then enters the
workflow approval process.
• Where claims are in the workflow approval process, the claim and its transactions cannot
be edited.

The timesheet status e.g. Submitted, Approved has an impact where timesheets have been
entered into the submission/approval process.

2.5. Unprocessed Claims and Period End Where a period end occurs, the generate timesheet program will only transfer timesheet claims
where final approval has been completed.
What happens where claims have not reached final payment?
• Employees have timesheet claims that are ‘Saved for Later’ and never submitted them.
• Manager fails to approve timesheet claims before the period end.
• Manager has rejected claims and the employee failed to action the claim.
As part of the period end process any claims that have not reached final approval are
automatically carried forward to the next period so that the claims are not lost, and the relevant
roles can action them as required e.g. so that employee can submit that “saved for later” claim
for the manager to approve.
While the claims are brought forward to the next period the actual dates of the claim are
reflective of the period, they were recorded in. The dates are displayed below the person’s name

picked up in the next period?

Ticking this option will mean that any absence starting before the 1st anniversary of the
employee's start date will be ignored when calculating occupational sick. Occupational sick will
only be calculated on the first new absence after the anniversary date.

2.2. First Anniversary Start/End Month
These settings allow you to pro-rata Occupational Sick entitlement from the first anniversary of
the employee’s start date until the end of the current sick year.
You can configure how many months you wish the anniversary date to fall on, for most people
using this option this will be a start month of 12 and an end month of 23.99. This will configure
the system to calculate the occupational entitlement from the first-year anniversary of the start
to the end of the absence year, but not to pro-rata for more than one year.
If you were to pro-rate up until three years, you would enter a start month of 12 and an end
month of 35.99.

1.2. Overview of Feature Overlapping Warnings display during the actioning of employee Leave Requests, alerting the
approver at the approval/rejection stage. This feature alerts approvers if a Leave Request overlaps
with:
• An absence or approved Leave Request for another employee in the approver’s remit.
• An un-actioned request for another employee in the approver’s remit.
• A previously rejected request for the same employee.
For further information on general Leave Requests, view Leave Requests & Absence user guide on
CoreHR University.
Note:
• This feature provides a warning to the approver only, to be taken into consideration.
However, does not prevent the approver from approving/rejecting the Leave Request.
• Warnings for ‘Sick’ absence are only displayed when it is submitted for manager
approval, not when it is directly entered on the employee record. This means that the
warnings are only triggered if the absence request goes through an approval process.
Therefore, warnings are not triggered if absence is directly e ntered for the employee
without approvals.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This document outlines how to access and manage the Period Closure screen. The screen
enables Administrators to pre-book company closure periods for example, Christmas or a
summer shutdown and automatically deduct the relevant leave from staff entitlements.
Benefits include:
• Pre-booking of leave for closure periods ensures the required days/hours are
automatically deducted from the staff entitlements.
• Stops staff from over-booking or forgetting to keep days/hours for closure periods.
• Staff can see the impact of the closure booking on the leave entitlements.
• The closure period automatically validates to employees working schedules & public
holidays determining the number of days/hours required.

tlements.
• The closure period automatically validates to employees working schedules & public
holidays determining the number of days/hours required. • Where staff change working schedules the booking days/hour are automatically
updated.
• The closure period will be reflective of Joiners (new employees), Leaves (employee that
leave before the closure period).
• Where required staff can be paid in advance for full periods of leave such as 2 weeks
summer closure.
1.2. How to access the Period Closure Screen
The Period Closure Screen is menu security driven, see section 6.1 Importing Menu Options for
further guidance, and once enabled the screen can be found in the WFM Admin Dashboard.
1. Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.
Note: The following preconditions need to be met for the roll out of period closures:

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Pro Rata Length of Service Increments
functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. This includes:
• What is Pro Rata Length of Service Increments and when is it used?
• Detailed guidance on the configuration options within Pro Rata Length of Service Increments.
1.2. What is Pro Rata Length of Service Increments?
The Pro Rata Length of Service Increments functionality makes it possible to pro rata anniversary-based
length of service increments.

vice Increments?
The Pro Rata Length of Service Increments functionality makes it possible to pro rata anniversary-based
length of service increments. The service increment calculation, to determine the number of additional days awarded, can be based
on:
• Dates (days)
• Weeks
• Months
Therefore, the increment calculation takes the date s, weeks, or months , between the employee’ s
anniversary date and the end of the annual leave year into consideration.
For example, where the increment calculation is configured as ‘days’ based, this instructs the system to
calculate the service increment from the start of the year , to the date im mediately before the service
date. To do this, the system:
• Adds the full -service increment entitlement, then deducts the part of the year (days) to be
excluded from the additional days awarded.
• Applies the employee’s FTE to the remainder.
• Adds to the employee’s opening entitlement.
• Rounds the result, based on the Rounding Rule specified at the balance level.
Note:
If an employee is leaving an organisation, this also impacts their service increment.

• Part year excluded, is 5 months (from January 1st to June 1st)
• Excluded value = 0.8333 days (2 days / 12 * 5)
• 2 days – 0.8333 days = 1.1667
• Impact remaining by the FTE (1.1667 * 1.00)
• Actual service increase is 1.1667 days
Opening Entitlement: 22.00 days
+1.1667
23.1667 days (rounded, if req.)
New Entitlement: 24* days (or nett 2 days)

not edit.

stating the employee has signed off the RTWI.

RTWI questionnaire is read-only, the manager can not edit.
6. The RTWI will display as Complete for both Manager & Employee.

1.1. Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to explain the Team Calendars screens and allow employees to view
their co-workers’ calendars and managers to view their team members calendars.
The Team Calendars display leave and absence records for an employee’s co-workers and
managers ‘reports to’ team in a calendar format. The managers ‘report to’ team is based on the
organisational hierarchy.
This document covers the following:
• Employees view of Team Calendars (co-workers)
• Managers & Admin view of Team Calendars
• The Team Calendar Configuration Screen

2. The Team Calendar Screen
The Team Calendars screen displays the employees work schedule, leave records and bank
holidays for the pay codes that have been configured to display within the configuration screens.
2.1. Employees viewing Co-Workers Calendars
The Co-Workers Calendars screen displays the work schedule, leave records, bank holidays of the
employees for the date range. You can change the dates being viewed using the date picker or
click the < > buttons to move forward/back, 7 days at the time.
The Co-Workers Calendars is available to Employees on the following screens:
• Employee Calendar (1-Month view)
• Work Week
• Book Time-Off
• My Calendar (12-Month view)
By default, the Co-workers calendars opens based on today date. Where accessed from the Book
Time off widget, the calendar open based on the leave request start date entered.
Note: If Leave Requests have not been actioned, they are highlighted by the colour legend
located at the top of the screen.

Workflow enabled timesheet entry and approval process, supporting employees to enter and
submit timesheets into workflow for managers notification and approval. On final approval, the
timesheets are released to payroll for payment.

for approval.

1.4. Timesheet Claims – Need to Know
The following describes the high-level working of Timesheets claims & the approval process.
• Employees enter timesheets and returns to the timesheet claims summary screen the
system automatically sums the hours by the grouping identified and the claim has a
saved for later status.
• Where a claim is not submitted for approval e.g. Saved for later or Not Submitted, the
employee can continue to enter/maintain timesheet details whereby the summary

is not submitted for approval e.g. Saved for later or Not Submitted, the
employee can continue to enter/maintain timesheet details whereby the summary screen continues to sum the timesheet entries by the defined grouping.
WFM Timesheet Claims - User Guide
Access Limited Distribution Page 10 of 91
• Once an employee submits a timesheet claim, the claim is formed and then enters the
workflow approval process.
• Claims that are in the workflow approval process cannot be edited, this includes
comment at the individual transaction level.
• Workflow is used to notify the relevant roles in the process where an action was taken
e.g. Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Recalled, Retuned to the Employee.
Employees have the option to recall timesheet claims that have not been actioned e.g. approved.
• Timesheet claims can only be actioned from the Timesheet Claims Summary screens.
• Employee timesheets that have a status of Saved for Later or Not Submitted, indicates
the claims have not been submitted into workflow for approval.
• Managers can send back claims to employee for re-work.
• Managers can enter and submit claims on behalf of employees.
• Claims are made up of a Header and Transaction Records e.g. 30-hour claim, could be
made up of 10 hours for 3 days
• Claim Pay Codes support entry in Hours, Values and Units
• Only claims that are approved are sent to payroll for payment.

up of 10 hours for 3 days
• Claim Pay Codes support entry in Hours, Values and Units
• Only claims that are approved are sent to payroll for payment. • Claims that are rejected are closed and not paid.
• Claims that are returned to the employee can be updated and re-submitted by the
employee
• Claims still in workflow (e.g. Submitted, Recommend Approval) are automatically carried

oyee Number, Appointment Id*, Cost Centre, Pay Code, Period
So, where an employee submits a timesheet claim, it’s the unique combination of Header Id, Person, Appointment, Cost Centre, Pay Code & Period that ‘groups’ each individual claim.

1. Overview
One of the main uses of trigger points is to highlight levels or patterns of sickness absence that
require further attention. Using trigger point configuration parameters can be set to determine
when action is needed. The attendance records of individual employees are then monitored
against set criteria. Examples of trigger points may include:
• Cumulative day’s absence in a set period
• Number of spells in a set period
• Combinations of days and spells
• Pattern related
• Notification:
o where Fit note/Certs due
o where staff returning from planned leave
o where there is a change in an employee’s rate of pay relating to long term absence

trigger in the system. A notification can be sent to their email and to the manager self-service/

1. Overview 1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Work Patterns define a daily work schedule. They identify the different work durations that exist
in your organisation and capture the expected working hours for an employee. Selected work
patterns are then used to configure an employee’s shift type. Work patterns are an integral part
of the system linking to multiple areas and can be highly configurable depending on your
organisational requirements.
The purpose of this guide is to show how to manage Work Patterns and explain the various
configurations screens.
Features to Work Patterns include:
• Filters and searches to allow easy access to a specific Work Pattern
• An Active / Non-Active switch
• Copying a Work Pattern
• Reducing menu items to improve user access
• Allowing administrators to show or hide menu items.
