1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Work Groups are groupings of personnel that are used, amongst other purposes, to control
access for supervisors. They also can determine whether a group is to feed timesheets to Payroll
(some groups of workers may clock in and out, but this is for tracking rather than payment
purposes).
Work Groups provide the ability to treat workers who have, otherwise, the same working roster
(Shift Type) in slightly different ways.
For example, one group of workers, might be Computer Data Input personnel who normally
work from home and who, unlike other Day Workers, do not Clock In. These Data Input
personnel could all be put into a new Work Group separate from the normal Day Workers, who

unlike other Day Workers, do not Clock In. These Data Input
personnel could all be put into a new Work Group separate from the normal Day Workers, who Clock In and Out. This new Work Group could be set up to generate a default number of hours
irrespective of whether clockings were received.
The purpose of this guide is to show how to manage Work Groups and explain the various
configuration screens.
2. Work Group Screen
The Work Group screen is where administrators can manage work groups for their organisation.
The screen lists all Work Groups created and shows if they are active or not. This screen can be
used to create new work groups, copy existing work groups and further configure groups to
organisational requirements.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this guide is to explain the WFM Year End Tasks screen which removes the year end guesswork by providing system administrators with a centralised view of the year end tasks
and actions required.
The WFM Year End Tasks screen displays 7 predefined year end tasks which are required to keep
the WFM system up to date. Administrators can also tailor this list, to their organisation
requirements, by adding checklist items to include additional year end tasks.
The administration of year end tasks is an WFM Administrator task.
This document covers how to access the WFM Year End task screen, outlines the predefined year
end tasks and guides you through adding your own year-end tasks to the list.
1.2. Granting access to the WFM Year End Tasks

need to ensure:
• The WFM_Year_End menu profile is enabled for the relevant users or imported to an
existing menu profile. This will enable all menu options & webservices to the user to
access the WFM Year End Tasks functionality. (see Section 6.1 for further guidance)
• Other menu profiles, which may already be enabled but if not are, required to complete
Year End Tasks are:
o WFM_COMPANY_SETTING_ADMIN
o WFM_BANK_HOLIDAY_CONFIG
o WFM_BALANCE_CONFIGURATION
o WFM_BALANCE ADMIN

To support you with the WFM year end process, we have collated the most common questions

Question Answer
When do I run Period Year
End?
Period Year End can only be run when the last week of the
previous period has been closed in WFM, i.e. the first
Monday of January.
For example, if the 31st December falls mid-week, then it is
going to be the following Monday before the process can be
run.
When does Length of Service
(LOS) calculate?
LOS will calculate during the overnight calculation after
Period Year End has been run. As a result, you won’t see LOS
addition until the day after Period Year end has been run.
Do I need to adjust the
Calendars?
Company calendar (and UDCs if in use) must be extended
until the end of the calendar year at minimum, until the end
of the balance year if balance year is a mid-year. It can also
be extended for future years.
When do I set the Carry
forward values?
Carry forward values are set during the previous year’s Year
End process to affect values carrying into the new balance
year.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of Document
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Break Recalculation functionality in Roster after an employee pattern has been amended, either extended or shortened. This includes:
• What is Break Recalculation and when is it used?

1.2. What does Break Recalculation do?
The Break Recalculation feature ensures that the breaks are fully Working Time Directive compliant,
and where possible, the break is scheduled for the most optimal time in a working day. This helps to
avoid staffing shortages.
Therefore, the Break Recalculation feature is present to ensure that employee breaks are scheduled on
the pattern at the most optimal times, guaranteeing:
• WTD (Working Time Directive) compliance
• Company rules compliance
• The avoidance of staffing shortages

If the Break Recalculation functionality is enabled, breaks are recalculated based on the AutoRoster

• The pattern start time is amended ( pattern made longer or
shortened).

This section provides steps to create an Employer Cost Grouping for Roster. Employer Cost Groupings

• The total employee cost to the organisation (employee + employer) is then 86.60.

4.4.1. Costing Types
Costing Types are codes and descriptions used to represent a breakdown of the Employer Costings
types, for example:
• Pension
• NI
• PRSI, etc.
These individual Costing Types are then assigned a Cost Percentage, that are rolled up, to give the
overall Costing Percentage.
• Each individual Costing Type is stored separately on the Planned and Cost underlying tables.
Therefore, through reporting, the overall cost on Employer Pension contributions can be
listed separately from NI charges.
• Each individual Costing Type supports Date Effective changes, for example, a Cost Type may
be increasing from 4% to 6% on the 10-Dec-2019.
It is recommended to create an individual Costing Type per employer costing. This means that each
individual employer costing can then be changed by a date effective, as required, going forward.
For example, if employer costs are NI and Pensions, you should create two Costing Types:
• One for NI
• One for Pensions

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Operational Demand is an enhancement to People XD’s Workforce Management Rostering
feature. It allows an administrator to configure grids displaying various imported and calculated
data and assign these grids to teams. A manager can then see these grids on the roster details
screen to assist in completing staffing requirements for the following week(s).
This guide will explain how to import data, configure the grids, assign the grids, and then view
the data.

2. Unrostered Bookings
2.1. Overview
Unrostered Bookings can be used within Roster to allow users to book leave and absences, in
advance of their schedules being created . Unrostered Bookings are required within Roster
environments as employee ’s schedules may not be created at the time a Leave Request is
submitted, or an absence has been recorded.
Important Considerations:
• You must have a Roster environment before using this functionality.
• For an absence to be picked up as an Unrostered Booking, all days between the start date
and end date of the absence must be rest days.
• An employee is not made aware that a booking is Unrostered when submitting a Leave
Request.
• The employee Absence Roster Contract is not date effective and is applied for all days going
forward once changed via the Unrostered Bookings screen. If an employee changes their
contract hours or days, you must update the employee’s preferences to reflect the change
in contract.

rostered. If required, you can submit the absence directly for the employee on the selected
date.
• Unrostered Bookings do not work in conjunction with entering times on absences.
• If Contract Hours change midway through an absence , the absence is not automatically
recalculated to pick up the changes to the contract. If this occurs, you should put in an end
date for the absence on the last day of the contract and enter in a new absence for the
start date of the next contract. For the new contract, the daily absence roster contract
hours need to be amended to reflect the hours of the new contract.

1.2. What is an Attribute?
An attribute is effectively a means of applying a label to an employee’s pattern . This will be the
task/job that the employee is scheduled to complete. The attributes are user specified, examples
may include ‘Cashier’, ‘Floor’, ‘Security’ or ‘Training’. The ‘Attribute’ can then be displayed on the

attribute is a job/task that is available within Roster to be assigned to an employee, for each pattern
they are working within the week.
This function provides the:
• Ability to assign attributes to employees.
• Ability to view each employee assigned attribute in Roster Details.
• Ability to identify what job/task an employee is scheduled to complete by their attribute.
The Roster Attribute functionality p rovides users with the abilit y to assign an attribute to an
employee on a pattern. The attribute is available to view and filter by, on the Roster Details screen
and can be used to identify what job/task an employee is scheduled to complete on a pattern.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This guide is to provide an overview of the alternate ‘lite’ calculation available for WFM Roster
solutions. This document runs through:
• How the calculation works
• Limitations of the calculation
• What configuration is required to allow the calculation to work?
1.2. Introduction
As part of the migration to Portal in v23/24, an alternate attendance calculation was developed
for WFM Roster, mostly to provide a solution to the clients who have patterns that constantly
change. This is a very light calculation and only uses some elements of the standard calculation.
1.3. Pre-Requisites
Employee must be on Roster (on a Team Area) before they can use the Roster Calculation to
calculate their hours.
1.4. Benefits of Retail Calculation Solution
A traditional roster solution requires a significant number of Work Pattern reference data to be
set-up as part of the build to cater for varying start/end times, overtime rules etc. The ‘lite’
solution requires only a handful of patterns, assuming a basic Overtime calculation is to be
deployed.

7. Frequently Asked Questions
Several commonly raised queries:
1. Employee has clocked in/out to match their shift but why is Unexplained Absence
is calculating?
A work pattern must be attached to each clocking. If the clockings were entered manually
the column CT_CLOCKING.CALCULATION_WORK_PATTERN will not be populated. To
resolve, assign a work pattern to the clockings via Timesheet Input, then recalculate.
2. Is it possible to assign an employee to two different schedules on the same day?
Yes. However, it is not possible to assign the same work pattern. It is standard to have one
BASE work pattern selected as the primary shift and a second similar pattern (BASE2, FLEX
etc.) available for assigning a second daily schedule.
3. Can I use the Roster Calculation if my employee is not a roster employee?
No, the Roster calculation should only be used for roster employees who have been
assigned a Team Area.

3. Shift Swap
3.1. Overview
Employees can submit a request to swap a shift with another team member and accept or reject
a request for a Shift Swap with another employee, within the same roster week. For the Shift
Swap to be successful, managers must approve a request for a Shift Swap.
The Shift Swap approval workflow is as follows:
1. Employee A submits a Shift Swap with employee B.
2. Employee B is notified of the swap and then accepts or reject the Shift Swap.
3. If employee B accepts the Shift Swap, then the swap notifies the manager of employee B.
4. If the manager approves the Shift Swap, the Roster is then update for employee A and B,
to reflect the Shift Swap.
5. When the status of the swap changes to approved or rejected, both employees are
updated of the approval/rejection.

Parameters.

3. Team Area and Structure Overview
3.1. Team Area Overview
A Roster Team Area is created to logically group similar employees working within the same team.
Teams within the Team Area Structure should ideally match the Work Groups defined in Workforce
Management. For example, Team Areas might be based on the different departments in a retail
store such as: Menswear, Womenswear & Household.
Depending on the needs of each Team Area, different rules and criteria can be assigned to each
to ensure the team is adequately resourced. Roster allows for rules to be assigned at Team Area
level, ensuring variation of requirements for each team.
The Team Area Configuration screen can be used to create the Team Areas that appear within
Roster. This screen allows you to define, the roster criteria at a team level, for example:
• Area Rules

d to create the Team Areas that appear within

• Area Rules • Validation Rules
• Budget
• Staff Requirements, etc.
These criteria are then applied to the Team Area, including any possible sub-teams in the
organisational hierarchy. Team Area configuration must be assigned at team level for employees
to be added to each team, during rostering. Shift dependencies, such as Area Rule and Validation
Rule templates can be attached to the individual Team Areas with a date effective.

2.4. Maximum Number of Staff to Roster
Staffing Demand in Workforce Management has previously had the ability to set a minimum
number of staff to be rostered. It is now possible to add a maximum number of staff to be
rostered. This will stop you having more staff than you require either for cost purposes or
because you do not have enough facilities to cater for more than the maximum number of staff.
Using a maximum number will restrict the number of staff rostered to this value even if the other
staffing demand calculations result in a higher number.

1. Navigate to the Workforce Management Dashboard. 2. Select Staff Requirements.
3. Expand the 3-dot menu of the Team you wish to set the maximum number of staff on
and select View Staff Requirements.
4. Enter the maximum number of staff value required to the Maximum Value column.
5. Click Save.
2.5. Staffing Demand Ranges
Range Values remove the 1 – 1 relationship between a value and the number of staff this would
roster.
Currently we have a one-to-one relationship with roster calculations. For example:
• For every 5 people I need 1 member staff.
• If you have a footfall of 100 people you would need 20 members of staff
We need this to be more flexible and support intervals or ranges of values. For example:
• Between 1 and 5 people I need 1 member of staff

particularly occupation ones are correct.

7. Additional Options
There are two additional options that can be set, if required, that set the way shift information is
updated from People Planner into People XD and the way Absence totals are calculated.
7.1. Stopping People Planner overwriting a manual shift change
In the People Planner Mapping screen there is an option Do Not Overwrite Manual Shift
Changes. If this is set, then PeopleXD will check on receipt of shift information from People
Planner whether the current shift information has been created manually or by People Planner.
If it has been created by People Planner it will overwrite, if not, then the current information will
be retained.
7.2. Showing Live Absence Calculations
By default, in PeopleXD the Absence screen shows the information held in the absence tables
and is NOT updated with any shift changes. This is an issue with the People Planner integration

Question: What happens if Expense Claims are entered for the following year before the
Year End Rollover took place for the current year?
Answer:
There are several scenarios here:
1. If the Expense Run is complete, then information will have been processed in that tax
year. Proceed with your Year End Rollover.
2. If the Expense Claims have been processed , but the Expense Run is not complete, you
can reverse the Expense Claims status. Once reversed, the Year End Rollover can occur,
allowing the Expense Run process to proceed in the correct year.

"submitted", or "approved", then it is okay to complete the Expense Run, and then run your

1.2. About SEPA Changes (ISO20022)
The SEPA (ISO 20022) schema changes are being introduced as part of a European Directive
aimed at enhancing payment processing across Europe. These changes, originally set to become
mandatory from October/November 2025, are designed to facilitate instant and more
efficient payments, benefiting both businesses and individuals.
In November 2024, the European Payments Council (EPC) announced a change to the
implementation timeline:
• The adoption of ISO 20022 messaging remains mandatory from October 2025.
• However, the structured address requirement has been delayed to November 2026
to give organizations more time to comply.
Employers should consult their banks to determine whether early adoption of structured
address reporting is recommended.

The October 2025 vs. November 2026 deadlines for SEPA ISO 20022 changes are due to
different regulatory and implementation timelines:
1. October 2025 Deadline
• This is the general deadline for the adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging
format for SEPA credit transfers and direct debits.
• It is set by the European Payments Council (EPC) and applies to all SEPA
participants, including banks, payment service providers, and businesses
processing SEPA payments.
• By this date, organizations must ensure their systems are compatible with the
new format.
2. November 2026 Deadline
• This is a separate deadline specifically for the structured address reporting
requirement.
• Initially, this requirement was part of the October 2025 changes, but it has
been delayed by the EPC to November 2026 to give businesses and banks
more time to adapt.
• Most banks, however, recommend implementing structured addresses
alongside the October 2025 migration to avoid additional system changes
later.
Note:
It is critical that you have a conversation with your Bank regarding their plans for supporting
ISO20022 and what they recommend you do.

1.3. Key Changes
1.3.1. Structured Addresses
One of the significant updates under the SEPA ISO20022 schema is the requirement for
structured addresses within payment files. This ensures consistency and accuracy in payment
processing across financial institutions.
Employers should verify with their bank what address format they require or if its ok to omit the
address from the SEPA File completely. The mapping of the address format can be managed as
outlined in section 3.2 Mapping SEPA Address Data. Once a decision on the structured address
reporting requirement is confirmed, users will need to review their system address data and any
HR or other system feeds to identify and potentially cleanse any necessary data.
1.3.2. Customised Bank File Implementations
While the SEPA ISO20022 schema provides a general framework, its implementation can vary
slightly between banks. Each bank’s specific requirements will need to be validated to ensure
compatibility with their systems.

2.4.1. Overview
In SEPA ISO20022 payment messages, the Local Instrument Code specifies the type of payment
instrument being used for a transaction. This code defines how the payment should be
processed, including any specific rules or formats that apply in different countries or for various
transaction types.
The Local Instrument Code ensures that:
• Processing Rules: Payments adhere to country-specific regulations.
• Payment Types: Different payment instruments, such as credit transfers or instant
payments, are correctly handled.
Location in XML Messages
The Local Instrument Code is included in the payment instruction under the <PmtTpInf>
(Payment Type Information) element. It is typically represented as follows:
Example XML Structure:
<PmtTpInf>
<LclInstrm>
<Cd>INST</Cd>
</LclInstrm>
</PmtTpInf>
• <Cd> Element: Represents the code for the local instrument.
• INST: Indicates instant payments as per the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst)
scheme.
Purpose
The specific Local Instrument Code used depends on the payment method and applicable
country regulations. It enables banks and payment systems to:
• Correctly interpret the payment.
• Apply local standards and processing rules.

4.1. Background
Gardaí, Prison Officers, Permanent Defence Forces personnel and full-time firefighters must retire
before the general compulsory retirement age of 70 for Single Scheme members. In reflection of
this, these grades (which can be collectively termed “uniforme d services”) have a customised set
of pension terms in the Single Scheme, which in particular give them
• pensions paid earlier than in the case of standard-accrual public servants (those earlier
ages may vary),
• higher accrual rates for pension and retirement lump sum than those applying to
standard-accrual public servants,
• a higher contribution rate than applies to standard-accrual public servants.
As such, a separate Scheme must be created to cater for these members.

Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a government-mandated payment that offers financial support to employees unable to work due to illness. SSP is calculated based on a standard 5-day workweek, but issues may arise if the system incorrectly divides it over 7 days.
This miscalculation often results from incorrect employee work patterns or system configuration errors, leading to lower SSP payments than employees are entitled to receive.
SSP payments are configured at the organizational level to use either an employee's work pattern or qualifying days.
To review this configuration, follow these steps in portal.
Click Settings, then under UK Tax Rates, click General.
If the employee's Time/Workforce Management work pattern should take precedence over the OSSP qualifying days, select the Work Pattern indicator.
If necessary, select the Qualifying Days indicator and enable the appropriate days of the week for SSP eligibility.

According to SSP guidance, an employee's average earnings must exceed the Lower Earnings Limit (LEL). The Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) is calculated based on the eight weeks prior to the start of the Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW).
To qualify for SSP, ensure that employees have an average above the LEL for the past eight weeks.
If you wish to pay the employee SSP despite their AWE being lower than the LEL, you can update the Average Weekly Earnings toggle.
To do this, follow the steps below.
Click Settings then under UK Tax Rates, click General.
From the Pay Group Code drop down menu, select the relevant pay group
Under General, turn on Average Earnings toggle.
📌Note: Enabling this option means you will pay SSP regardless of an employee's AWE, even if it falls below the LEL. This adjustment will apply system-wide and affect all employees. You cannot configure this setting for an individual employee only.
If the AWE is incorrect, check the incorrect AWE for Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), as it affects all statutory sick pay calculations.
If the employee does have an average above the LEL, please raise a new case online, referencing this article's title and include the following details:
The dates for which SSP should have been generated.
The employee number.

Rolled-up holiday pay ensures that employees with irregular hours or patterns receive their holiday pay spread across each pay period, rather than as a lump sum when they take their leave.
This method complies with legislation requiring holiday pay to reflect regular earnings, including overtime and bonuses, by adding a proportionate amount to each payment.
Set up rolled-up holiday pay
Create a percentage-based pay code: Create a new percentage based pay code using the pay code wizard. This should have a percentage of 12.07% to reflect the statutory calculation for allocating holiday pay.
Set up the pay code formula: When setting up the pay code specify which earnings should be considered for the holiday pay calculation. Typically, this includes all basic pay codes and any overtime pay codes. These selections ensure that the rolled-up holiday pay reflects an employee's regular earnings.
Assign to employees: Assign the pay code to your employees. Each pay period, a percentage of the designated earnings will be automatically calculated and added to their pay as rolled-up holiday pay, ensuring compliance with the legislation.
Manage Absences
To account for absences and ensure accurate holiday pay calculations:

rolled-up holiday pay, ensuring compliance with the legislation.
Manage Absences
To account for absences and ensure accurate holiday pay calculations: Download the Insight report: From the Insight report store, download the 'Irregular Paid Employees - Absence Holiday Pay Calculation' report. This report helps identify employees absent during the current pay period and provides a detailed history of their earnings over a specified period (e.g., 52 weeks) for accurate calculation.
Override ralculations: With the report's information, you can manually adjust the rolled-up holiday pay for absent employees, ensuring their holiday pay reflects their average earnings accurately.
XD Workforce Management

If you enter a negate in the leave details field on the Maintain Leave Without Pay screen, you may encounter the following error:
**Start UnHandled Exception
SOURCEREF: s37000_insert_day_history
EMPNO: XXXXXX
ERRNO: -6502
ERRMESS: ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: number precision too large.**
This error can cause the PAY140 file to fail. To troubleshoot the issue, check the `number_of_units` in the log file. If this number exceeds 999, it will indeed cause the PAY140 to fail.
Here are the steps to resolve the issue:
1. Retrieve the PAY140.trcXXXX file, where XXXX represents the pay group.
2. Review the ERRDATA row, as the system only permits values up to 999.
If the negate value is greater than 999, it is recommended to split the negate into two parts. For instance, negate half of the amount in one period and the other half in a subsequent period. This approach is necessary due to user access rights.

The Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) is the European Union's initiative aimed at integrating payment systems to standardize euro transactions across participating countries. This initiative allows for seamless electronic payments using unified formats and procedures.
Organizations need to update their SEPA mode settings when they expand operations into new European markets, change banking relationships, or adapt to evolving regulatory requirements.
CorePersonnel offers three distinct SEPA modes to meet various banking requirements and operational needs:
Mode 1: Bank sort code and bank account number only.
Mode 2: Bank sort code, bank account number, BIC and IBAN.
Mode 3: BIC and IBAN only.
Initially, we place clients in Mode 2 to allow them to generate both the old bank files and the new SEPA files. Once clients are satisfied with the SEPA files, we switch them to Mode 3, as the old bank details become irrelevant.
​
Regarding Portal:
In Mode 1, users see the account and sort code.
In Mode 2, users see the account and sort code.
In Mode 3, users see the BIC and IBAN.
If you need to update the SEPA mode for all companies or for specific companies, please raise a new case online. Reference the title of this article and include details of the companies that need updating.

The pro-rata indicators on the Allowances/Payment tab of an allowance pay code play a crucial role in determining how the system calculates and applies allowances in specific scenarios.
By understanding these indicators, you can ensure accurate adjustments and compliance with Benefits In Kind (BIK) regulations, particularly when applying BIK deductions for the days an employee is available.
Understanding these settings helps ensure accurate calculations. Below is a summary of the impact of each indicator:
Pro Rata Indicator: Select this check box if the Pay Code is a Permanent/Recurring Allowance Payment which is pro-rated by the employees Contract Hours and Timesheet Basic Hours and Pro Rata Elements. By way of example if an employee's contract hours are 39 but they have only worked 20 hours then the employee will get paid 20/39 of the value of this allowance.
​
Pro Rata Element: Select this check box if this Payment is an Hourly /Daily Pay Code qualifying for the pro-rata Indicator described above i.e. the hours for this code qualify for making up the 20 hours in the example above.
📌Note: This field should only be enabled if the pay code is Hours or Days.
Pro Rata Calculation: Select this check box if the pro-rata calculation is based on the number of days the allowance is paid for. Otherwise the calculation is based on the number of days in the period.

When generating timesheets in WFM, if the system prompts: "Would you like to close?", select either:
Yes: This automatically closes the period and triggers PayWise+ message generation.
No: The period remains open and requires manual closure.

Click WFM Configuration then under Company, click Company and Calendar Config.
Beside the relevant company, click the three dot icon then click View/ Edit.

The Pro Rata BIK feature changes this behaviour for employees who start or leave employment part-way through a period. When enabled, PeopleXD calculates a proportional BIK value based on the number of days the employee was active within that period, rather than applying the full amount.
This ensures that leavers and starters are charged an accurate BIK figure that reflects their actual days of employment, rather than a full-period charge regardless of start or leave date.

How it works
Pro rata is triggered for a BIK record when either:
The BIK start date is after the period start date (employee is a starter mid-period), or
The BIK end date is before the period end date (employee is a leaver mid-period).

The calculation
Pro Rata BIK = (Standard BIK Value ÷ Days in Period) × Pro Rata Days
Term
Definition
Standard BIK Value
The employee's BIK value for the period
Days in Period
Total days in the payroll period (calendar or working days — see Day Basis below)
Pro Rata Days
The number of days the BIK was active within the period
Pro Rata Start
The later of: BIK start date or period start date
Pro Rata End
The earlier of: BIK end date or period end date
Pro Rata Days = (Pro Rata End − Pro Rata Start) + 1. The system automatically clamps the BIK active range to within the current period — date ranges do not need to be manually adjusted.
Example: An employee with a monthly BIK of £600 leaves on the 10th of a 30-day period. Pro Rata Days = 10, Days in Period = 30. Pro Rata BIK = (£600 ÷ 30) × 10 = £200. Without this feature, the full £600 would have been applied.

The PRSI Class Automation feature automates the update of Irish Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI) classes for employees based on their age, date of birth, and State Pension Contributory (SPC) status. Without this feature, PRSI class changes for older employees must be applied manually. When enabled, PeopleXD applies the correct class transitions automatically during each payroll run.
The feature is relevant for employees aged 66 and over. Irish legislation requires that PRSI classes change from Class A or S to Class J or M depending on whether the State Pension (Contributory) has been awarded and the employee's date of birth. PeopleXD automates this lookup and transition, reducing manual intervention and the risk of incorrect PRSI reporting.
📌Note: This feature is disabled by default. No PRSI class changes will be made automatically until the feature is explicitly enabled.

If the employee meets the age and SPC criteria, the system automatically transitions their PRSI class to the correct value. The system determines which rule to apply based on three factors: the employee's age (calculated from date of birth), whether the State Pension (Contributory) has been awarded (SPC indicator), and the original PRSI class on record.

Frequently asked questions
What happens if an employee's SPC status changes mid-year?
The system re-evaluates SPC status and age on each payroll run. If the SPC indicator is updated on the employee record, the correct class transition will be applied from the next payroll run that processes that employee.
Can I enable this for some pay groups but not others?
Yes. Set the System Type flag to N and enable the pay group-level flag only for the pay groups where automation is required. Pay groups with the flag set to N will continue to require manual PRSI class management.
Does this affect employees under age 66?
No. The automation logic only applies to employees aged 66 and over. Employees below 66 are not evaluated and their PRSI class is not changed by this feature.

es aged 66 and over. Employees below 66 are not evaluated and their PRSI class is not changed by this feature.
What happens when an employee turns 70? Once an employee reaches age 70, the class transition (A → J or S → M) is applied unconditionally on the next payroll run, regardless of SPC status or date of birth. This age 70 override cannot be suppressed by the SPC indicator.
How do we exclude employees who should not be transitioned?
Disable the automation at pay group level for any pay groups containing employees who require manual PRSI class management. If all affected employees are in a specific pay group, set that pay group's flag to N while leaving others enabled.
Does enabling this feature affect historical periods?
No. PRSI Class Automation applies to the current payroll period only. Previously processed periods are not reprocessed or affected.

Employment Allowance is a UK government scheme that allows eligible employers to reduce their annual employer (secondary) Class 1 National Insurance Contributions (NICs) by up to £10,500 per tax year. The allowance is claimed via the Employer Payment Summary (EPS) submission to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC).
Previously, the Third-Party Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) listing used for HMRC payments did not include Employment Allowance as a line item. This has now been corrected — Employment Allowance will now appear in the Third-Party EFT output alongside other HMRC payment obligations, once the indicator is enabled.

Once the Employment Allowance EFT indicator is enabled:

What happens if I do not enable the indicator?

Digital Employment Verification allows your employees to share payroll data digitally with financial service providers, removing the need for manual payslip requests and giving them full control of their data and personal finances.
Access PeopleXD Payroll supports this through two provider integrations: Experian Work Report™ and The Verification Exchange® from Equifax. As an employer, you control whether this feature is active for your workforce.
Each time an employee initiates a credit application such as a credit card, mortgage, or loan, they provide consent for their payroll data to be accessed.
​
Overview
What is Digital Employment Verification?
Digital Employment Verification is the ability for employees to share their employment and income information digitally with financial service providers such as banks or mortgage lenders, directly from your payroll system. This removes the need for manual payslip requests and speeds up credit application decisions.
Access PeopleXD Payroll supports this through two provider integrations:
Experian Work Report™
The Verification Exchange® from Equifax
What does it mean for your company?

oll supports this through two provider integrations:

What does it mean for your company? A recent Experian survey of 230 Human Resources (HR) and Payroll professionals shows that many large organisations receive an average of 150 requests a month from employees to source and share payroll data. This equates to 11 hours a month of HR and Payroll team time devoted to requests.
Enabling Digital Employment Verification removes this administrative burden, reduces your carbon footprint where paper payslips would otherwise have been shared, and supports a more direct and secure way of sharing employment information on behalf of your employees.
What does it mean for your employees?
When employees apply for credit with a financial institution, they can choose to upload payslips manually or use Digital Employment Verification. If they choose the service, it automatically accesses, with their explicit consent, the required records from their employer and passes them to the provider. This delivers direct confirmation of gross and net income, employment status, and tenure in seconds.
How do employees know they can use this service?

This delivers direct confirmation of gross and net income, employment status, and tenure in seconds.
How do employees know they can use this service? Each provider maintains a list of opted-in employers supplied by Access Group. If the financial institution uses one of these providers and the employee's employer is on that provider's list, the employee is offered the option to use the service at the point of the transaction.
Is there a cost to my organisation for enabling this?
No. The integration is free for employers. There are no ongoing costs associated with enabling Digital Employment Verification for your employees.
How the integration works
What is required from my organisation to provide this service?
You enable the integration directly in your Access PeopleXD system. Once enabled, your employees can consent to a financial institution using the service to digitally share their relevant employment and income data. It is not possible to enable the integration on an employee-by-employee basis, it applies to all employees when switched on.
How does the integration work?
When the integration is enabled, the relevant data for your employees is shared with a secure holding database hosted within the Access Group UK. This database exists solely to make data available to employees who choose to use the service.

ure holding database hosted within the Access Group UK. This database exists solely to make data available to employees who choose to use the service. Only when an employee opts in with their chosen financial institution and provides explicit consent will the verification provider Experian or Equifax; access that employee's data. Access is made via a secure Application Programming Interface (API) on a one-time, transaction-by-transaction basis.
📌Note: Payslip data is held in the holding database for a rolling period of 12 months. Data older than 12 months is deleted automatically. If your organisation disables the integration, all corresponding data is deleted from the holding database.

A priority 1 (P1) case refers to a critical issue that severely impacts business operations, such as system outages or payroll failures. You should classify a case as P1 when it meets the following criteria:
Business Critical Payroll Deadlines: The case involves a risk to a business-critical payroll deadline, and no workaround is available. Workarounds may include manual interventions.
Stalled Payroll Jobs: A payroll job is stuck, has failed, or is unavailable, jeopardizing a business-critical deadline.
Bank File Transfer Risks: There is a risk of failing to transfer the Bank file to the Bank on time.
Software or Screen Availability: The software or a specific screen is unavailable, putting a business-critical deadline at risk, and no workaround is available.
Security or Data Breach: There is a security or data breach that requires resolution from the PeopleXD Support, Development, or Product teams. While other security alerts may be high priority, only issues caused by the software can be aligned with contractual SLAs.
When logging a P1 case, please outline any affected or potentially impacted deadlines.
📌Note: Next-day deadlines may be appropriately managed under a P2 classification. Do not classify an issue as P1 if it affects only a few employees and a workaround is available (including manual timesheet input).

The Payroll dashboard serves as a crucial tool for monitoring employee compensation accurately. However, discrepancies such as incorrect employee rates can occur for several reasons, including data entry errors, outdated information, or integration issues with HR systems.
To resolve an incorrect rate, you need to update the rate toggle.
Understanding combined rate displays
When an employee has two different rates within the same period (e.g., due to a mid-period salary change), the system displays a combined rate by default.
For example, if an employee had an original rate of €13.01 and received a new rate of €12.49, the Current Period screen shows a total rate of €25.50 when you haven't enabled the toggle.
📌Note: This represents a display issue only. The system calculates and pays the correct amount at the appropriate rate.
View pay details

Click Employee, then in the search field, search for employee.
Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW.
Click Current Period or OneView then click BREAKDOWN.
Turn on the Rate toggle then click OK.
Results after enabling the rate toggle
After you enable the Rate toggle, the system will:
Display the individual rates applied during the period.
Separate the hours worked at each rate
Clearly distinguish between old and new rates, including appointments.

An employer's PAYE reference number and accounts office reference are essential legal identifiers used by HMRC. Each company registered with HMRC must have a unique PAYE reference and accounts office reference.
If you submit an RTI or FPS file and it gets rejected, the cause is an incorrect PAYE reference or accounts office reference stored in PeopleXD, which does not match the information held by HMRC.
To resolve this issue, check and update the PAYE reference and accounts office reference. To do this, follow the steps below in Portal.
PAYE reference
A PAYE reference number includes two parts:
A three-digit HMRC office number.
A unique reference number for your business, typically structured like 123/A56789 or 123/AB56789, with some exceptions.
To update the PAYE Reference, follow these steps.
Click Settings then click Organisations.
From the Code dropdown menu, select the relevant company.
In the Tax Office Number and District Number fields, enter the first three-digit part of the PAYE reference.
In the Registered No and Tax Office Ref fields, enter the second part of the PAYE reference.
🤓Tip: For example, if your PAYE reference is 123/A56789, enter 123 in the Tax Office Number and District Number fields, and enter A56789 in the Registered No and Tax Office Ref fields.
Click Save.
Accounts Office Reference

e Tax Office Number and District Number fields, and enter A56789 in the Registered No and Tax Office Ref fields.
Click Save.
Accounts Office Reference An accounts office reference consists of thirteen characters, typically in the format 123PX00123456 or 123PX0012345X. You can find this reference in letters from HMRC regarding PAYE or when you registered as an employer.
To update the accounts office reference, follow these steps.
Click Settings then click Other General Settings.
From the Company dropdown, select the relevant company.
In the Inland Revenue Paypath Reference field, enter the accounts office reference.
Click Save.

There would be several reasons as to why an employee's pay group will need to be changed, such as:
Changing pay frequency (monthly, weekly, etc.).

It is important to first take the below into consideration before doing so.
User access

Auditing (Amendments)
During the PAY300 Control report update process, all details regarding employee gross pay, tax, and PRSI are transferred to the new pay group.
This change will appear in the amendments column of the payroll control report, which may lead to mismatches in opening and closing balances.
​Timing
Always move employees to a new pay group at the start of a payroll cycle to ensure correct handling of cumulative values.

nd closing balances.
​Timing
Always move employees to a new pay group at the start of a payroll cycle to ensure correct handling of cumulative values. Avoid making changes during active payroll cycles.
Move to a different company
If the new pay group belongs to a different company, all data will transfer to the new company’s previous pay, including cumulative values for the new period. You may still see historical details for both companies.
Before changing pay groups across companies, process the employee as a leaver and ensure they are marked as dormant. Only rejoin them after completing the pay group change.

NIable pay= LEL + PT + ST + UE

What is an increment?
An increment is an increase or addition to an employee's pay, especially one that is part of a series based on a fixed scale.
What is the Increment Process?
This process applies only to employees who have a pay scale salary.
Increments cannot be automatically generated for those on personal rate salaries.
Using the increment process eliminates the need to manually create a salary amendment for standard annual or periodic salary increments. This process can apply to all employees or a group of employees in an organization on a common date each year.
Increments may also be applied on a date specific to the employee's post appointment, for example, 12 months from the start date or upon turning 18 or 21 years old.
When increments are processed from the CorePay side, they are generated during a payroll run and typically have a reference or reason code starting with "PAY" followed by a number indicating they were generated from CorePay.
When increments are processed from CorePersonnel, they are generated by a nightly increment job. This job usually generates increments a fixed number of days before the due date to allow HR and payroll to approve or reject them.

Key CorePersonnel increment attributes
Increment Due Date This is the date on which the increment is due to be applied to the post appointment salary record. For example, if an employee starts in the organization on January 1, 2018, the employee may be due for an increment on January 1, 2019.
Managing increment due dates
You can capture the increment due date and the increment hold indicator on a salary record during the appointment stage.
These can be manually entered by the user or automatically calculated based on the terms and conditions assigned to the post appointment.
You can update the increment due date and increment hold indicator for an employee directly on the pay profile screen.
Increment details are managed at the post appointment level. The increment due date is associated with a salary record on the post appointment, not on the employee record itself.
Therefore, if an employee has multiple post appointments, it is crucial to record the increment due date for each post appointment as relevant.

Increment system job The CorePersonnel nightly job reviews all employees' increment due dates, creates a new salary record based on the pay scale point increment rules, and generates a new increment due date for the employee's salary. For example, if the increment due date is set for January 1, 2019, the increment system job will identify that the employee is due for an increment on that date. It will then move the employee to the next point on the scale by creating an approved salary amendment and aligning this to the employee's pay profile. The new increment due date will be updated to 12 months later, on January 1, 2020.
Increment hold indicator
This indicator ensures that the increment job does not process for the employee on the increment due date. For example, if the increment hold indicator is set against an employee's record on January 1, 2019, during the review on that date, no increment will be applied to the employee's record. However, if the increment hold indicator is removed a week later, and the increment due date is still present for January 1, 2019, the job will process it at that point, and the pay will be backdated for the seven days missed.

Pay scale point increment rules
Rules are established for each pay scale point to control: The next point available.
The progression pay scale and point to be used when the maximum point has been reached on the current pay scale.
The length of time at the current point (if different from the standard 12 months).
A bar point, which stops an employee from incrementing beyond that point.
Age restrictions on progression to the next point.
Increment due date policy
The increment due date will not be removed when an employee reaches the top of the scale.
If a manual salary amendment is made to bring the employee to the top point on the scale, the increment due date will not be removed.
If bar points are used, the increment due date will also remain as the top of the scale will not be reached by the increment process.
The increment due date will only be removed if the increment process results in moving to the top point on the scale.

If an employee has both a DEO (Child Maintenance) and a DEA, the DEO will take priority over the DEA. The system will check the employee's net wage and ensure that it is equal to or greater than 60% before calculating the DEA. If the net wage falls below this threshold, the DEA will not be calculated. This means that the DEO will be deducted first, followed by the DEA.
📌Note: If the DEO deduction results in the employee receiving less than 60% of their net pay, then no DEA should be deducted.
During each pay period, People XD will evaluate the employee's net wage to determine whether the DEA deduction should be applied in full, partially, or not at all. The system has been designed in accordance with HMRC guidelines.
For further information regarding protected earnings associated with DEAs, we recommend visiting the HMRC website on Direct Earnings. This resource will help you understand what to expect in People XD concerning a DEA with protected earnings.
According to the HMRC website, here is some important information regarding protected earnings:
When operating a DEA, you must consider the Protected Earnings amount, which is equal to 60% of an employee’s net earnings. For each pay period when a DEA calculation is applicable, you must ensure that after adding the DEA amount to any other orders in place, the employee is left with at least 60% of their net wage."

The Minimum Wage Exception report identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage(NMW), the National Living Wage (NLW), or the minimum apprenticeship rate. The report compares the employee’s hourly rate against the statutory rate applicable to their age.
To check the Periodic Employee Hours setting, follow the steps below.
Click Manage Payroll then click Payroll Checking.
Click View Gross to Nett then click the Minimum Wage tab.
Turn the Periodic Employee Hours toggle on or off as needed.
📌Note: We recommend enabling Periodic Employee Hours where the contracted hours on the employee’s contract do not represent weekly hours.
For example, if the pay group uses a fortnightly pay frequency and the contracted hours stored on the contract represent fortnightly hours, the toggle should be turned on.
How the hourly rate is calculated
The calculation used in the Minimum Wage Exception report depends on whether Periodic Employee Hours is enabled or disabled.
When periodic employee hours is enabled
The hourly rate is calculated as: Hourly Rate = Pay in Period ÷ Hours at Appointment Level
Example:
Pay frequency: Weekly
Pay in period: £600
Employee hours: 40

If the repayment amount for the AOE or DEA deduction seems incorrect, it may be because the net earnings used in the calculation do not align with the expected formula.
For both AOE and DEA, the net earnings for an employee are calculated using the following formula:
Net Earnings = Gross Pay – Applicable Deductions
Applicable deductions include:
PAYE (Income Tax)
Employee NI/PRSI
Pension contributions
📌Note: Other deductions such as student loans, are not included in this calculation.
The deduction is then calculated using this formula:
(Lower band × lower rate%) + (Reminder (net earnings – lower band) × balance) = Deduction amount
Example
This example is based on a monthly employee.
Earnings: 2000.00
Deductions:
Pension: 100.00
PAYE: 150.00
Employee NI: 100.00
Total Deductions: 350.00
Net pay earnings used for AOE: 2000.00 – 350.00 = 1650.00
📌Note: The lower band, lower rate, and balance information can be found on the pay code used for AOE.
Lower Band: £1480
Lower Rate: 17%
Balance Rate: 50%
Deduction calculation:
Step 1: 1480 × 0.17 = 251.60
Step 2: (1650 – 1480) × 0.50 = 85.00
Total AOE Deduction: 251.60 + 85.00 = 336.60

If an error has occurred within payroll and the incorrect data has already been reported to Revenue, the inaccurate submission data can be corrected and sent again.
You have three submission types available:
Normal submission
Full resubmission
Delete submission
The system can also generate a correction submission file in specific scenarios. Choose the correct option based on the following factors.
Correction files
Correction files for past periods are generated under these circumstances:
Updated PPSN
If you update an employee's PPSN (Payee Public Services Number), and they were previously reported to revenue using a different PPSN, a correction file will be generated the next time PMOD is processed for payroll, provided the employee is active.
📌Note:
A correction payslip will be issued for each period with the incorrect PPSN.
If the PPSN was null for a period, we do not create a correction file for that time, as it may have been correct at that point (e.g., the employee was subject to emergency tax).
No correction file is generated if the only modification is changing an employee's PPSN from one ending in "W" to a different PPSN.
Updated leave date
If you update an employee's leave date and they were previously reported with a different leave date, a correction file will be created for all prior periods associated with the employee's current employment ID that had a leave date.

ferent leave date, a correction file will be created for all prior periods associated with the employee's current employment ID that had a leave date. If the updated leave date pertains to a different payroll period, a correction file will be generated for the old period, omitting the leave date, and the new leave date will be sent for the current period.
Cancel payment
If a cancel payment is entered for an employee for a previous period, a correction file will generate with these details.
📌Note: When you cancel a payment, it can be reflected in one of two ways:
As a negative gross amount within your monthly payroll submission.
As a separate correction file submission.
Deceased employee
A correction file is generated when an employee has passed away.
No generation of correction files
Correction files will not be created in these situations:
No correction file is generated if the only modification is changing an employee's PPSN from one ending in "W" to a different PPSN.
If the employee has no pay recorded for the period, no correction file will be generated. You must record a pay for the period or submit a Full Submission.
Full Resubmission
A full resubmission contains both delete line IDs and new line IDs (payslips) to replace the previously deleted data. It deletes all payslips previously sent to revenue for that pay group and period while sending the new payslips.

replace the previously deleted data. It deletes all payslips previously sent to revenue for that pay group and period while sending the new payslips. You should use a full resubmission if there was an issue with the originally sent file, such as an incorrect pay date. If the payroll has not progressed, users can select the full resubmission option and enter the correct pay dates.
The new file will generate updated payslips with the corrected pay date and include delete line IDs for the originally sent payslips for that period.
Ultimately, this allows for the old payslips to be replaced by the new submission. Users can verify that the figures received by revenue are accurate after making a check payroll run via a web service call.
Delete submission
A delete submission file contains only delete line IDs and will remove previous submissions sent to revenue once transferred.
You should use a delete submission if an employee was incorrectly included in the submission file and should not have been. This option is appropriate if an employee or pay group should have been excluded but was mistakenly included.
If a file was sent twice for a period, you can delete the duplicate by specifying the submission ID.

Do not use a delete submission if a payment was reported to revenue but the employee should never have received it; in that scenario, you need to perform a delete cancel instead. Otherwise, the cancellation will be picked up in the next submission file.
If you do not enter a submission ID, the system will create a file with delete lines for all submissions for that pay group and period, which will be deleted from revenue upon transfer.
Clients can specify an employee number if they wish to delete submissions for that specific employee, and they can also enter a submission ID for the employee.
The submission ID field will display a list of all submissions previously sent and accepted by revenue for that pay group and payroll period combination. If no submission was accepted, there will be no entries in the submission ID list.
If the previous period functionality is enabled, the screen will operate similarly, allowing users to enter the relevant period in the previous period's field.
The submission IDs displayed in the list icon will show the most recently generated submissions first.

The Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) is a real-time system from the Irish Revenue that provides employers with up-to-date tax information for each employee, including tax credits, cut-off points, and USC rates.
This system automatically updates employee tax details as circumstances change, ensuring accurate tax calculations throughout the employment period.
When managing employee changes such as departures, rehires, and temporary rejoiners, it is essential to follow specific procedures to maintain tax compliance and ensure accurate tax calculations.
Leavers
When an employee leaves the organisation, the payroll submission file will notify Revenue during the employee's last pay period. Consequently, Revenue will update the employee's RPN details.
After processing a leaver in CoreHR, the employee will no longer appear in the RPN retrieval system.
Rejoiners
When rehiring an employee, there are two scenarios to consider regarding RPN based on how the rejoiner is set up in CoreHR:
Rejoin the employee with their existing employee number (recommended)
This process reactivates the existing employee record.
A rejoin date (the new start date) is recorded.
Their RPN will be retrieved using the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process.
A new Employment ID will be created (valid characters for Employment ID are [A-Za-z0-9_\-]).

e retrieved using the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process.
A new Employment ID will be created (valid characters for Employment ID are [A-Za-z0-9_\-]). The employee will not appear on the submission file with the latest start date until after their first payment.
Create a new employee record (not recommended)
If a new employee number is generated in CoreHR for the returning employee, they will be treated as a new employee.
A new employee number is created.
Their RPN will be retrieved via the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process.
A new Employment ID will be created (valid characters for Employment ID are [A-Za-z0-9_\-]).
Temporary rejoiners
The process for retrieving RPNs for temporary rejoiners differs based on whether the payroll period falls in the same year or the previous year.
For a temporary rejoiner in the same year:
Retrieve the employee RPN.
Enter the company or employee reference.
Use the most recent Employment ID for RPN retrieval; this will not be treated as new employment.

When retrieving RPNs at the company level, the employee reference will be blank, and the company last updated will default.

Enter the company or employee reference.

Revenue have recently announced that non-taxable advances will be allowed in certain scenarios.
This change is being implemented following feedback on the ERR release in relation to advanced not being allowed.
What this means?
Irish Revenue will introduce an optional administrative practice allowing the processing of non-taxable advances under certain conditions.
For example:
Conditions for Application
Advances are only allowed for anticipated travel & subsistence expenses and Employers must ensure appropriate controls are in place to track and reconcile all travel and subsistence advance payments.
Reporting Advances
Advance travel or subsistence payments must be reported under Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) using a new designated “Advances” subcategory. In addition, as the advance is drawn down on, this must also be reported to Revenue under ERR.
Reasonable Estimates
It's crucial that advance payments represent a reasonable estimate of the expected claim amount and qualify for relief under section 114 TCA 1997.
Timely Reconciliation
Employers are required to reconcile advance payments with actual claims promptly. Any excess in payment should be recouped without delay or subjected to tax if not settled.
Notification to Revenue

yments with actual claims promptly. Any excess in payment should be recouped without delay or subjected to tax if not settled.
Notification to Revenue While there's no requirement to notify Revenue in advance, employers must have appropriate governance and controls in place to meet the required conditions.
No Obligation
Employers have the discretion to opt into this administrative practice. If choosing not to, standard tax rules apply, meaning any advance payments must be taxed through payroll.
Further guidance and examples, check the Revenue Tax Duty Manual (TDM) part 38-03-33.
What do I need to do next?
Employers deciding to operate advances must report all advance travel and subsistence payments under ERR once their chosen reporting mechanism becomes available.
Revenue Manual screens:
Revenue plans to make a software change to their ROS screens to allow employers to capture and report these advance payments manually. The Revenue ROS online/file Tax and Duty Manual Part 38-03-33 upload and API are anticipated to be available within approximately two months.
PeopleXD solution:
We will be updating our software solution to accommodate the ERR reporting requirements. Until this is released, non-taxable advance payments need to be manually reported using Revenue screens.

When processing salaries, arrears may not generate correctly for an employee due to several factors.
Below, we outline common scenarios that can cause inaccuracies in arrears calculations.
Null or zero multiplier for previous rate
If the multiplier for the employee's previous rate is null or zero, the system will not generate any arrears because there is no prior pay to calculate against. To ensure correct arrears payment, you need to manually enter a timesheet.
Incorrect pay group
If an employee was initially set up in the wrong pay group during payroll processing and then moved to the correct pay group, you need to process a manual timesheet entry to pay the correct arrears since the system does not accommodate this scenario.
Incorrectly entered new rate
Check that the new rate has the correct effective date recorded for that row.
Transaction date outside payroll period
Check the timesheet transaction date reflects the date of the salary change or a later date.
Multiple salary changes in the same period
If the employee experiences two or more salary changes (e.g., an increment and a promotion) within the same period, you need to enter a manual timesheet entry to pay the correct arrears, as the system does not handle this situation.
Input date on or before complete update date

enter a manual timesheet entry to pay the correct arrears, as the system does not handle this situation.
Input date on or before complete update date If the input date for the allowance/salary line matches or predates the complete update date, the system considers the history row as processed in the previous payroll run. To resolve this, enter a manual timesheet to pay the correct arrears.
Discrepancy in pay days in period
If the pay days in the period are set to five days but the calculation uses seven days, you need to process a manual timesheet entry to pay the correct arrears.
No net pay row for the period
If the period lacks a net pay row, no arrears will be generated. To resolve this, you need to enter a manual timesheet to pay the correct arrears.
Employee changed pay groups
When an employee changes pay groups (e.g., from weekly to fortnightly), timing issues may arise. Run payroll updates in the old pay group first, and once that is complete, proceed with updates in the new pay group.
Incorrect number of units on nett pay row
If the number of units on the net pay row in the day history is incorrect, please raise a new case online and reference this article title. A support analyst will update the field accordingly.
Incorrect pay group for new starter

ase raise a new case online and reference this article title. A support analyst will update the field accordingly.
Incorrect pay group for new starter If a new employee is placed in the wrong pay group and then moved, the system indicates that the employee has been paid for those days based on the last processed period. Enter a manual timesheet to ensure the correct arrears payment
Positive input retro job needed for hourly pay codes
For hourly type pay codes, you need to run the positive input retro (PIR) job to generate the necessary retrospection payments.
Incorrect Rejoin Date generating unexpected arrears
Please raise a new case online and reference this article title. A support analyst will check and remove the rejoin date and correct the employee's latest pay start date if necessary.

Similarly, a percentage allowance will not generate if the applicable percentage pay codes (i.e. what to get a percentage of) are not set up for the allowance.

A salary offset deduction reduces an employee's salary to account for their absences, aiming to ensure fair compensation during periods of sick leave.
Incorrect salary offset deductions can happen for the following reasons:
Cause 1: The daily rate looks incorrect.
The daily rate is determined by the number of days set at the pay group level. To check this, follow the steps below in portal.
Click Settings then under Codes, click Pay Groups.
In the Pay Group Code drop-down menu, select the relevant pay code.
In the Days in Year field, update the value.
If the employee is salaried, divide their salary by the number of days in the year to calculate the daily rate. Then, multiply this daily rate by the number of sick days taken during the period. If this results in a different amount, check the override settings associated with the sickness category according to the article "Occupational Salary Offset for Absence using the Wrong Hourly Rate."
Cause 2: An employee has taken 10 sick days
For example, if an employee works 20 hours per week (4 hours per day) and has taken 10 sick days, their salary is £18,720 (£9 per hour). The total absence should account for 40 hours; however, the payslip reflects a deduction of 80 hours instead of 40 hours.

Scottish Arrestment Order rates specify the statutory deduction amounts that employers must apply when court orders instruct them to withhold money from an employee's wages to satisfy debts or legal obligations. Before setting up a reducing balance allowance, you need to be aware of the following:
A reducing balance allowance is setup with a capital sum that reduces each time it is paid by the employee. The capital sum can be set-up as a standard value or percentage-based.
The balance due is reduced by the value that the employee is setup to pay for each payroll run.
This type of allowance will continue to be taken until the balance is reduced to zero.
The value or percentage is assigned to the employee. If a value is assigned, it is the periodic value that is entered and not the capital sum.
A capital sum value also needs to be assigned. This represents the total annual value to be deducted.
The balance due is automatically set to this value initially and will be decremented each payroll run until it reaches zero. The allowance will cease at this point.
📌Note: The system will not process retrospective arrears for a reducing balance pay code assigned to the employee with a date in the past. Reducing balance pay code will calculate from the current period or period relative to the future start date only.

A taxable redundancy payment is compensation provided to employees when their employment ends due to redundancy. Sporting testimonials are payments made to recognize a sportsperson's contributions. Both types of payments require careful handling in payroll due to specific tax treatment rules.

Click Edit then click Rules.

Enhanced Holiday Pay allows you to calculate holiday pay based on average earnings. You can record annual leave, generate calculations, and view pay history.
If you use Enhanced Holiday Pay, you need to update your annual leave start and end dates each year. This ensures that the system applies the correct entitlement period.
Failing to update these dates will cause the system to continue using the previous year's entitlements instead of resetting for the new holiday year.
How the system works
When you set up Enhanced Holiday Pay, you enter your holiday year dates (for example, 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024). The system uses these dates to determine which entitlement to deduct when an employee takes a holiday.
The system provides a 12-month grace period, during which it automatically rolls forward your entitlement dates by one year.
For example:
If your parameters are set to 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024:
An employee taking holiday in December 2024 will use the 2024 entitlement.
The same employee taking holiday in January 2025 will automatically use the 2025 entitlement.
However, this automatic roll-forward only applies for one additional year. If you do not update the Parameter screen:
Using the same parameters: 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024:

orward only applies for one additional year. If you do not update the Parameter screen:
Using the same parameters: 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024: If an employee takes a holiday in January 2026, the system cannot roll forward a second time, and it will incorrectly deduct from the 2025 entitlement instead of the 2026 entitlement.
When to update your dates
Update your annual leave start and end dates during the first or second pay period of your new holiday year.
Although you have a 12-month grace period from the end of your old holiday year to the end of your new holiday year to make this change, updating early in the new year helps prevent processing issues.
To update your dates, follow the steps below.
From the dashboard menu, select Payroll Dashboard.
Click Settings then under Codes, click Enhanced Holiday Pay.
Click Pay Group Parameters tab.
For each pay group, review your annual leave start date and annual leave end date.
For the relevant pay group, update both dates to reflect your current holiday year.
Example:
Current parameters: 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024.
Update to: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026.
What happens if dates are not updated
If you do not update your dates within the grace period, the system will continue to use the previous year’s entitlement. This will lead to:
Employees potentially exhausting their holiday entitlement incorrectly.

Recommended action
If you still have your holiday years set to 2024, check the following as a proactive measure:
Check your Enhanced Holiday Pay setup screen and review the Pay Group Parameters tab.

As Payroll Year End approaches, it's essential to ensure your non-production environment mirrors production for testing and validation. This article outlines how to clone your production environment and whether a backup request is necessary.
Clones
What is a clone in the context of Payroll Year End?
A Clone refers to copying one environment to another. Although an optional step, cloning your Production environment to your UAT environment in advance of validating the Year End process on UAT ensures that the employee and payroll data on UAT is up-to-date and appropriate for Year End validation purposes.
​
However, any data on UAT which is not on production (e.g. configuration or test data for an in-progress implementation project) will be lost. This means that a production to UAT clone may not be appropriate, it depends on what's going on in your organisation at the time.
​
When should the clone be taken?
It’s best to take a clone after completion of the last payroll of the year, to enable testing of Year End on the latest data.
How do I arrange a clone (Production > UAT) for Year End validation purposes?
Email peoplexd.professionalservices@theaccessgroup.com to arrange a clone. Depending on your contractual entitlements, there may be an additional charge per clone. If you have a contractual entitlement to a clone, then there is no charge.

your contractual entitlements, there may be an additional charge per clone. If you have a contractual entitlement to a clone, then there is no charge. 📌Note: It's critical that you check internally before requesting a clone to ensure that you don't interfere with work being carried out by other teams or functions. The clone process will delete any data on UAT that is not yet on Production. Please consider:
Who else uses the UAT environment?
Are there any in-progress or on-hold projects taking place on UAT (new product implementations, new feature adoptions or anything else)?
Is there data on UAT that does not exist on Production? Who owns this data? Is it ok to lose this data?
Back ups/Data exports
Do I need to arrange for my Production environment to be backed up in advance of running the Year End cleardown?
If your PeopleXD solution is hosted by PeopleXD (exdata platform), then you do not need to specifically request a back up as this will happen automatically.
​
If your PeopleXD solution is not hosted by PeopleXD (exadata platform), then you need to arrange the backup with your I.T. department.

Individuals who qualify to defer their State Pension Contributory are those born on or after January 1st, 1958. They can claim the Contributory State Pension between ages 66 and 70.
However, once you begin claiming your Contributory State Pension, you can no longer choose to defer your pension claim, even if you continue to work. This is due to the non-payment of PRSI once you start receiving your pension.
Related Articles

From January 2024, individuals will have the option to defer the start date of their State Pension Contributory between the ages of 66 and 70. This means they can choose to claim their pension at any time within this age range.
The State Pension Contributory is available to those who are at least 66 years old and have made sufficient PRSI contributions.
The reason you will consider deferring the start date of your State Pension (Contributory) is because of the following reasons:
During the deferral period, you can continue working and contributing to the Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI), which can help you either increase your personal rate of payment or meet the qualifying criteria of having at least 520 contributions (equivalent to 10 years) for the State Pension.
By deferring, you can qualify for the State Pension if you were not eligible at age 66.
You can receive a higher rate of State Pension than you would have if you started receiving it at age 66.

Below are the common reasons why your year end reports do not match:
​
Reason
Description
Details
Employee moving company
If during the tax year, one or more employees transferred to another company in your payroll.
​
If an employee moves from company A to company B during the year, their cumulatives aren't included in the employee cumulatives (all) report or the final control report for the old pay group.
​
However, their cumulatives are still included in the pre year end data check report for the original company, similar to what would happen on the old P35.
Manual or cancel payments processed
Processing cancel or manual payments after the final payroll run is processed, and the final control report has been generated, can cause reports not to balance.
The complete update report reflects the employees’ cumulatives before the cancel or manual payments were processed, whereas the pre year end data check report reflects the employees’ current cumulatives.
Manually adjusting cumulatives
Adjusting the employees’ cumulatives after the final payroll run, and the final control report has been generated can cause reports not to balance.
The complete update report reflects the employees’ cumulatives before the employees’ cumulatives were adjusted.
​
The pre year end data check report reflects the employees’ current cumulatives.

Checking the reports in the middle of a payroll run Checking the reports in the middle of a payroll run can cause the reports not to balance.

Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)
Overview of changes The Employment Rights Act 2025 (Royal Assent December 2025) introduces the most significant Statutory Sick Pay reforms since 1985. These changes apply from 6 April 2026 and affect all UK employers.
The aim is to strengthen worker protections and provide financial security during sickness.
Day One SSP: Waiting days abolished.
LEL removed: Wider eligibility.

What was the rule before?
Under the previous rules, employees had to serve three waiting days (also known as qualifying days) at the start of every new Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW) before SSP became payable.

d to serve three waiting days (also known as qualifying days) at the start of every new Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW) before SSP became payable. This meant that if an employee became sick on a Monday, they would not receive SSP until Thursday (based on a Monday–Friday working pattern). The first three days were unpaid.
A PIW had to be at least four consecutive qualifying days. Any absence shorter than four days did not qualify for SSP.
What changes from 6 April 2026?
Waiting days are completely abolished. SSP is payable from the first qualifying day of sickness absence. Simultaneously, the minimum PIW is reduced from 4 days to 1 day, meaning a single qualifying day of absence can now trigger SSP.

Change 2: Removal of the lower earnings Limit
What was the lower earnings limit?
The Lower Earnings Limit was the minimum weekly earnings an employee needed to qualify for Statutory Sick Pay(SPP). For 2025 to 2026, the limit was £125 per week (£6,500 per year). Employees who earned below this amount, regardless of their hours or length of service, had no entitlement to SSP.
This rule disproportionately affected part‑time staff, zero‑hours workers, and lower‑paid employees, many of whom received no sick pay at all.
What changes from 6 April 2026?
The Lower Earnings Limit for SSP is completely removed. All employees become eligible for SSP from 6 April 2026, regardless of weekly earnings, as long as they meet the remaining conditions: they are an employee, they are sick, and they follow the employer’s notification process.
Who is newly eligible?
Approximately 1.3 million additional workers gain SSP eligibility from 6 April 2026.
The groups most affected include:
Part‑time employees earning below 125 pounds per week.
Zero‑hours contract workers with low or variable earnings.

How is Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) calculated?
AWE uses the same eight‑week reference period used for other statutory payments such as Statutory Maternity Pay.
