Overview
When a Company Holiday Scheme is linked to a balance, the system manages Public Holiday (PH) adjustments through two key figures:
PH FTE Entitlement
PH FTE Reserved
These values ensure accurate public holiday calculations based on employee work patterns and Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) status.
How the system calculates PH FTE Entitlement and Reserved
Term
Meaning
PH FTE Entitlement
The total number of Public Holiday days the employee is entitled to, based on the assigned Holiday Scheme and their FTE percentage.
PH FTE Reserved
The number of Public Holiday days that the employee is rostered to work and therefore has hours reserved for deduction. These are days the system expects to deduct from their annual leave balance because the employee was scheduled to work.
Key calculation
The system uses the following calculation to determine the Public Holiday adjustment:
PH FTE Entitlement – PH FTE Reserved
This ensures that only Public Holidays that affect the employee's actual work schedule are deducted.
Detailed example
Scenario
Impact
Employee is rostered to work on a Public Holiday
PH FTE Reserved is increased (hours deducted from leave balance).
Employee is on a rest day (day off) on a Public Holiday
The system treats this as PH FTE Entitlement only. No deduction is made because the employee is not scheduled to work.
Factors affecting the calculation

e system treats this as PH FTE Entitlement only. No deduction is made because the employee is not scheduled to work.
Factors affecting the calculation Employee’s FTE (Full-Time Equivalent)
Example:
100% FTE → 10 days PH Entitlement (if the scheme has 10 Public Holidays)
80% FTE → 8 days PH Entitlement
Employee’s Rostered Work Pattern
Only Public Holidays where the employee is scheduled to work are counted in PH FTE Reserved.
⚠️Important: If a Public Holiday (e.g. 7th April) is not appearing in PH FTE Reserved, this usually means the employee was on a REST day (non-working day) for that date. The system ignores Public Holidays when the employee is already scheduled off.
Conclusion
The Public Holiday calculation is dynamic and personalised. It considers:
The Holiday Scheme assigned to the employee or their Work Group
The employee’s FTE percentage
The employee’s rostered work pattern
This ensures fair and accurate adjustments to leave balances based on real working schedules.

Understanding the Bradford Factor score
The Bradford Factor score increases when an employee records absences related to pay codes configured in System Params under Reference A - C, in the Bradford Factor Parameters section.
The score only reflects absences within the current Bradford calendar period, so note the start and end dates of this period.

The only way to reduce the Bradford Factor score is to remove the related absences. After removing absences, recalculate the score by following these steps:
In Back-Office, go to CoreTime.
Select Time Management.
Click Bradford Factor.
In the Bradford Factor Rule field, select Bradford Factor.
Query the related employee.
Click Calculate to update the score.

If Absence Trigger Points in CorePortal are not sending any emails or notifications, there are six possible causes and corresponding resolutions to check:
Possible causes and resolutions
Cause 1: Trigger Point Rule not added to a Grouping
Resolution:
Ensure the Trigger Point Rule is added to the correct Group ID or Grouping.
In CorePortal, go to Administrator Dashboard > Trigger Points > Rule Grouping.
Confirm the rule is assigned to the Grouping that matches your company setup (e.g., Grouping 1 if your company uses Group ID 1).
Cause 2: No Organisational Role configured on the Trigger Point Rule
Resolution:
Edit the notification settings to assign an Organisational Role.
In CorePortal, navigate to Administrator Dashboard > Trigger Points > Rule Grouping > Notification Details > Organisational Roles.
Add or update the relevant organisational role(s) for the notification.
Cause 3: Known issue with Reminder Rules using certain absence date options
Issue:
Reminder Rules configured with Days after the end date of Absence or Days after the start date of Absence do not send notifications.
​Resolution:
This was fixed in minor release v22.0.13. Ensure your system is updated to this version or later.
Cause 4: Invalid log file directory path
Resolution:
The log file path must point to a valid directory on the database server.

this version or later.
Cause 4: Invalid log file directory path
Resolution:
The log file path must point to a valid directory on the database server. This requires Support to run database scripts to update the path.
Please raise a support case online referencing this issue.
Cause 5: Trigger Points not activated for the CoreTime Company
Resolution:
Activate Trigger Points in the CoreTime back office:
Go to CoreTime > System Params > Reference A-C > Control Parameters
Select the company

Select a default code

The scheduled job that sends trigger points may have stopped.
Support must restart this job.

Additional errors you might encounter include "0 Contracted Hours" and "Unable to Determine Absence Duration," which are also related to scheduling issues.
Since annual leave can only be applied to scheduled working days, the system blocks the request if the date is marked as a rest day. Updating the employee’s roster for that date will resolve the issue.
Why scheduling errors occur
The error appears when the selected leave date does not contain a working shift in the employee’s roster.
This usually happens because:
The employee is not scheduled to work on that date
The working pattern or shift is missing
The wrong contract or schedule is being used
The roster has not been updated in Workforce Management
Bank holiday scheme settings are not configured to allow leave requests on specific dates
Once a working shift is added to the schedule, the annual leave request can be submitted successfully.

This helps teams maintain visibility and consistency when managing leave activity across the organisation.
Overview of the Bulk Leave Approval screen
The Bulk Leave Approval screen displays a consolidated list of leave requests so users can review, filter, and approve them in bulk.
It is commonly used by:
Managers handling team leave approvals

By centralising requests, it supports faster decision-making and more efficient leave management.
Date range filtering
Instead of a start date offset, the Bulk Leave Approval screen uses a date range filter.
Users select a start date and an end date
The system then returns all leave requests within that period
This allows precise control over the data being viewed

This error occurs when an employee was not rostered at the time they submitted their leave request, but later became rostered for those dates. The mismatch between the original submission and the current rostering prevents approval.

To close a balance period and move into the next one, you need to run a balance period end.
Important considerations
Things to consider before running your balance period end:
Question
Answer
When can I run Period Year End?
Period Year End can only be run when the last week of the previous period has been closed in WFM, i.e. the first Monday of January.
For example, if the 31st December falls mid-week, then it is going to be the following Monday before the process can be run.
When does Length of Service (LOS) calculate?
LOS will calculate during the overnight calculation after Period Year End has been run. As a result, you won’t see LOS addition until the day after Period Year end has been run.
Do I need to adjust the Calendars?
Company calendar (and UDCs if in use) must be extended until the end of the calendar year at minimum, until the end of the balance year if balance year is a mid-year. It can also be extended for future years.
When do I set the Carry forward values?
Carry forward values are set during the previous year’s Year End process to affect values carrying into the new balance year.
For example, when running period year end for 2024 to open 2025, the carry forward values are set in the 2025 Balance Calendar to dictate the carry forward values that can be brought from 2025 to 2026.

You can understand why missed clockings show up for employees due to the timing of the overnight calculation job or an uneven number of clock times. This guide explains these scenarios and how the system handles them.
Why missed clocking appears after an employee clocks out
The overnight calculation job runs between 1am and 2am each day. At this time:
The employee may only have clocked in but not yet clocked out.
This causes the system to generate a missed clocking because it sees only one clock time.
The calculation job runs again the following night. By then, it will detect the employee’s clock out (for example, at 4:00 am) and calculate the hours worked correctly.
Missed clocking caused by uneven number of clock times
Another reason for missed clockings is if there is an uneven number of clock times (for example, one clock in and no matching clock out).
The system requires an even number of clock times to match clock ins with clock outs.
If there is an uneven number, a missed clocking will be generated.
In this case, the latest clocking entry should be reviewed and possibly removed to resolve the issue.
📌Note: Missed clockings caused by overnight processing will automatically correct after the next calculation run. Manual correction is only needed if there is an unmatched clock time.

CLOCK_DATE records the business date a clocking is assigned to in PeopleXD Workforce Management. If clockings are appearing on the previous day, this is usually caused by overnight shift patterns or your previous day threshold settings. This article explains how CLOCK_DATE works and what you can review to resolve unexpected date assignments.
⚠️ Important: CLOCK_DATE behaviour is expected when shift patterns and threshold settings are designed to support overnight working. Adjusting configuration should always be done in line with payroll rules and organisational definitions of a working day.
What CLOCK_DATE is used for
CLOCK_DATE records the business date a clocking is assigned to, not necessarily the exact time a clocking occurred. The system uses configuration rules to decide whether early hours belong to the current or previous working day.
Why CLOCK_DATE shows the previous day
Early shift start times
When shift patterns include very early start times, particularly around midnight or shortly after, the system may assign those clockings to the previous day.
For example:
A shift starting at 00:30 may still be treated as part of the previous working day depending on configuration.
This ensures shifts that span midnight remain grouped correctly for payroll and reporting.
Previous day threshold setting

depending on configuration.
This ensures shifts that span midnight remain grouped correctly for payroll and reporting.
Previous day threshold setting PeopleXD Workforce Management uses a previous day threshold to determine when a new working day begins.
If the threshold is set to 03:00:
Any clockings before 03:00 are assigned to the previous day.
Any clockings after 03:00 are assigned to the current day.
This setting is commonly used to align system processing with overnight shifts and operational day boundaries.
Shift pattern alignment
If shift patterns and threshold settings are not aligned, the system may consistently assign clockings to an unexpected date.
This is most likely to occur when:
Shift start times fall before the threshold.
Multiple overnight shift patterns are in use.
Temporary or placeholder patterns are assigned.
Reduce date discrepancies
Review shift pattern design
Ensure shift patterns reflect how your organisation defines a working day. Check:
Start and end times for overnight shifts.
Whether shifts cross midnight.
Consistency across employee groups.
Adjust the previous day threshold
Set the threshold to match operational requirements. For example:
Early morning operations may require a later threshold.
Day-based operations may benefit from an earlier cutoff.
Assign correct patterns in advance

e:
Early morning operations may require a later threshold.
Day-based operations may benefit from an earlier cutoff.
Assign correct patterns in advance Ensure employees are assigned the correct shift patterns before clockings occur. This reduces the risk of temporary or mismatched pattern rules affecting CLOCK_DATE.
Troubleshoot CLOCK_DATE issues
Check the assigned shift pattern for the employee
Review start times and overnight coverage.
Review the previous day threshold configuration
Confirm the cutoff time used by the system.
Compare affected clocking records
Identify whether the issue is consistent across specific shifts or employees.
Validate reporting outcomes
Confirm whether payroll or attendance reports are aligning with expected working days.

Run Retrieve Hours again.

When you action a Missed Clock notification in PeopleXD Workforce Management, the system generates a new timesheet entry based on the employee's assigned work pattern. If the timesheet has already been manually amended, this can result in duplicate entries appearing in your approval screens. Managers who action Missed Clock notifications and admins who review hours need to be aware of this behaviour.
How Missed Clock processing works
When you confirm a Missed Clock notification, the system follows these steps:
It checks the employee's assigned work pattern.
It generates a new timesheet entry for the missed clock day.
It treats this as a new record, not a modification of existing data.
The new record is sent to Approve Hours or Sign Off for review.
This process happens regardless of any previous manual adjustments.
Expected behaviour
This is expected system behaviour.
The purpose of the Missed Clock workflow is to ensure all missing clock events are formally captured and recalculated based on the employee's work pattern. Even if hours were previously edited on the timesheet, the system generates a new entry when the notification is actioned.
Why duplicate entries appear
Duplicate entries typically occur when:
An admin manually amends clockings on the timesheet first.
A manager later actions the Missed Clock notification.
The system generates a new work pattern-based entry.

y amends clockings on the timesheet first.
A manager later actions the Missed Clock notification.
The system generates a new work pattern-based entry. As a result, both the manual adjustment and the newly generated entry may appear in approval screens.
What managers and admins need to know
Approval impact
Actioning Missed Clock notifications can create additional entries requiring approval or sign-off.
Data accuracy
Review entries carefully in Approve Hours or Sign Off to ensure only the correct hours are processed for payroll.
Recommended practice
To avoid confusion, align admin adjustments with manager actions on Missed Clock notifications where possible.
Key takeaway
Actioning a Missed Clock notification always generates a fresh calculated entry based on the employee's work pattern. If the timesheet has already been manually adjusted, this can result in duplicate entries appearing in approval and sign-off screens.

Roster attributes let you label an employee's scheduled pattern with the job or task they are assigned to complete, such as Cashier, Floor, Security or Training. You can assign a default attribute to each employee, override it at day level, view and filter by attributes on the Roster Details screen, and report on attribute data via CoreInsight. This article covers everything you need to manage roster attributes, from initial configuration through to day-to-day use.
You'll need Team Manager access to assign and maintain roster attributes. An administrator must enable the Roster Attribute Active parameter before the feature is available.
What is a roster attribute?
A roster attribute is a label applied to an employee's rostered pattern to identify the job or task they are scheduled to complete for that pattern. Attributes are user-defined — examples include Cashier, Floor, Security and Training.
Roster attributes give you the ability to:
Assign attributes to employees at employee level, pattern level, or across multiple employees in a team area.
View each employee's assigned attribute on the Roster Details screen.
Identify what job or task an employee is scheduled to complete by their attribute.
Filter the Roster Details screen by one or more attributes.
Report on attribute data in CoreInsight.

Each employee can only have one attribute assigned per pattern — patterns cannot be split across multiple attributes.
Attributes are not displayed or maintained in HR Admin.
AutoRoster and Uncovered Shifts cannot be used against an attribute (Phase 1 only).
📌Note: This feature is delivered in two phases. Phase 1 covers the fundamental ability to assign jobs and tasks to employees. Phase 2 will extend attribute support to AutoRoster, Rules, Statistics and Uncovered Shifts screens.

Work patterns in PeopleXD are essential for defining employee schedules and operational workflows. However, there are specific limitations and processes to be aware of when managing these patterns. This provides an overview of how to handle work patterns, including setting them to inactive and understanding their visibility.
Overview of Work Pattern Management
You can’t delete work patterns in PeopleXD once you create them. If you no longer need a work pattern, set it to inactive instead. This prevents it from being used in future while keeping it available for reference.
Steps to Set a Work Pattern to Inactive
Go to the work pattern management section in PeopleXD.
Locate the work pattern you wish to deactivate.
Change the status of the work pattern to Inactive.
Once a work pattern is inactive, it will no longer be available for use in scheduling or other operations. However, it will remain visible in the system interface.
Limitations of Work Pattern Management
Deletion: Work patterns cannot be deleted once created. This ensures that historical data and references remain intact.
Visibility: Even when set to inactive, work patterns cannot be hidden or archived. They will continue to appear in the configuration or management interface.

If you see the error “You are not allowed to modify this personal shift override”, it means the system is preventing the override because the shift falls outside the current open calendar period.
Shift overrides can only be applied to shifts that fall within the current open period or in a future period.
Why this error occurs
This error happens when:
The date effective on the shift is before the current open period on the system calendar
The system calendar does not allow edits or overrides for past or closed periods
A personal shift override is being added to a shift that is no longer editable
How to resolve the error
Assign a new shift within the open period
Go to the employee’s profile.
Assign a new shift with a date effective that falls within or after the current open period.
Save the new shift.
Apply the personal shift override to the newly assigned shift.
📌Note: The system does not allow overrides on shifts dated before the current open period.
Always ensure the date effective is within an open calendar period before applying overrides.
If you need to make changes to historical shifts, contact your system administrator to review calendar settings.
🤓Tip: If you frequently see this error, check the system calendar open period before assigning or modifying shift overrides to avoid rework.

Managing shift types effectively is crucial for maintaining an organised workforce schedule. If you have unused or mistakenly created shift types in PeopleXD, you can delete them to keep your system clean and efficient. This article provides a step-by-step guide to deleting shift types, including prerequisites and troubleshooting tips.
Prerequisites for deleting shift types
Ensure the following conditions are met before you delete a shift type:
No Assignments: The shift type must not be assigned to any employees. You can only delete a shift where it has never been used. If a shift has ever been assigned to an employee or a work group the system stops you from deleting it.
Necessary Permissions: Ensure you have the required permissions to delete shift types. This may involve assigning specific menu profiles or roles to your user account. If you do not have the necessary permissions, contact your system administrator for assistance.
Process to Delete Shift Types
Follow these steps to delete a shift type in PeopleXD: go to the list of shift types, find the shift type you want to delete, click the three-dot menu next to it, select Delete, and confirm the deletion when prompted.
📌Note: The Delete option will only appear if the shift type has never been assigned to any employee.

Permission Issues: If you lack the required permissions, contact your system administrator to update your user profile with the necessary access rights.

You can manage shifts for employees who do not have a fixed schedule in PeopleXD's Workforce Management module. Use REST shifts as a default placeholder, manually override shifts for specific working days, or configure Flexi Work Patterns for more advanced scheduling needs.
REST shifts as a default for flexible employees
For employees who do not have a fixed shift pattern, assign a REST shift type as their default. This acts as a placeholder, ensuring every employee has a shift type assigned at all times. You can then manually adjust their schedule as needed.
Override shifts for specific working days
To roster an employee on specific working days, update the default REST shift for those days directly in the Roster screen or Weekly Work Schedule.
Open the Roster screen, or go to Timesheet Input and select Weekly Work Schedule.
Select the employee whose shift you want to update.
Change the default REST shift to the required working pattern for the days the employee needs to work.
Click Save.
📌Note: This approach lets you customise individual days while keeping REST as the standing default for all other days.

Follow these steps to update the user’s access:
From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.
Click WFM Configuration.
Click WFM System Users Configuration.
Find the relevant employee and click the three-dot menu next to their name.
Select View/Edit.
Click Access Privileges.
Enable the checkbox for Ignore Data Entry Restriction.
Click Save.
What happens next?
Once this privilege is enabled, the user will be able to delete historic absences in the Portal without receiving the restriction error.
📌 Note: Be cautious when deleting historic data, as this can affect payroll records or reporting.

Extending the system calendar each year is essential to avoid errors such as "Failed Contact Support" when you generate timesheets. PeopleXD uses both yearly and weekly calendars:
Yearly calendars: Ensure the full year is covered.
Weekly calendars: Used for day-to-day time tracking.
You should extend both calendar types to cover the next calendar year.
🤓 Tip: Always complete these steps before the start of the new year to avoid any service interruptions.
Extend the yearly calendar
Click CoreTime then click System Params.
Select Calendars then click System Calendars.
Enter the relevant company number then click Calendar Years.
On the next available row, enter the year, start date, and number of weeks.
Click Save.
Extend the weekly calendar
Click CoreTime then click System Params.
Select Calendars then click System Calendars.
Enter the relevant company number then click Generate Period.
For End Period, enter the week number for the final week of the new year.
​
For example, for the last week of 2025, enter 202552.
​
Click OK then click Save.

The legacy portal will be permanently retired on 30th June 2025.
What's changing?
From 30th June 2025, the following will occur:
The legacy portal will no longer be accessible.
The new portal will be the single location for all PeopleXD idea submissions.
Any ideas submitted in the last 12 months or with 10 or more votes will be automatically transferred to the new portal.
Older ideas that don’t meet the above criteria will not appear in the portal, but will still be retained internally by our product team for reference in roadmap planning.

Received an invite

You have previously submitted or voted on an idea in the old portal in the last 12 months.
We have automatically created a user account for you in the new portal.

Job Title Mapping lets administrators group multiple job title variants under one standard reference title in Workforce Management. These variations often occur due to different employment types, legacy setups, or workforce pool structures.
Once configured, all mapped titles are treated as equivalent in Required vs Rostered calculations, providing a more accurate view of staffing coverage across diverse workforce groups.
This feature is available to UK and Irish clients.

The Maintain Clockings parameter controls whether users can input or maintain clockings for a specific employee. If this is not enabled for an employee, no user—regardless of their own permissions—can modify that employee’s clockings.
To enable Maintain Clockings in Portal:
Go to WFM Admin > Person Maintenance.
Query the employee.
Click the ellipsis (...) and select View.
Select Person Settings.
Enable Maintain Clockings.
Click Save.
To enable Maintain Clockings in Back Office:
Go to CoreTime > Pers Data > Person Maintenance.
Search for the employee.
Select the General -1 tab.
Enable Maintain Clockings.
Save changes.
System Users: Assign clocking privileges to users
Users must have appropriate privileges enabled to input or modify clockings for employees. However, these privileges are ineffective if Maintain Clockings is disabled for the employee.
Available clocking privileges in Portal:
Modify Automated Clockings
Allows updating or deleting clockings received from devices or employee ESS clock-ins.
Maintain Historical Clockings
Allows entry, update, or deletion of clockings in past weeks. Historical entries are marked with a clock type prefix H.
Move Automated Clockings
Allows moving automated clockings to a different day without changing the clock time (useful for night shift adjustments).
Reset Clock Types

Clockings
Allows moving automated clockings to a different day without changing the clock time (useful for night shift adjustments).
Reset Clock Types Allows changing the clock type attached to a clock time. (Refer to related Knowledge Base articles for clock type explanations.)
To assign privileges in Portal:
Navigate to WFM Admin > Config > System Users Configuration.
Query the user.
Click the ellipsis (...) and select View/Edit.
Under Access Privileges, tick the relevant options.
Click Save.
To assign privileges in Back Office:
Go to System Params > System Users.
Query the user.
Select Access Privileges.
Tick or untick the relevant privileges as appropriate:
Modify Automated Clockings
Maintain Historical Clockings
Move Automated Clockings
Reset Clock Types
Save your changes.

The HR Changes screen in PeopleXD Talent shows leaver and manager changes from PeopleXD People Management. Changes sync overnight, so you can review and approve or reject them the next day.
When you approve a change, appraisals and objectives update automatically, keeping data consistent across both modules.

You need access to the HR Changes screen to use this feature.
Changes made in modules other than PeopleXD People Management won't appear in HR Changes.
Types of HR events
There are two types of HR events in the HR Changes screen:
Leaver: Employee with a past end date and active appraisals or objective cycles.
New HR Manager: Employee whose manager has changed, with active appraisals or objective cycles.
Review HR changes

From the dashboard menu, click Talent Dashboard.
Click the HR Changes tab.
The screen displays all pending HR events. You can search by employee name or personnel number, and filter by HR event type using the Filter by HR Event drop-down.
Approve or reject a change
To action changes individually or in bulk, watch the video or follow the steps below:
⚠️ Warning: Manually Assigned indicates whether an administrator has set a specific manager for the employee’s appraisals or objectives. If it shows Yes, review carefully before approving a manager change.

When you clone a review or appraisal and want to update the dates for a new year or period, PeopleXD won’t let you change the stage dates unless the main review dates are aligned first. To resolve this, you need to adjust the dates in a specific order.
The review is already cloned
If the review you cloned already has its date range moved into the new year, but the stage dates are stuck, follow the steps below.
In Edit Details, change the Review Start Date back to its original date.
Extend the Stage End Date forward into the new year.
Update the Stage Start Date so it also moves into the new year.
Move the Review Start Date forward again into the correct year.
The review hasn't been cloned
If you haven't cloned the review into the new year yet, or to avoid any issues in future years, we recommend you complete the process in the following order:
Extend the Review End Date into the new year.
Extend the Stage End Date into the new year.
Move the Stage Start Date into the new year.
Update the Review Start Date to the new year.

In PeopleXD Recruitment, you can use the Applicant Cleardown feature to automate the removal or anonymisation of applicant details. This process runs nightly and targets closed vacancies with a closed date older than six or twelve months.

Their application for that vacancy is deleted.
If they have other active applications, their applicant record and those other applications remain unchanged.

GDPR gives individuals the right to ask organisations to delete their personal data. For example, if a candidate has registered on an organisation's website e.g. Careers Portal, or has submitted an application but been unsuccessful, they may request the right to be forgotten. The Right To Be Forgotten feature in PeopleXD Recruitment allows users to action this request by deleting any candidate information retained in PeopleXD.
Process Candidate Right to be Forgotten Requests
To process a request, follow the below steps:
Navigate to the My Recruit Toolbox widget on the Recruitment Dashboard.
Click Open on Right To Be Forgotten.
Search for the applicant to be deleted using their name, applicant number, or email address. Alternatively, click OK to view all available candidates.
Click Delete on the relevant row.
Click Yes to confirm the deletion.
Note: Only candidates who are eligible to be deleted will be available on the Right To Be Forgotten screen. These are candidates who:
Do not have an employee record (i.e. an applicant record with a personnel number attached)
Do not have another application at the accepted stage
What Data is Deleted?
The following are all deleted when a Right to be Forgotten request has been processed:
All Candidate Data held within the PeopleXD ATS i.e. Portal View of PeopleXD Recruitment
Generated PDF View of the Candidate Application

en processed:
All Candidate Data held within the PeopleXD ATS i.e. Portal View of PeopleXD Recruitment
Generated PDF View of the Candidate Application Candidate Data held within eRecruitment website
The following candidate data is not deleted:
Candidate Data held within the new Careers Website (powered by Volcanic). However, customers have a self-serve facility to delete this data.
Merged PDF Packs of Candidates (where multiple candidates are merged into one PDF document). These merged documents can be deleted manually by users, or when closing the vacancy. These documents can also be deleted as part of the automated Applicant Cleardown process, subject to the vacancy and candidate being eligible for cleardown.

Error about sanitizing data is caused by ModSecurity. ModSecurity is an Application Firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application. By inspecting HTTP traffic, it can prevent attacks stemming from webion, and security misconfigurations.
Items that are likely to be blocked or cause an error application security flaws, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), file inclusror/conflict are the following:
SRC, Style, !=, <>, /bold. This is not an exhaustive list.
​
As for the hyperlink, we would advise using any online to shorten URL https://www.shorturl.at/ as a long URL might also cause this issue.
​
And for copying text from Word, it is better to do formatting in Portal as text in Work might contain whitespace characters and non-Unicode characters. Copying text directly from Word will copy those as well and you might not spot them. So it would be better to type text in Portal.
To Resolve
You would need to determine which paragraph is causing the issue (by copying and pasting it into the portal). Once you know it try typing the words and saving after two or three words.
Sometimes words like 'from' and 'create' can trigger the error - If so, you must update the wording of the text.
If there are URLs then try shortening the URL.

When you process your Year End Rollover in Core Expense, if the company car's 'Available From' date disappears in the car administration center, this is because the car Available From date has been manually updated.
​
When processing your Year End Rollover, the following car BIK values reset:
Available From (available_from).
Days car unavailable(days_car_unavailable).
Dates Free Fuel Provided(dates_free_fuel_prov).
Once you complete the Expense Year End, the system will always clear out the Available From date when no 'Available To' date is populated. The system will automatically set the Available From date to the start of the new tax year, eliminating the need for manual input at the beginning of each new tax year.
​
For the 'Available To' date, it will not be cleared out during the Expense Year End. If there is an existing Available To date, this indicates that the car has been returned on that date and the record is complete. A new Available To date should only be provided once the car is returned. A new record can be created when the car is available again by updating the Vehicle Cash Equivalent.

If an expense claim still shows as PROCESSED after the expense run it was included in has been finalized, this is because the claims are set as Payment by Company.
​
When claims are set to Payment by Company, it means that payment was made using a company credit card and the claimant will not be reimbursed for any expenses. Claims will show a value of 0.00 because the claimant is not receiving reimbursement, so the system does not recognize a payment being made. This is why the status of the expense claims remains PROCESSED.
​
If all the expense items on the report are marked as 'Paid by Company', the status will not move past PROCESSED. If the expense had a few items and only one of them was ' set to Paid by Company' rather than all items, then that one line would stay as '0' and the trip would get to PAID.

We're implementing the recent HMRC changes to electric vehicle mileage reimbursement rates that came into effect from 1st September 2025. HMRC announced these changes on 22nd August, introducing split rates based on charging location: 8p per mile for home charging and 12p per mile for public charging.
This enhancement allows you to accurately reimburse employees based on where they charge their electric vehicles, ensuring legislative compliance whilst maintaining P11D Section E classification.
​What is this feature for?
The new EV split mileage functionality enables your organisation to charge different mileage rates based on where electric vehicle miles were charged. This feature is based on changes to UK legislation and can be configured according to your requirements.
Key benefits:
Complies with the latest HMRC guidelines for EV reimbursement.
Maintains existing audit trail and reporting capabilities.
Offers flexibility to use traditional threshold rates for some vehicles if preferred.
​How it works
When employees submit mileage claims for electric vehicles:
They enter the total miles travelled and the miles charged away from home (public charging).
The system automatically calculates home-charged miles: total miles - away miles = home miles.
The blended reimbursement is calculated using: (away miles × public rate) + (home miles × home rate).

ed miles: total miles - away miles = home miles.
The blended reimbursement is calculated using: (away miles × public rate) + (home miles × home rate). The calculation breakdown is displayed transparently on the expense claim.
For example: An employee travels 11 miles total with 1 mile charged away from home:
1 mile × 12p (public rate) = £0.12
10 miles × 8p (home rate) = £0.80
Total reimbursement = £1.20
​Implementation timeline
Development prioritisation: This has been fast-tracked due to the short notice period from HMRC.
​UAT availability: 30th October 2025
​Live release: 6th November 2025
​Mobile app enhancements: Early 2026
​Note: The web app version will provide mobile access from the initial 6th November release, so employees can submit claims via mobile browser while we complete the native app updates.

Step 1: Enable the feature
The enhancement operates behind a feature flag (exp-ev-split-mileage) and must be activated for your organisation. To request activation, please raise a support ticket.

Navigate to Dashboard Configuration

There are several reasons why your pension benefits might be incorrect. To help you resolve this, we've put together a list of possible reasons below 👇
​
Joining and end dates
You should first check that the date of joining and pension end date are entered correctly, depending on whether the employee is active on the scheme. To check this, follow the steps below.
Click CorePension then click Maintenance.
Click Employee Details then click Pension Details.
If the dates are correct, move on to the next section.
Employee's appointments
Next, you should check the employee appointments. To do this, follow the steps below.
Click CorePension then click Maintenance.
Click Employee Details then click Employee Appointments.
Check all fields are correct.
Check that the appointment is set as pensionable or non-pensionable, as required.
If the appointment details are correct, move on to the next section.
Retirement date override
Lastly, you should check if the retirement date has been overridden, and check that the retirement date doesn't conflict with other dates set up.
For example, if an employee has a retirement date input for their 60th birthday, if they generate a statement for an age past 60, the benefits will result as 0.

This error usually pops up when a report includes columns with numbers that aren’t formatted correctly. To resolve this, you need to convert those columns using a calculation and remove the original versions from the report so Insight can read the data properly.
Which columns can be calculated?
Allowed: Columns with purely numeric values, such as Current Salary and Pension Scheme.
Not Allowed:
Date fields, such as Date of Birth and Pension Start Date.
Mixed-type fields, such as Employee Code, which may contain both numbers and text.
Apply the calculation
Open the report in Edit Mode.
Click Add then click Calculation.
Enter the calculation name, this appears as the column header.
Select the relevant column.
​
For example, if you select Pension Scheme, the field populates with PECI_PEN_PENSION_PERSON_MERGE.PENSION_SCHEME.
​
In the Calculation Text field, enter the following calculation:
​
to_number(nvl([instert column name from step 4], 0), '99,999,999.9999')
Save the calculation then remove the original column from the report.
Once you've done this, only the calculated version remains.
⚠️Important: You need to repeat these steps for every numeric column in the report.

If you’ve generated a pension benefit statement but noticed that some merge fields are displaying incorrect or unexpected values, this usually indicates an issue with how the letter template and data source are linked. This can happen when the merge fields in your Microsoft Word letter don’t correctly match the headers in the data source that provides the pension information.
Before generating the pension benefit statement, make sure you create the correct data source and set up your letter template with the appropriate mail merge fields. Ensuring that each field matches between the data source and the letter template is essential for displaying accurate information.

When editing your letter template in Microsoft Word, avoid renaming merge fields manually. If you need to change a field, delete the existing one and reinsert the correct field using the Insert Merge Field option. The same approach applies if you want to use the same merge field in multiple places; rather than copying and pasting with Ctrl + C, use Insert Merge Field each time you add it.

How this works
Once the support agent has added the collaborator to the conversation:
All participants will receive replies via email only.

All replies will be threaded within the same conversation.

You'll see a notification in your conversation whenever collaborators are added or removed from the conversation.

How do I set up non-employee users on Access Evo?
A non-employee user is any user that needs to login to Access Evo to access any of your Access Evo applications.
​
The assumption is that if they are not employees, they will not be set up on PeopleXD and therefore not synced to Access Evo Members.
​
The Access Evo Administrators can still create users directly on Access Evo for these scenarios. There is no change to how you currently manage this i.e. create the user, send an invitation email, assign their role to the products they require, deactivate the user when they no longer require access.
Can I update the Tags that are synced from PeopleXD?
The following Tags are synced from PeopleXD:
Department
Job Title
Location
You must not edit the value for any of these tags directly in Access Evo. If a Tag is not synced from PeopleXD, you can continue to manage this directly in Access Evo i.e. add new values, update values, assign to Members etc.

Access Identity definition
Access Identity is the authentication provider for Access Evo – Identity determines the security configuration, for example, password policies and timeout details to align with your organisation’s security policies, SSO configuration where required, and so on.
​
As all PeopleXD users are now customers of the Access Group, you too get to benefit from the security policies that we refer to as Access Identity.
​
This new login process is shared across the wide range of products offered by the Access Group and allows you to log into other products including Access Evo.
Benefits of Access Identity
Security Policies: Govern your whole domain and the users in the organisation through a security policy. Control users' session lengths, authentication for all users in the domain, such as password length, CAPTCHA and failed sign in attempts.
SSO: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect supported services through Federation.

When you ask Copilot a question about a company policy using PeopleXD Skills, it should retrieve information from your organisation's uploaded policy documents. If it returns a message such as ‘I couldn’t find specific information in the company documents’, or suggests you check with your HR department or manager, one or more configuration issues may be preventing access.
The sections below explain the most common causes and how to resolve them.
Top causes
The following are the most common reasons Copilot may not return policy documents, listed from most likely to least likely.
The prompt is not specific enough to trigger the correct skill
Copilot uses automatic skill selection to decide which skill to use based on your prompt. If your question is too general, Copilot may not select PeopleXD Skills and will not search your organisation’s uploaded documents.
For example, a prompt like "tell me about probation" may be too vague. A prompt such as "what is our company probation policy?" clearly indicates that Copilot should search company documents. To confirm this:
Check the skill label shown above Copilot’s response. If it doesn't say PeopleXD Skills, the HR Documents plugin wasn't used.
Rephrase your question to refer explicitly to company policies or documents.

. If it doesn't say PeopleXD Skills, the HR Documents plugin wasn't used.
Rephrase your question to refer explicitly to company policies or documents. Select PeopleXD Skills manually from the skill picker before asking your question. If Copilot then returns the expected document, the issue is related to automatic skill selection rather than the document itself.
No criteria group has been assigned to the document
Every policy document must have a criteria group assigned before it can be accessed by anyone through Copilot. Even if the document has been uploaded and saved, Copilot will not return it unless a criteria group is applied.
🤓Tip: If the document should be available to all employees, assign a criteria group with no restrictive rules.
To assign a criteria group, follow the steps below:
From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.
Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, then click Policy Documents.
Click the three-dot menu for the relevant policy, then click Criteria Groups.
Click Assign New Group, then select a criteria group from the dropdown list.
📌Note: If no suitable criteria group exists, you can create a new one.

The user does not meet the criteria group for the document Criteria groups control which employees can access specific policy documents. If the user asking the question does not meet the criteria rules, such as company, department, or location, Copilot will not return the document.
To resolve this, follow the steps below.
From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.
Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click Open, then click Policy Documents.
Click the three-dot menu for the relevant policy, then click Criteria Groups.
Note the criteria group assigned, then click Manage Criteria Groups.
Click the three-dot menu for the relevant group, then click Edit.
In the left-hand menu, review the criteria applied.
📌Note: Applied criteria are identified by a red circle showing the number of rules in use.
If the criteria exclude the user, update the existing group or create a new one.
⚠️Warning: Changes made to an existing criteria group apply wherever else it's used.
The document was not saved correctly after upload
When uploading a new policy document, you must click Save to trigger the indexing process. The Upload button in the actions menu is only used to re-index a document that has already been saved.
To save the document correctly, follow the steps below:

ad button in the actions menu is only used to re-index a document that has already been saved.
To save the document correctly, follow the steps below: From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.
Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click Open, then click Policy Documents.
Click the three-dot menu for the relevant policy, then click Edit.
Click Upload, then click Click or drop files here to upload.
Select your document in the explorer window, then click Open.
Click OK, then click Save.
🤓Tip: Large documents may take additional time to process after saving.
The document is in an unsupported format
The HR Documents plugin only supports .pdf and .doc file formats. Documents saved as other formats, for example, .docx, .xlsx, or .txt, are not indexed and cannot be found by Copilot.
Convert the document to a supported format, then upload it again using Policy Documents.
Required menu profile options are not active
The employee’s menu profile must include the required Copilot web service options. If any of these options are missing, Copilot cannot communicate with the HR Documents plugin.
Ask your system administrator to check that the employee menu profile includes all of the required Copilot web service options. Further guidance is available if required.

Temporary processing delay for large documents Large documents can take over a minute to process after saving. During this time, the document may temporarily appear unavailable to Copilot.
If you recently uploaded a large document, wait a few minutes, then try your Copilot query again.

Impersonation allows a user to grant someone else the ability to sign into Access Evo on their behalf, without sharing their password.
As an organisation administrator, you can control whether impersonation is permitted across your organisation and restrict which users (internal and external) are able to request it, i.e. sign into your account.
When enabled at organisation level, all users can grant impersonation access to others.
📌Note: Only domain owners can access and edit the Security Policy setting described in this article.
Access your Security Policy
To access your Security Policy, follow the steps below.
Go to MyAccount then select Security Policy.
Locate the Security Policy already set up and attached to your domain.
Beside the relevant security policy, click Edit.
Enable impersonation for the organisation
Within the Security Policy, there is a setting called Allow impersonation. Once enabled, users within your organisation will be able to grant impersonation access to others via their own account settings. To do this, follow the steps below.
From the Security Policy edit screen, locate the Allow impersonation setting.
To make this option available to all users, turn on Allow impersonation.
To save changes, click Save.

Changes to user management in PeopleXD Evo

When PeopleXD is synced with Access Evo, two distinct administrator organisation roles are available. Having two roles prevents accidental changes in Access Evo members that could create sync conflicts with PeopleXD, whilst ensuring Access Evo administrators can still manage platform settings, branding, and user access to products and features.
For example, the ability to change email address is not available for an XD Admin as changes to member email addresses should come from PeopleXD to ensure that PeopleXD and Access Evo are kept in sync​.
The two administrator organisation roles available are:
Access Evo Administrator: This role grants full access to manage all Access Evo platform settings, member records, and configurations.
XD Admin: This is a limited version of the Access Evo Administrator role that restricts access to member management actions.

The Living Roadmap gives you direct visibility of what Access is building for your products. Available within Access Evo, it shows you the roadmap for every product in your licensed Product Suite, so you can see what has just been released, what is coming next, and what is planned for the future. You no longer need to wait for a scheduled review with your account team to find out what is in the pipeline.
You can also register your interest in upcoming features, putting yourself forward as a stakeholder in the development process or as an early adopter when a feature becomes available for preview.
What you can see
The Living Roadmap groups features into four categories for each product in your Product Suite:
General Release — features available to all clients now.
Preview — features available for early adoption before general release.
Coming soon — features currently in development.
Futures — features planned to start development within the next six months.
📌Note: Only products in your licensed Product Suite are shown. Contact your Access account team if you expect to see a product that is not listed.

Customers using SAML, AD, or LDAP
If your organisation has been using SAML, AD, or LDAP authentication methods to log in to PeopleXD, you now need to configure SSO using OIDC in Access Identity.
Is OIDC secure?
Yes. Configuring SSO using OIDC in Access Identity is a secure authentication approach.
You're still connecting your PeopleXD login experience to your existing Identity Provider (IDP). Only the underlying protocol connecting to your IDP is changing.
The benefits remain the same:
Passwords never pass through Access Identity. Authentication happens with your IDP.
Encrypted connections protect all data in transit.
Your corporate security policies remain in effect.
You maintain centralised control over how your users access your systems.
What's different?
The key difference is that SSO configuration is directly linked to the domain of the email address for each user logging in. It's not a system-wide setting for all users.
Multiple domains: Configure a security policy per domain. This provides greater flexibility where you require different authentication policies for different domains.
You don't own a user's email domain: You can't force an SSO authentication flow if you don't own the user's email domain.

Changes to user management in PeopleXD Evo

With the upgrade to PeopleXD Evo, user management now integrates with Access Identity. This changes how user accounts are created, how users log in, and how security is managed across your system.
User management integrates with Access Evo
User accounts are automatically created in PeopleXD Security from your employee records. You can continue to use the user management area to define system access through menu profiles.
User accounts automatically sync to Access Evo as member accounts, where Access Identity manages user authentication, including:
Login methods such as email and password, two‑factor authentication (2FA), or single sign-on (SSO) via OpenID Connect (OIDC).
Security policies such as session, authentication, and password management.
Forgotten password management, which users manage on the login screen.
Email address is the unique identifier
In PeopleXD Evo, the login experience uses email address as the verified unique identifier for each account holder.
As part of the update, all users sync to Access Evo with their email address as their new login ID. Users receive an email invitation to complete their first time login through Access Identity.
📌 Note: If a user doesn't have an email address, you can create a username account for them. However, this provides a limited authentication experience.
Automated email invites for account setup

ess, you can create a username account for them. However, this provides a limited authentication experience.
Automated email invites for account setup Users are automatically created and invited by email to complete their PeopleXD account setup. How they complete their login depends on your Access Identity security configuration.
You can define rules in PeopleXD Security to control when the invites are sent and exclude groups if needed.
You can manually resend invitations to any user who hasn't completed their setup, for example, if they can't find the original invite.
⚠️Important: The PeopleXD Security Self Registration feature is no longer applicable in PeopleXD Evo.
Accounts deactivate automatically for leavers
Subject to your existing leaver profile rules, a user's account is automatically deactivated when an employee is made a leaver.
By default, the employee's account becomes inactive the day after their leaving date.
If you use PeopleXD leaver profiles to provide access for a defined period after their leaving date, the employee can continue to log in until the end of that period. During this time:
They have access to their limited view of PeopleXD.
They have no access to other Access Evo products.
📌 Note: During your upgrade, only active employees sync to Access Evo.
PeopleXD employees sync as members

have no access to other Access Evo products.
📌 Note: During your upgrade, only active employees sync to Access Evo.
PeopleXD employees sync as members PeopleXD employees sync to their Access Evo members record. A member is the name of the user account for Access Evo. This ensures that if you use other Access Evo connected products, your employees already exist as users and only need their permissions updated.
If you already use Access Evo for another Access Group application, the PeopleXD user syncs to the existing member account using the email address as the unique identifier.
IP restrictions apply at module level only
PeopleXD Security allowed system-level IP restrictions. In PeopleXD Evo, restrictions apply only at module level. This means a user can log in to Access Evo but, if module restrictions are in place, they can't access the corresponding PeopleXD dashboards.

Resolving an Insight error begins with isolating the issue. Errors such as "ORA-01476: divisor is equal to zero" usually occur due to an Insight calculation not liking particular data being passed through to the calculation.
​
Identify the Problem
Identify the problem by isolating the column causing the error. To isolate the error, we recommend the following steps.
Run the original report.
Save a copy of the report. This copy will be used to troubleshoot.
Using the copy of the original report, remove a calculation* column from the report, save, rerun the report making sure to refresh the data.
Repeat step 3. until the error no longer displays.
Once the error no longer displays, this confirms the last column removed as the cause of the issue.
​
Investigate the Data
Interrogate or review what data is returning for this column in relation to the error message.
e.g. A common cause of "ORA-01476: divisor is equal to zero" is that an employee incorrectly has a 0 entered for fte hours, contract hours or salary. The solution may be to update the employee's contract with the correct data OR add an NVL to the calculation.
*Unsure if it's a Calculation? Simply remove each column one-by-one, beginning with number columns.
​
Error Console
If still unsure, try using the Error Console for further assistance. To use the Error Console.
Run the original report until the error displays.

nsole
If still unsure, try using the Error Console for further assistance. To use the Error Console.
Run the original report until the error displays. Select Actions.
Select Error Console.
Select the relevant error message based on Run Time and Run By.
Scroll down to see a more detailed error message.
Use the error message to further help troubleshoot the issue.
​
​Note: the error message displays technical information which may require a Business or BI analyst to review. This information may also be shared with Customer Support.

When a contract has a commenced appointment sequence, the end date on that sequence will remain NULL.
Each night a job runs which checks for appointments with a future start date.
When an appointment has a start date for that night, the job updates the status on that to commenced and it updates the status on the previous commenced appointment to ended. It is only then that the end date is populated on that previous commenced appointment.
​
It is not possible to report on end dates for current commenced appointments where there is also a future appointment sequence.

PeopleXD Insight now supports a new report type called Web Services. A web service report works like a standard Insight report, but instead of viewing the results in the Portal, the report is set up as an API endpoint. When you call the endpoint, the report runs and returns your data as a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) response.
This means you can expose PeopleXD data to other internal systems or external third parties without building an interface. The endpoint sits within the existing B2B API framework at api.corehr.com and uses the same authentication methods.
📌Note: Creating and managing Web Service reports requires the appropriate Web Services permissions in PeopleXD Portal. Contact your HR Systems team if you do not have access.
What you can use it for
Web Service reports are suited to situations where another system or team needs regular access to a defined set of XD data. Common use cases include:
Sharing employee, payroll, or workforce data with a third-party application.
Providing a data feed to an internal system without building a full interface.
Replacing a manual export process with an automated API call at regular intervals.
Giving an external vendor controlled access to a specific subset of PeopleXD data.

ual export process with an automated API call at regular intervals.
Giving an external vendor controlled access to a specific subset of PeopleXD data. 🤓 Tip: Web Service reports are not intended for high-volume or data warehouse-style feeds. For high-volume requirements, consider using the B2B APIs alongside Insight Web Services and interface files.
How it works
Creating and using a web service report involves four steps.
Create the report
An HR Systems user creates the Web Service report in the dedicated Web Services area of Insight. Build the report in the same way as a standard Insight report — adding columns, filters, and calculations — with some restrictions on complexity. See the limitations section below for details.
Add parameters (optional)
WS Params can be added to the report to allow the calling system to filter the data it retrieves at the point of calling — for example, by employee reference, date range, or pay group. This avoids the need for separate endpoints for each data subset.
Generate the endpoint
Once the report is tested and ready, the HR Systems user generates an API endpoint from the Web Services screen. The endpoint is immediately available to call. The Endpoint Details screen gives the calling system's developers everything they need:
The endpoint path.
The expected JSON response format.
Any parameters required.
Call the endpoint

the calling system's developers everything they need:
The endpoint path.
The expected JSON response format.
Any parameters required.
Call the endpoint The calling system authenticates using credentials from the PeopleXD-Access Evo-Insight Web App in the PeopleXD Security area, obtains a bearer token, and calls the endpoint. The report runs and returns the data as a JSON array.
Key limitations
Web Service reports have restrictions in place to protect the performance and integrity of the live PeopleXD environment. The main ones to be aware of are:
Report complexity: Each report is limited to 50 columns, three Business Intelligence (BI) views, and 10 calculations. Some Structured Query Language (SQL) aggregation functions are not permitted.
Row limits: When called via the API, a maximum of 250,000 rows can be returned. The Portal view is limited to 250 rows and is for testing purposes only.
Active endpoints: You can have a maximum of 20 active endpoints at any time. This means you can have a maximum of 20 active web service reports.
Call frequency: Endpoints have rate limits — for example, a maximum of 10 executions in any five-minute window.
Restricted views: A number of views aren't available for Web Service reports, including all audit and security views.

tions in any five-minute window.
Restricted views: A number of views aren't available for Web Service reports, including all audit and security views. No scheduling: Web Service reports are called on demand by the consuming system. The calling system must manage scheduling, not PeopleXD.
⚠️ Important: An endpoint is automatically disabled after three consecutive failed executions. Monitor the Web Services History screen regularly to catch and resolve failures promptly.
Security
Web Service report security works differently depending on how the report is run.
When run via the PeopleXD Portal, the report uses the logged-in user's security. When called via the API, the report runs under a Back Office system user called CI User. Ensure the CI User’s security profile is up to date — if new workgroups or teams are added to the system, update CI User access to match.
📌 Note: If the data returned in the Portal differs from what the API returns, this is usually due to a difference between the logged-in user's security and the CI User's security profile.
What your IT team or vendor needs
Once the report is created and the endpoint generated, the calling team only needs:
The Web App credentials (Application ID and Secret) from the PeopleXD-Access Evo-Insight Web App.
The UAT and Production API endpoint paths.
The endpoint details, including the response format and any required parameters.

to_char(CTCI_WORK_PATTERN.DEFAULT_START_TIME, 'HH24:MI')

Reference data with numeric codes is in Hr Reference1(Data Validation) e.g. Locations.
Reference data with both numeric and alphanumeric codes is in Hr Reference2(Data Validation) so this is the best view to use for reporting on reference data.

​ Hr References (Data Validation) - This has all the reference data from Hr Reference2(Data Validation) and in addition has reference data for Work Groups, Pay Codes, Pay Scales/Grades and Pay Groups.

Your file is changing size because hidden, unneeded data is being removed.
When a file is downloaded from a database server, it will keep the formatting associated with the server.
This formatting is hidden as it is just a reference for the server and can only be read by a server and will not affect the data.
​
When you download a file from the database server, in this case via insights, it will keep the hidden formatting of the server on the file as well as it is essentially just copy pasting and sending you the file.
​
Once you then save the file elsewhere or rename it etc., it will save the correct size as it will get rid of this hidden formatting.

The reason all the trip IDs are not showing is because in back office if a Trip Id has multiple rows with the exact same data . The way insights were designed, multiple rows with the same data would be seen as duplicates and grouped to one.
​
For the Insights report, the Trip ID is not a unique enough identifier but by including the Trip Detail Id, it is possible to see the four rows with the same information separately because the Trip Detail Id is unique.
​
The grouping is determined by the report's columns. Queries with grouping do not display duplicate rows, and these rows are seen as duplicates by Insights because there is no differentiation between these rows, trip Id, expense code, dates, and amounts all are seen the same. When you add the trip detailed ID column, those rows are no longer duplicates because the trip detailed ID makes each row unique and produces the expected results.

This error message usually appears because an existing DECODE calculation based on Person Status treated all data as a number. As Person Status can be a number of characters (e.g. 1, 2, A, Z etc.) a mismatch of datatypes existed.
​
There are two options to resolve this issue:
Option 1
Add single quotes to the DECODE calculation so all data is treated as characters and not numbers.
E.g. Update this calculation:
DECODE(Person Type, 1, Balance, 2, Balance, 'A', Balance, 0) to
DECODE(Person Type, '1', Balance, '2', Balance, 'A', Balance, 0)
Option 2
Systematically remove the columns and see which column is causing the issue. If it is a large report, do it in batches to narrow it down.

Access to data in People Analytics depends on a user’s existing People Management data access rights. However, administrators can grant additional access using criteria groups.
Understanding data access
In People Analytics, users have specific data access based on their roles. For instance, consider the following scenarios:
Jane's Access: Jane initially has access to departments A and B in People Management. By employing criteria groups, she is granted additional access to department C. As a result, Jane can now access departments A, B, and C within People Analytics.
John's Access: Initially, John has no access to People Management data. However, by using criteria groups, he gains access to department C. John can now access department C within People Analytics.
To apply additional data access to enhance user access, follow these steps:
Create criteria groups
Create a data acccess group and assign it criteria groups.
Assign users to the data access group.
Criteria Groups
To create and manage criteria groups, follow the steps below in portal.
From the dashboard menu, select People Management.
Click Data Centre.
Beside the People Analytics Configuration, click Open.
Click the Data Access tab then click Actions.
Click Manage Criteria Groups then click Add.
In the Name field, enter a name then click OK.
Select a reference data option from the left-hand menu.

s.
Click Manage Criteria Groups then click Add.
In the Name field, enter a name then click OK.
Select a reference data option from the left-hand menu. Beside the relevant criteria, select the checkbox.
To move the user to the Assigned column, click the right arrowicon.
Repeat for all required criteria.
Data access group
To create a data access group, follow the steps below in portal.
From the dashboard menu, select People Management.
Click Data Centre.
Beside the People Analytics Configuration, click Open.
Click the Data Access tab then click Actions.
Click Create a Data Access Group.
In the Group Name field, enter a name.
From the Copy Data Access Group drop down menu, select whether to copy an existing group.
Click OK then click Assign Access.
Select the Criteria Groups then click OK.
Assign data access
To assign users to the data access group, follow the steps below in portal.
From the dashboard menu, select People Management.
Click Data Centre.
Beside the People Analytics Configuration, click Open.
Click the Data Access tab then click Users.
Beside the relevant user, select the checkbox.
Click Assign Access.
Select Data Access Group then click OK.

People Analytics

Purpose
Aimed at exploring and extracting deeper insights from the data across multiple sources within a dashboard. The data is built up over time and modelled and stored in a way that supports exploration and drilldown without need for specialist BI knowledge by the user
Primarily designed to generate standardised, scheduled reports. These operational reports provide information on specific items like absence. Data is modelled in standard BI Views by business area.
Focus
Supports interactive exploration, trend analysis, forecasting, and strategic decision-making (e.g., predicting turnover trends, identifying cost-saving opportunities).
Provides an actual snapshot by summarising past data (e.g., payroll details, attendance records), and current data (e.g. headcount, payroll details, attendance records)
Decision Making
Empowers users to identify trends, forecast future outcomes, and make proactive, data-driven strategic decisions.
Offers a clear and concise view of what has happened, which is essential for supporting day-to-day operational activities

To set a default currency in People Analytics and add exchange rates for converting from your default currency to another, you need to select a default currency in portal.
Doing so will enable you to choose a default currency for displaying your payroll information. This is particularly useful if your PeopleXD solution processes payroll in both the UK (£) and Ireland (€).
Note: By default, the solution’s currency is set to GBP
Default solution currency
To set a default currency, follow the steps below in portal.
From the dashboard menu, select People Management.
Click Data Centre.
Beside People Analytics Configuration, click Open.
Click the Currency tab.
From the Select Default Currency drop-down menu, select a default currency.
Click Save.
Add Currency rates
The solution employs a process called constant currency when converting values to a single currency. It uses only one exchange rate per currency for calculations, regardless of how many periods are involved. The exchange rates are based on the last day of the selected period in the Time picker.

for calculations, regardless of how many periods are involved. The exchange rates are based on the last day of the selected period in the Time picker. The constant currency method effectively analyses cost changes over time. If varying exchange rates were applied, differences in values could arise from the fluctuations, which would not be visible in the analysis as they occur before display. By using constant currency, trends in costs and trend line slopes are represented through a consistent exchange factor, offering a clearer and more reliable view of cost changes between periods.
To add currency rates, follow the steps below in portal.
From the dashboard menu, select People Management.
Click Data Centre.
Beside People Analytics Configuration, click Open.
Click the Currency tab then click Add Exchange Rate.
From the Currency drop-down menu, select a currency.
From the Currency Rate drop-down menu, select a currency rate.
From the Date Effective drop-down menu, select a date( i.e the date the currency rate should apply)
To apply all changes, click OK.
Note: For premier users, to ensure that People Analytics uses the exchange rate set in the PeopleXD configuration area, select Use admin default as your display currency in the Preferences tab of People Analytics.

Configure Pay Planner to apply proration to bonus calculations and ensure employees receive a bonus that reflects their actual contribution period. Two proration methods are available.
📌Note: You need Pay Planner admin access to configure proration.
Start-date proration: Which you configure in the incentive plan settings.
Custom factor proration: Lets you upload individual factors per employee during cycle set-up.
Start-date proration
Start-date proration adjusts an employee's bonus based on how long they have been employed during the bonus period. When you enable this, Pay Planner automatically calculates a proration factor for any employee who did not work the full bonus period, and reduces their bonus proportionally. To turn on start-date proration, follow the steps below.
From the dashboard menu, select Pay Planner.
Click Settings, then click Incentive Plans.
Click the pencil icon to edit the relevant bonus plan.
Select the Employment start date checkbox, then click Save.
📌 Note: This setting applies to all employees in any cycle that uses this bonus plan. Employees who worked the full bonus period are unaffected.
Custom factor proration

ng applies to all employees in any cycle that uses this bonus plan. Employees who worked the full bonus period are unaffected.
Custom factor proration Custom factor proration lets you upload a proration factor for each affected employee, and gives you flexibility to handle scenarios that start-date proration cannot accommodate — such as leave of absence or partial-year arrangements. The factor is a decimal between 0 and 1 and is displayed as a percentage in Pay Planner.
You can upload the file during the Bonus step of the New Cycle wizard, or in the set-up stage under Budget. To upload custom proration factors, follow the steps below.
⚠️Warning: Once the cycle moves to the allocation stage, you cannot upload, remove, or replace the file.
During cycle creation, go to the Bonus step.
Alternatively, in the Set-up stage, go to the Budget tab, click Bonus, then click Edit.
Under Upload individual proration, click Upload file.
🤓Tip: Use the Download template link to get the correct file format. The file must be saved as a CSV file and contain two columns: Employee ID and Factor.
Click Save.

wnload template link to get the correct file format. The file must be saved as a CSV file and contain two columns: Employee ID and Factor.
Click Save. ⚠️Important: Uploading a new file replaces the previous file and does not merge with it. Employees not included revert to a 100% factor. For example, if you upload employee A and employee B at 0.75, then upload a file with only employee A at 0.5, employee A updates to 50% and employee B loses their custom factor.
📌Note: You cannot update individual employee factors directly on the screen. To make any change, reload the complete file with all required factors included.
How the two methods interact
If both start-date proration and a custom factor are active for the same employee, both apply and multiply together to produce the final factor that the system uses in the bonus calculation. For example, if start-date proration produces a factor of 0.8 and the employee also has a custom factor of 0.75, the effective proration is 0.6 (0.8 × 0.75).
If an employee has no custom factor uploaded, the system assumes a factor of 100% and only start-date proration applies if you enable it. If a custom factor is uploaded but start-date proration is not enabled, only the custom factor applies.

Bonus plans define how to calculate bonuses in your compensation cycles. Set up your bonus plan formula once in Pay Planner settings. It applies when you create a cycle that includes bonus as a pay type. You need Pay Planner admin access to do this.
Available bonus formulas
Pay Planner supports five standard bonus formulas. Each formula applies selected performance factors as multipliers against the budgeted bonus. Employees receive their full bonus only when all performance targets are met.
📌 Note: If your formula includes team performance, you must set team performance targets when you create a compensation cycle. Apply a single percentage across all teams, or adjust each team individually.
Budgeted bonus × company performance × individual performance.
Budgeted bonus × (company performance × company weight + individual performance × individual weight).
Budgeted bonus × (company performance × company weight + team performance × team weight) × individual performance.
Budgeted bonus × company performance × (team performance × team weight + individual performance × individual weight).
Budgeted bonus × company performance × team performance × individual performance.

When creating your compensation cycle in the setup stage, you can select how manager budgets are calculated. There are two options to select from:
Budget Method
Description
Uniform Budgeting

the setup stage, you can select how manager budgets are calculated. There are two options to select from:
Budget Method
Description
Uniform Budgeting Is where each manager's budget is based only on employee base pay. For example, if a manager has two employees, one earning £50K and the other £100K, and the merit increase is 10%, the budget would be £15,000.
This method doesn't take performance or recommendations into account, meaning managers may end up over or under-budget based on actual recommendations.
Flexible Budgeting
Uses your pay philosophy recommendations to calculate each manager's budget. For example, a team of high performers may be allocated a larger share of the budget.
It's a more dynamic approach, but requires careful management to stay aligned with overall strategy.

Username accounts allow employees to access PeopleXD Evo when a verifiable email address isn't available. However, email accounts are strongly recommended as best practice for authentication, security policy compliance, and self-service account management.

Username account limitations
Username accounts have the following limitations:
Users cannot manage their own password resets: Access Evo administrators must set temporary passwords for account creation or when a user forgets their password. This creates additional administrative overhead for IT teams.
Cannot apply company security policies: Security policies manage user authentication and session management, and are defined based on email domains. If a user doesn't log in with an email address, only the Default Security Policy in Access Identity can be applied.
